## Scope note, 2026-07-25 (Viewer UX audit): unreduced, and now demonstrably two-sided

The viewer audit produced 76 findings across six reader journeys and **every one was driven on a
desktop pointer**. Nothing in it touched this ticket's scope, so its scope is not reduced by any of

hover-discovery on canvas marks, popover anchoring (the note card floats beside the canvas), and

## Scope call, 2026-07-25 (Viewer UX audit): NEITHER folds in NOR narrows to Studio

`Archie-c831` asked at resolution whether the read surface's a11y subset should fold into this
ticket. Answer: no, and this ticket does not narrow to Studio either. They are different activities.

- The per-finding structural work — roles, accessible names, focus behaviour, tab-stop counts — is

- This ticket is a SCREEN-READER WALK, which has never been done anywhere in the repo, plus the
  overlay contrast gate. Structural correctness is a precondition for that walk being worth
  running, not a substitute for it. A surface can have perfect roles and still be unusable to
  narrate.

title: SNAG: zoom-band (1.1) and arrival-pulse (1.3) CSS are INERT — Annotorious 3 renders marks to WebGL canvas
description:

The 2026-06-11 premise (svg.a9s-annotationlayer has NO per-annotation children) may be stale: Canvas.svelte:~102 now queries .a9s-annotation[data-id] SVG nodes for the Q-5 a11y marker labels, and that shipped through browser-verified a11y merges (9d33b29/32ed159). First step is a live-browser probe of the DOM under the annotation layer; do it AFTER the d48e chrome rewrite lands so the probe is against a stable tree.

## Probe result 2026-07-19 (ledgers/PROBE-annotorious-dom-2026-07-19.md)

Live studio probe (Rosettes exhibit, 5 notes, 4 checkpoints incl. 104x zoomOnSelect): svg.a9s-annotationlayer's only child is one empty transform <g>; .a9s-annotation matches 0 nodes ALWAYS; marks render via canvas.a9s-gl-canvas (WebGL/PixiJS). description:
## Notes

- Source: ledgers/UX-AUDIT-studio-wireframes.md (findings W1-W25) + wireframe board http://localhost:3002/?board=archie-studio-wireframes
- Domain: Archie Studio - Svelte 5 SPA, dual-target (browser + Tauri/Flatpak webview). Gates: per-app svelte-check / astro check; 1,250-test suite.
- Standing rules: CHECK PRIOR ART before any approach (fff / Prior Art dir); WWWWH-first copy; user-story template. Worktree agents: verify base vs main HEAD after spawn; uncommitted specs must be read from primary tree by absolute path.
- Skills: grilling tickets use /grill-with-docs — USER-INVOKED ONLY: ask the user to type it. Companions: /domain-modeling. Prototypes: /prototype. UI text: product-copy. Layout: interface-design.
- Cross-tracker: ISSUES.md Issue 13 (collab identity UI inert) = W23 - resolve together, do not fork.
- TERRITORY RE-ISSUE (2026-07-20): App.svelte no longer belongs to the nav-implementer — Archie-02ae is closed and nav/place-addressable merged. Three open tickets now write App.svelte (07a7 call site, 7e5b, 1244). Claim it per-ticket via the assignee field before editing; do not run two of those as concurrent worktree agents.
- MERGE POLICY (user directive 2026-07-19): merge each branch automatically once its code review is clean and gates are green — no per-branch ask; run full gates post-merge, close tickets with the implementer resolution, push.
- Tickets carry label map:studio-ux-overhaul. Claim (assignee + in_progress) before work. Frontier: sd ready. Conventions: docs/agents/issue-tracker.md. Glossary: CONTEXT.md.

## Decisions so far

- Navigation model: routable views and the overview skip (Archie-02ae) — place-addressable URLs (library/slug/slug+objectId), Overview mandatory (skip removed), push-on-every-place-change, nearest-ancestor fallback + notice, web bare URL=home vs desktop restore-last-place, session-only transient restore; ADR-0024.
- One save vocabulary (Archie-0b7b) — single end-to-end safety state (Failed > Action needed > Saving > Saved) over autosave+binding mirror; editor Save button dies, ⌘S = flush-now, indicator is the control when action needed; "Save" reserved for the one non-automatic act; CONTEXT.md → Persistence.
- Overview canvas mode (Archie-a9fc) — keep both modes, canvas primary (W9 corrected: drag already = reorder); chrome trimmed to first-use legend + Fit/% zoom; density slider removed; Canvas/List + library lens become persisted view preferences (ADR-0024 amendment).
- Where the narrative is edited (Archie-da38) — ADR-0016 §56 upheld (beats authored on canvas, overview spine read-only); friction fixed by beat deep links from spine rows (impl Archie-696d, blocked on nav+canvas merges).
- ADR-0016 amendment confirmed: mandatory Overview supersedes single-emergent auto-open; cross-referenced in ADR-0016 and ADR-0024.

title: Navigation model: routable views and the overview skip
description:
## Question
W1+W2: what is the navigation model? Should views be routable/addressable (URLs, browser back, deep links, refresh survival) in a dual-target web+Tauri app, and should single-object exhibits still skip the Overview screen (same click lands on different screens today)? Decide the desired behavior, not the mechanism.
closeReason: Resolved: place-addressable navigation. (1) URLs name places only (library / slug=overview / slug+objectId=editor); (2) Overview mandatory, single-object skip removed; (3) every place change pushes history incl. filmstrip switches; (4) unresolvable places degrade to nearest surviving ancestor + notice; (5) launch split: web bare URL=Library Home, desktop restores last place; (6) back restores transient screen state session-only; modals never in history. Full record: docs/adr/0004-place-addressable-navigation.md + CONTEXT.md (Navigation).

title: Routing mechanism for web + Tauri webview
description:
## Question
W1 mechanism: given the decided navigation behavior, how do we implement routable state in a Svelte 5 no-router SPA that also runs inside a Tauri webview? Survey options (hash routing, history API, a router lib, Tauri deep-link plugin), check Prior Art dir, produce a recommendation doc.
closeReason: Resolved: hash routing, hand-rolled over pure apps/studio/src/place.ts, no router dep. Static-host (GH Pages, no rewrites) + base-path /studio/ + Tauri webview: a History-API deep link 404s on refresh on every target; a # fragment reaches no server and runs one code path everywhere. Grammar deliberately reuses the archie-viewer hash cite-ladder (ADR-0021: #/{slug}, #/{slug}/o/{id}) with degrade-upward semantics — Studio and viewer share one address vocabulary. Full rationale docs/research/routing-mechanism.md. Merged to main f8fc422.

title: One save vocabulary
description:
## Question
W5+W19: reconcile the save concepts into one model: autosave vs the Save button vs Saved-check indicator (editor) vs Save-to-disk (library project bar) vs dirty dot vs writer-lock banner. What is THE save state model and its one prominent indicator?
closeReason: Resolved: one safety-state save model. (1) Single end-to-end indicator over both stages (session→store autosave, store→disk mirror); Saved only when both clean. (2) Editor Save button removed; ⌘S = universal flush-now; indicator IS the control when action needed; library bar save buttons collapse into same pattern. (3) One shared component, same header slot at every place; states Failed > Action needed > Saving > Saved; stale file binding + unbound-with-real-work = Action needed (gentle, never for untouched seed content). (4) 'Save' names exactly one act: completing the stage that can't auto-complete. Writer-lock banner explicitly NOT a safety state. Vocabulary: CONTEXT.md → Persistence. No ADR (reversible, unsurprising).

title: One affordance for details editing
description:
## Question
W3: DetailsEditor is reached via 3 different affordances (info-chip, pencil, accordion Detail panel). Pick one icon/entry convention for edit-details across library, overview, and editor.
closeReason: Resolved: one labeled 'Details' affordance everywhere — the word Details, ✎ pencil iconography where space is tight (tooltip 'Details'), opening the details surface at that thing's level. ⓘ retired (it promises read-only info; these entries open an editor). Per-item pencils on cards/plates/rows KEPT as entry points (batch-tidy workflow) but with identical presentation — one affordance in several places, not three affordances. Editor sidebar 'Detail' panel keeps its place in the This-object zone (Archie-5e96) and adopts the same label ('Details'). Copy standardization rides the product-copy pass.

title: New-exhibit create/import surface
description:
## Question
W6: the first-run flow crams 3 ingestion paths (title, media folder, IIIF via window.prompt) into one grid cell. Prototype a proper create/import surface with validation and preview. Use /prototype.
closeReason: Resolved via prototype (prototypes/create-surface, both variants Playwright-verified): VARIANT A — one scrimmed 'New exhibit' dialog, three paths as in-surface expanding cards (Start empty / From a media folder / From a IIIF link), single-scrim compliant; B's best trait grafted: page-level folder drop opens the dialog pre-populated. IIIF validation auto-starts on paste (debounced; plain-language errors lifted from ManifestImportError). Text-first paths — no new bare glyphs (W18 discipline); decorative marks allowed, meaning never rides on them. Subfolder grouping = progressive disclosure: only when the folder contains media subfolders, offer 'one exhibit from everything / one per subfolder (n)'. Surface built scope-parameterizable ('into exhibit X') but add-to-existing is Archie-beb6's decision. Replaces the grid-cell trio incl. window.prompt IIIF (W6).

title: Library home layout: project bar, search, templates
description:
## Question
W5+W7+W8: with the save model decided, redesign the library home top: where does storage/project state live (not dominating the primary bar), how does search stay unambiguous across the Exhibits/All-images toggle, and how are Example templates separated from user exhibits?
closeReason: Resolved: (1) SafetyState relocates from project bar to the LIBRARY HEADER (same-slot rule, consistent with editor+overview mounts); project bar demotes to one quiet line — 'Living in {location} · Open a library… · Close · Recents ▾' — no dots, no save buttons, no bar-scale prominence (W5 dissolved). (2) UNIFIED SEARCH: one box always searches both corpora; lens toggle governs browsing only; a typed query renders both groups labeled 'Exhibits (n) · Media (n)' (filterExhibits/filterImages both already computed); W7's silent scope switch eliminated. (3) EXAMPLES SHELF: user exhibits + New-exhibit lead; labeled Examples section below with the playground contract stated at shelf level ('edits here aren not saved unless you keep a copy'); expanded for zero-own-exhibit users, auto-collapses to header line at >=1 own exhibit; badge + editor playground banner unchanged.

title: Overview canvas mode: keep, kill, or rework
description:
## Question
W9+W12: the pan/zoom tableau fights the reading-order domain model (two orderings visible; drag ambiguity; heavy zoom chrome for ~10 items). Keep canvas mode, kill it in favor of list, or rework it? Also: does the density slider survive at toolbar level?
closeReason: Resolved: keep both overview modes, canvas primary, trim the chrome. (1) Light table stays — code already implements position=reading-order, drag=reorder, guarded under sort/filter (audit W9 core claim CORRECTED, see ledger). (2) Chrome trim: legend + hints first-use-only (auto-hide after first successful drag), zoom cluster collapses to Fit + live %. (3) Density slider removed everywhere; list gets one fixed row height. (4) Canvas/List and library Exhibits/All-images become persisted view preferences (last choice = default); transient-vs-preference split added to CONTEXT.md, amendment noted in ADR-0004. List remains the structured home for future keyboard reorder (a11y ticket).

title: Bulk selection and destructive actions
description:
## Question
W10: Select mode morphs the sort toolbar into bulk actions; Remove sits beside Sort/Size with a two-step confirm as only guard. Where do selection and destructive bulk actions live in the reworked overview?
closeReason: Resolved: dedicated selection bar. Toolbar never morphs (search/sort keep their home). Entering Select (toggle or starting a marquee) slides in a distinct bottom tray: 'N selected · Remove N · Clear · Done'; two-step confirm on Remove retained; bar exists only during selection (appears-when-real idiom); Esc = clear selection then exit mode per dismissal ladder; a11y keyboard range-select (Shift+Arrow, Ctrl+A, Space — docs/research/a11y-interactions.md) binds while active.

title: Where the narrative is edited
description:
## Question
W11: the overview shows the whole-exhibit spine read-only; editing requires entering some object editor. Where SHOULD the narrative be authored - overview, editor, or a dedicated surface?
closeReason: Resolved: uphold ADR-0005 + ADR-0016 §56 — narrative beats stay authored in the object editor (a beat is camera + prose; framing needs the canvas); overview spine stays read-only. W11's real residue (round-trip friction) is fixed by navigation, not a second authoring surface: each overview spine row becomes a beat deep link — editor at the beat's object with the Narrative panel open and scrolled to that section; browser back returns to overview (cheap under ADR-0024 places). No new authoring surface, no ADR needed (nothing amended).

title: Editor scope separation and one object-nav scheme
description:
## Question
W15+W16: exhibit-scope Narrative stacks in the same accordion as object-scope Notes/To-place/Detail with no boundary; and 3 parallel object-nav schemes coexist (rail filmstrip, narrative go-to, reading order). Decide the scope structure of the editor and the single navigation scheme.
closeReason: Resolved: (1) Scope boundary = two labeled zones in ONE sidebar — 'Exhibit — {title}' zone (Narrative panel; ADR-0016 always-present honored) above a visually distinct 'This object — {label}' zone (Notes, To place, Detail); sticky zone headers, object zone re-labels with filmstrip position. Tabs rejected (hides narrative, defeats ADR-0016 discoverability); side-split rejected (right edge reserved for docked note editor). (2) The filmstrip rail is the ONE object-nav scheme; navigation becomes its ONLY job; the rail is MINIMIZABLE (collapsible to a slim strip); keyboard face [ / ] prev-next is the same scheme. Rail sheds non-nav cargo: +Media/+Map relocate (home decided by Add-grammar Archie-beb6), toasts/mode-banners relocate (Editor-chrome Archie-b671). Spine go-tos are beat deep links (Archie-da38), reading order is ordering — neither is a competing scheme.

title: Editor chrome: dock the note editor, un-float the overlays
description:
## Question
W13+W14: floating chrome (readings rail, note popover, banners, toasts) occludes the artifact; the note form has two homes toggled by cryptic pin glyphs. Prototype an editor layout with one docked note editor and minimal canvas occlusion. Use /prototype + interface-design.
closeReason: Resolved via prototype reaction (prototypes/editor-chrome, two variants): (1) Readings = Variant A sidebar panel in This-object zone, VISUALLY SUBORDINATE to Notes — a quiet legend, not a peer workspace; (2) rail default EXPANDED, collapsed state persists as a view preference; (3) note dock RESIZABLE (ResizeDivider idiom), 320px default, min ~280, width persisted; (4) To place folds into Notes as a collapsible badged group 'To place (n)' — absent at n=0, full worklist when expanded; (5) status strip ABSENT when idle — renders only with an active mode/toast, collapses away otherwise. Docked editor replaces the floating popover; canvas carries zero chrome. Implementation: Archie-96im-successor (see impl ticket).

title: One grammar for adding things
description:
## Question
W17: add-verbs are scattered (+Media/+Map in rail, Box/Outline/Whole in Notes, Add-a-section in Narrative, Add-media plate in overview) with different placement and grammar. Define one add model across surfaces, given the decided create surface and editor structure.
closeReason: Resolved: the two-kind grammar. (1) BRINGING SOMETHING IN = the one chooser: every add-media affordance (overview Add-media plate, single '+ Add media' in the editor object-zone header) opens the 8482 dialog scoped 'into this exhibit'; Map becomes a fourth path card inside it (AddMapModal retired as a standalone surface — in-surface expansion, single-scrim); separate +Media/+Map buttons die (answers chrome-builder's parked TODO). (2) MAKING SOMETHING HERE = a gesture from its panel: Box/Outline/Whole stay in Notes, Add-a-section stays in Narrative, per ADR-0011 gesture-initiated creation. One-sentence grammar recorded in close + CONTEXT-worthy if it recurs.

title: Label the load-bearing glyphs
description:
## Question
W18: bare glyphs carry load-bearing meaning (drag grip, pin, outline/box/whole, cite, cmd-K). For the chrome that survives the editor redesign, write labels/tooltips/affordance text. Use product-copy skill.
closeReason: Merged (branch copy/glyph-labels, commit 5fa1af1; review: CLEAN). W18 closed for the surviving chrome — and the survey's headline finding is that the redesign already did most of the work: the popover pin, floating rail, +Media/+Map, MediaPicker, AddMapModal and edit-ⓘ all died in earlier tickets, and grips/rail-collapse/ResizeDivider/Details pencils were already labeled. What remained was accessible-name pollution: ~28 decorative Unicode glyphs sitting unhidden beside visible text (a screen reader announced 'black rectangle Box' for the Box button). Every such site across 8 components now wraps the glyph in aria-hidden; the map zoom buttons gained tooltips; the list-row ⠿ grip stays deliberately aria-only (tight footprint, correct aria-label already). Zero wording/behavior/aria-label changes otherwise. Genuine glyph-only gap found in AvEditor (Clear ✕ buttons lack aria-labels) — out of territory, filed as Archie-ba74. Gates post-merge: 0/0, 456/456, build green.

title: Modality rules: cite-flow nesting and surface stacking
description:
## Question
W4+W20: modal-over-modal in the cite flow (CmdK opens MediaPicker); drawers+modals+popovers+banners stack with undefined focus/escape/z-priority. Define the modality rules: what may stack, what must replace, how each dismisses.
closeReason: Resolved: (1) Single-scrim invariant — at most one scrimmed surface ever; opening from inside one REPLACES it; W20 fix: MediaPicker becomes the image tab inside CmdK (one surface, internal tabs, one Esc); drawers are scrimmed surfaces (drawer-vs-dialog is presentational only). (2) Strict dismissal contract: Esc ladder = topmost floater then the scrimmed surface; scrim-click = Esc; focus trapped + returned to opener; NO close-confirmations anywhere (autosave payoff; destructive-act confirms untouched); toasts/banners outside the ladder. Publish wizard mid-auth close = clean cancel, resumable — warn-or-not delegated to Archie-7d9b. Vocabulary: CONTEXT.md → Surfaces. Modals never in history per ADR-0024.

title: Publish flow continuity
description:
## Question
W21: publish is a 3-surface chain (button, dialog, wizard) that exits the app for device-code auth; failure recovery lands outside the app. Redesign for continuity - fewer hops, in-app recovery.
closeReason: Resolved: (1) PublishDialog + Publish wizard merge into ONE scrimmed surface — destination choice (web/local/zip) is step 1, internal steps with in-surface back (modality contract). (2) Esc mid-device-code-auth = clean cancel, SESSION-RESUMABLE, no warning: the machine keeps the pending device code (valid ~15min); reopening Publish resumes at the same waiting state/code; expired code → plain start-again sentence. Consistent with no-close-confirmations (fix the cost, not the exit). AUDIT CORRECTION recorded in ledger: in-surface retry/progress already existed; device-code auth + Pages-enable fallback are inherent to the serverless architecture, not flaws. Local/zip destinations unchanged.

title: Help and onboarding surface
description:
## Question
W22: help is fragmented (menu, iframe tutorial deck, shortcuts sheet) and non-contextual. What is the help model - contextual cues at moments of confusion vs the deck? What survives?
closeReason: Resolved: (b) the tutorial deck is the help investment. HelpMenu remains the deck's only entry point (no Library Home first-run card); shortcuts sheet stays; NO new contextual-cue system beyond the already-built first-use cues (legend/hint, narrative first-add). Deploy bug found + fixed during grilling: build-gh-pages.sh bypassed the package build's sync-learn step, so the gitignored public/learn never shipped from CI and the deployed tutorial iframe 404'd — fixed in b564ac2 (sync before raw vite build; verified CI-simulated). Deck content refresh ticketed behind the chrome implementation.

title: Collaboration: wire it or remove its signals
description:
## Question
W23 (= ISSUES.md Issue 13): IdentityPrompt and MergeReview are built but unmounted while collab signals (toast, writer-lock banner) still show, promising features that dead-end. Wire the collab flow in, or remove the signals? Resolve jointly with ISSUES.md Issue 13.

title: Keyboard equivalents and colour-independent coding
description:

closeReason: Resolved: research doc at docs/research/a11y-interactions.md. (6) Deletes hide-by-ancestry: one tombstone, subtree hidden at read, atomic un-delete; explicit bulk-delete as a user verb; write-cascade retired (existing cascaded tombstones remain valid history). title: Implement beat deep links from the overview spine
description:
## Question
Build the Archie-da38 resolution: overview spine rows deep-link to their beat (place URL for the beats object + a focus-narrative-section intent; NarrativeEditor scrolls to + highlights the section). Requires ADR-0024 place infrastructure; touches ExhibitOverview + App + NarrativeEditor, so it runs AFTER nav/place-addressable and canvas/light-table-trims merge.
closeReason: Merged d226a4f (branch beats/spine-deep-links, commit b822e6a, review fix 8c80f5f; review: no blockers). Each overview spine row is now a real beat deep link — activating it jumps into the object editor with the Narrative panel scrolled to and pulsing on that section, fixing W11's round-trip friction without a second authoring surface, per decision Archie-da38. The focused section is transient screen state riding App's existing focusSectionId channel — never in the URL, per ADR-0024's transient/place split — so browser back to the overview is ordinary place history with no bespoke code, and refresh degrades to editor-at-object without the pulse. Review fix: openObject nulls focusSectionId so a plain plate click can't inherit a stale beat jump (focus steal repro). Orphaned sections (beat object deleted; sections are never pruned) degrade to an inert row with visible 'Media item removed' text; the model guarantees every section has a framed object so no prose-only case exists. Pulse and smooth-scroll respect prefers-reduced-motion. Gates post-merge: svelte-check 0/11, 370/370, build green.

title: Mount SafetyState app-wide; single ⌘S owner
description:
## Question
Post-merge integration of the safety-state model (runs after nav/place-addressable AND save/safety-state merge). Requirements from save-reviewer: (a) DELETE App.svelte onBindingKey ⌘S branch when SafetyState mounts app-wide — otherwise clean-⌘S opens a picker under a Saved flash; (b) editor mount MUST pass sessDirty={sess.dirty} explicitly (optional prop, silent under-report if omitted); (c) mount SafetyState in the Overview header too (same slot at every place); (d) DECIDE + implement: library-level meta edits (title/summary/rights) should count as real work for the unbound Action-needed gate (recommended; today only exhibit-slug work counts); (e) accepted edge, document in code: writer-lock-refused persist shows "⚠ Retry save" with adjacent take-over guidance. Use the implementer integration note in the Archie-bb1a agent report + the actual props contract from the save-reviewer report.
closeReason: Merged with chrome/editor-redesign (same branch as Archie-c7ef; review: merge-ready). SafetyState is now the sole save UI at every place — the library, overview, and editor headers each mount the one component in the same slot, and App's competing onBindingKey ⌘S branch is deleted, so a clean ⌘S flashes Saved instead of opening a picker under it. The editor mount passes sessDirty explicitly (guarding the silent-under-report contract), the overview mount is threaded through a safety snippet on ExhibitOverview so App keeps the binding wiring, and the view branches are mutually exclusive so exactly one ⌘S handler is ever live. The decided library-meta gate is implemented app-locally: hasRealWorkIn treats an authored title/summary/credit as real work for the unbound Action-needed state via an optional third arg — backward-compatible, no new model fields (carry-sentinel territory untouched).

title: Split the canvas legend's two jobs: teaching vs reorderability state
description:
## Question
From canvas-reviewer: the light-table legend carried two jobs — gesture TEACHING (correctly first-use-only now) and REORDERABILITY STATE ("clear search & sort to reorder", relevant forever). The second job is now invisible to veteran users in canvas mode (list mode keeps its persistent hint + grip tooltip). Give the always-relevant state message a small persistent home in canvas mode (e.g. it appears only while a sort/filter is active), separate from the retired teaching legend. Also from review: a first reorder done in LIST mode dismisses the CANVAS legend unseen — consider per-mode teaching flags. Small, self-contained in ExhibitOverview.svelte; runs after canvas/light-table-trims merges.
closeReason: Merged (branch canvas/legend-split, commit 7841aa1 + review fixes e5b025b; review: no blockers). The light-table legend's two conflated jobs are now two independent affordances: a first-use-only teaching legend (unchanged lifecycle, now scoped per-mode) and a standing role=status reorderability indicator that appears exactly while search/sort disables drag — always-mounted live region (reliable AT announcement), width-clamped against legend overlap, with dynamically accurate copy from reorderBlockedMessage (search-only / sort-only / both variants; list mode's hint and grip title route through the same helper, fixing the same pre-existing copy flaw there). Per-mode teaching flags (v2.canvas/v2.list) mean a list-mode first reorder no longer robs a canvas user of the canvas legend; read-only fallback to the old v1 flag grandfathers existing users into seen-for-both. Both the indicator's visibility and the drag guard derive from one tested isReorderable predicate, closing the silent-divergence bug class. Gates post-merge: svelte-check 0/3, 393/393, build green.

title: Implement the modality contract (CmdK absorbs MediaPicker)
description:
## Question
Build Archie-389f: merge MediaPicker into CmdK as its image tab (one scrimmed surface, internal tabs, in-surface back where nested); enforce single-scrim (opening dialog closes drawer and vice versa); shared Esc ladder + scrim-click=Esc + focus trap/return in one small modality helper used by CmdK, PublishDialog, Publish, ReadingsModal, AddMapModal, PropsDrawer, TutorialModal, ShortcutsHelp; remove per-surface ad-hoc key handling. Runs after nav/place-addressable merges (App.svelte wiring).
closeReason: Merged 5e7899b (branch modality/single-scrim, commits f64823c+12d7bf6+fea62a1, review fixes f7952f4; review: no blockers). The modality contract is now one implementation: modality.svelte.ts owns the single-scrim invariant (replace-not-stack, with opener-aware focus-return — a surface opened from the page keeps its own opener; one opened from inside the replaced surface inherits), the Esc ladder (topmost floater then the one scrimmed surface), scrim-click=Esc, and focus trap/return. All nine scrimmed surfaces — dialogs and drawers alike — adopt it via use:scrimmed; each surface's hand-rolled Esc/trap/focus code is deleted, including LibraryHome's hand-wired dialog-drawer mutual exclusion (the helper's replace is the sole mechanism). MediaPicker.svelte was verified UNREACHABLE at base (requestVisualCite had zero call sites) and deleted — cite-by-image lives as CmdK's Browse tab with a byte-identical insertion payload, so the cite flow is one surface, internal tabs, one Esc (W20 dead). App's global keydown gained one scrim gate swallowing app shortcuts behind a modal (AvEditor's listener gated too; SafetyState's flush-through-scrim documented as deliberate; ? no longer replaces an open surface). Adopting real dialog semantics dropped the standing a11y baseline 11 -> 3 branch-local (5 on merged main). No history/URL coupling (ADR-0024). Gates post-merge: svelte-check 0/5, 380/380, build green.

title: Adopt the a11y interaction patterns
description:
## Question
Implement docs/research/a11y-interactions.md in priority order: (1) overview list Grid pattern + move-mode reorder + announcements; (2) notes-panel listbox with roving tabindex driving canvas selection; (3) readings numbered index across legend/marker; (4) filmstrip roving tabindex/aria-current. Runs after nav + canvas branches merge (ExhibitOverview + App territory).
closeReason: Merged (branch a11y/interaction-patterns, commits 164f319+43b508f+f2e947f+d5ec02b + review fixes 32ed159; review: no blockers, 3 should-fixes landed). The four drag-first/colour-only gaps from docs/research/a11y-interactions.md now have keyboard-and-AT paths: (1) the overview list is an honest APG Grid triple (div grid>row>gridcell — the ul deviation is deliberate, svelte-a11y forbids widget roles on ul; the selection-bar's deferred svelte-ignores retired with real semantics) with a keyboard move-mode on the grips — lift/arrow/Home/End/drop, Esc cancels via a working-copy that never touches canonical order, focusout abandons WITH announcement, lift-while-lifted cancels first, drag disabled mid-move; one mounted polite live region speaks the doc's grammar incl. distinct at-top/at-bottom strings. (2) The notes panel is a roving listbox whose selection drives the canvas through the existing bind:selected wire (WebGL marks can't focus); Enter/Space activation added in review. (3) Readings carry a derived colour-independent number (base ①, registry order; shift-on-delete is the doc's accepted semantic; announcements say plain 'reading 2') across panel/chips/picker/filing cue. (4) Filmstrip tiles rove with aria-current, activation explicit, works collapsed. +31 tests in four pure modules. Gates post-merge: 0/0, 487/487, build green.

title: Unify the Details affordance
description:
## Question
Build Archie-3e0a: one labeled Details affordance (word + ✎ where tight, tooltip Details) across LibraryHome header, exhibit cards, ExhibitOverview header + plates/rows, and the editor Detail panel label; retire ⓘ. Small, copy-sensitive (product-copy skill). Runs after nav + canvas + save branches merge (all three own affected files).
closeReason: Merged (branch details/one-affordance, commits 945d39b+990c98d+a9e20a0; review: one CSS-cascade blocker found and fixed pre-merge). W3 closed: three lookalike affordances for opening DetailsEditor collapsed into one. The edit-opening ⓘ is retired everywhere in studio (it promises read-only info; the viewer's genuine read-only Credit ⓘ correctly remains); library and exhibit headers show '✎ Details' with tooltips leading with Details; per-item pencils on cards/plates/rows keep their batch-tidy role but render from one shared .details-pencil class — the review verified in the BUILT CSS that scoped rules no longer out-specify it (row pencil re-asserts contested properties; excluded from the 3.3rem row min-height so all pencils are the same 1.85rem square). Accessible names use APG label-in-name — visible 'Details' uniform, aria-label 'Details — {item}' per item (an a11y trade-off the implementer flagged rather than shipping silently; both header chips gained aria-labels they never had). Editor panel header Detail -> Details. Zero mechanics changed — labels/glyphs/CSS/aria only. Gates post-merge: 0/0, 456/456, build green.

title: Back/forward navigation e2e (needs a Playwright gate)
description:
## Question
From nav-reviewer: the B1 popstate/hashchange re-entrancy bug class is untestable in the repo pure-module vitest posture — it needs a mounted App + real history traversal. When a Playwright gate exists (playwright already in deps index), add a back/forward e2e: rapid back/forward across library→overview→editor, manual hash edit, degrade landing keeps its notice, no double-transition. Also covers the two residual non-blocking hazards: rapid-traversal overlap, and committedUrl claiming an unreached URL if gotoPlace throws.
closeReason: Merged (branch test/e2e-gate, commits 367e18a+fed15ab; review: CLEAN — reviewer independently ran the suite twice, dev and CI modes). The repo now has a studio-scoped Playwright gate: e2e/playwright.config.ts (dedicated port 5198 strictPort, webServer boots studio's vite, chromium, workers:1 for the shared history, trace on-first-retry), a pnpm e2e script, @playwright/test pinned 1.60.0, and an isolated CI job matching checks.yml conventions with report upload on failure. The five-scenario navigation.spec.ts pins the ADR-0024 place contract over REAL browser history — the coverage hole vitest's SSR-compiled rune posture structurally can't reach: forward walk with URL grammar, back/forward unwind, rapid-traversal consistency (URL==screen wherever Chromium's history coalescing lands — the honest non-flaky form, with the deterministic corners pinned by scenarios 4/5), manual-hash degrade keeps its notice and the address bar never claims the unreached slug (committedUrl honesty), and one-back-moves-one-rung. Zero app changes — the session's aria work made role/label selectors sufficient. Both suspected re-entrancy hazards are now actively guarded and demonstrably do not fire. 5/5 green post-merge. Gates: 0/0, 499 unit tests, build green.

title: Implement the editor chrome redesign
description:
## Question
Build the Archie-b671 + Archie-5e96 resolutions in App.svelte and friends (territory now free — nav merged): two-zone sticky sidebar (Exhibit / This object, quiet subordinate Readings panel above Notes with To-place as collapsible badged group inside Notes); minimizable filmstrip rail (nav-only, expanded default, collapse persisted via view-prefs; [ / ] keys — coordinate with place push semantics); docked resizable NoteEditor (320px default, persisted width) replacing the floating popover + pinned inspector pair; slim status strip (absent when idle) absorbing rail toasts + mode banners; readings rail overlay removed. Prototype reference: prototypes/editor-chrome. Fold in Archie-c76d SafetyState mount reqs where they touch the same header. Gates + no new a11y warnings.
closeReason: Merged with chrome/editor-redesign (commits 3bfc71f+3ec28ba, review fixes 19276c4; review: merge-ready, no blockers). Variant A of the editor-chrome prototype ships with the reviewed amendments. The floating chrome that occluded the artefact is gone: the note editor is a stable, resizable right-edge dock (replacing both the marker popover and the pinned inspector; dock is resizable but deliberately not minimizable — ResizeDivider gained a collapsible prop), the readings controls are a subordinate sidebar legend (the floating ReadingsRail retired and deleted), and mode banners + import toasts collapse into one slim role=status strip that is absent when idle. The sidebar is two labeled sticky scope zones — Exhibit (Narrative) over This-object (Readings/Notes with To-place as a badged details group/Detail) — replacing the exclusive accordion; the filmstrip is nav-only and minimizable, with +Media/+Map parked in the object-zone header pending Archie-beb6, and rail-collapsed/dock-width persisted as view preferences. The canvas now carries zero chrome. Gates post-merge: svelte-check 0/11, 350/350 studio tests, studio+viewer builds green.

title: Merge Publish into one resumable surface
description:
## Question
Build Archie-7d9b: fold PublishDialog into Publish as step 1 (destination choice), internal back, one scrim; make the auth machine survive surface close within the session (pending device code kept until expiry, resume on reopen, expired -> restart state with plain copy); adopt the shared modality helper from Archie-5968. publish-machine.svelte.ts + Publish.svelte + PublishDialog.svelte retirement + App mount wiring.
closeReason: Merged (branch publish/one-surface, commit 8082b11 + review fixes b8f4c68; review: 2 blockers found and fixed, then MERGE verdict on re-check). Publish & Share is one scrimmed surface: step 1 picks a destination (all four PublishDialog cards verbatim — reviewer diffed card-by-card), choosing the web enters the GitHub wizard in place with ← Back to step 1; local/zip byte-equivalent. The publish machine lives for the app session: Esc/scrim-click mid-auth keeps the pending device code and reopening resumes the same waiting screen; an expired code lands on a plain 'That sign-in code expired — start again' state (review fix: the poll's expired rejection now parks there instead of silently re-minting codes forever); a publish that completes while closed shows its result on reopen; ← Back from parked auth keeps local/zip reachable. Review blocker fixed: the open-effect is untrack'd so in-wizard transitions no longer self-reset (headlessly untestable — SSR-compiled runes; browser drive queued post-merge). PublishDialog.svelte deleted; one open flag; use:scrimmed dismissal; fast-open with background projection (advisories pop in reactively; deploys always re-project so no race). Follow-up filed: Archie-363e publish Save-vocabulary copy. Gates post-merge: svelte-check 0/3, 421/421, build green.

title: Refresh the tutorial deck against the redesigned UI
description:
## Question
The docs/learn decks teach the pre-overhaul UI (floating note popover, Save button, ungated overview skip, old rail). Rewrite/re-shoot against the shipped redesign: places+back, safety state, two-zone sidebar, docked editor, minimizable rail, light-table trims, merged CmdK. Canonical source docs/learn; sync ships via build (fix b564ac2). Runs after chrome impl.
closeReason: Merged (branch docs/deck-refresh, 6 deck commits + fact-check fixes 12035dc; review: 11/13 sampled claims verified exact, 2 factual fixes landed pre-merge). The seven onboarding decks now teach the shipped redesign, every load-bearing claim verified against source before writing: the New-exhibit dialog and unified Add-media chooser, the Save-button-free Safety state (Action needed / Save to disk), Examples + Keep-a-copy replacing Playground/Project (glossary updated), CmdK cite with Search/Browse, the To-place badged group and Place on image, and the single Publish surface — with device-code auth correctly scoped to the DESKTOP app (a browser reader is steered to the portable file / token form, per isTauriEnv) and reading numbers correctly scoped to Studio (the Viewer legend shows swatch+name+count). Deck 1 was already accurate. CONTEXT.md vocabulary one-term-per-concept; nav chain and filenames unchanged; sync-learn ships it (dist/learn verified). Five real-pixel screenshots could not be honestly re-shot headlessly: two structurally-wrong ones removed (flagged in-file), three conceptually-correct ones kept with re-shoot flags — human re-capture list is in the ticket thread. Gates post-merge: 0/0, 499/499, build green.

title: Wire collab identity + live banner
description:
## Question
Build d71c part 3a: mount IdentityPrompt lazily (first zip-open containing others notes, or first share; skippable, never at boot); add Your-name field to Library Details (writes archie.displayName.v1); the shipped banner then renders real attribution (59a8 copy). Jointly resolves ISSUES.md Issue 13. After chrome impl (App territory).
closeReason: Merged a2a67eb (branch collab/wire-maximal, commits f0bfcea+a1ee49b). Identity is now captured lazily at the two moments it matters and never at boot: maybePromptIdentity() fires on (1) first publish click while unnamed and (2) opening a colleague's zip whose logs carry a foreign lastEditor stamp — the pending action always continues whether the user saves or skips (save/skip/Esc/scrim-click all resume the continuation; publish is never swallowed). IdentityPrompt is a scrimmed modality-contract dialog (use:scrimmed + trapFocus, copy 'Use this name' — no reserved 'Save'). A permanent Your-name field lives in Library Details, reading/writing archie.displayName.v1 — the same key author derives from; blank = anonymous, persists, never re-prompts. Append-only: no retroactive stamp rewrite. Reviewer-confirmed residual (ticketed, not shipped here): AnnotationSession captures editor at open, so a mid-session rename reaches new stamps only on the next exhibit open (S4, folded into the zip-merge wiring follow-up).

title: Mount MergeReview + attribution surfaces
description:
## Question
Build d71c parts 1-2: MergeReview summary in the status strip (non-blocking; review at leisure; keep-one-head only — semantics are Archie-697c contract, consume their spec/tests); editor chips on note rows + dock and filter-by-editor lens in Notes panel, both gated on >=2 distinct editors. After chrome impl (status strip must exist) AND after 697c spec lands.
closeReason: Merged a2a67eb (branch collab/wire-maximal, commits e2f2b87+a1ee49b). UI complete, pending a wired conflict source: MergeReview restructured from blocking summary panel to a scrimmed keep-one-head dialog opened from a status-strip entry ('N notes need a look · Review', absent when idle, live count); note-level C4 edit gate (conflictedNoteIds) makes the dock refuse conflicted notes and show the review card; attribution chips ('Meera · 2d ago') + filter-by-editor lens gated on hasMultipleEditors (exhibit-wide >=2 distinct lastEditor stamps; solo library renders zero attribution DOM), helpers unit-tested in collab-attribution.ts. Review fixes taken pre-merge: keep() now passes the CHOSEN head's interpretive fields (C14 — was inheriting reading/emphasis/geo from the lexicographically-first head) and the dialog closes only at zero remaining conflicts. All of it is inert today — importChanges has zero production callers (openZip replaces, never merges), so conflicts()==[] always; the wiring follow-up carries the reviewer's S3 (two gate-bypass write paths: canvas geometry drag, object-delete tombstone loop), S4 (identity capture lag), the dropped 'Added N notes' synced count, and the duplicate-logical-ids-to-Annotorious question.

title: Async round-trip package (share reframe + freshness badge)
description:
## Question
Build d71c part 3b-c: reframe zip destination as Share-a-working-copy with round-trip line (inside merged Publish surface, product-copy); per-exhibit +N-since-last-import badge on library cards, app-local watermark (never the model), shown only where a merge has happened. After publish impl.
closeReason: Merged (branch share/round-trip, commits 2ab487d+580a4a7). (a) The zip destination in the Publish surface is reframed as 'Share a working copy' — copy leads with the plain definition (a copy a colleague can open, annotate, and send back), demotes mechanics (backup/link/.archie.zip), promotes the round-trip line to lead the done screen; the existing 'Archie shows who added what' claim verified accurate against collabSummaryText + attribution chips. (b) New pure module import-freshness.ts (+14 tests): app-local localStorage watermark (archie.importFreshness.v1.<slug>, NEVER model fields — zero render-core changes) recorded at the one production import seam (openZip after replaceProjectFrom), rendered as a '+N since your last import' badge on library cards (calm accent, next to the Example badge). Semantics: baseline = others'-note count at last import (counting delegates to collabBreakdown — same rule as the collab summary panel); delta = increase since the previous baseline, floored at 0; FIRST import establishes the baseline silently (delta 0 — review-caught fix 580a4a7: the badge copy presupposes a prior import). Badge is a persistent fact about the last import, not a dismissable notification; solo libraries render nothing. Honestly dormant today: with openZip replacing the whole project, the badge fires only on a second zip-import of a previously-imported exhibit — a future incremental-merge caller (Archie-7e5b) wires through the same recordImportFreshness seam. Gates post-merge: svelte-check 0/0 (614 files), studio vitest 617/617, tsc clean, build clean, e2e 5/5.

title: Build the overview selection bar
description:
## Question
Build Archie-315e: bottom selection tray in ExhibitOverview (N selected / Remove N two-step / Clear / Done), de-morph the toolbar, Esc ladder integration, keyboard range-select per a11y research. After chrome impl (chrome-builder touches ExhibitOverview header for SafetyState).
closeReason: Merged (branch overview/selection-bar, commit ea43ef1 + review fixes 7a0ccb1; review: no blockers, 3 should-fixes landed). W10 closed: the search/sort toolbar never morphs — entering selection (toggle or marquee) slides in a dedicated bottom tray (role=toolbar, real flex child reserving space, not an overlay) owning 'N selected · Remove N · Clear · Done' with the same two-step Remove confirm. Review fix: the tray also shows for OFF-mode selections (⌘A / ctrl-click power path) — it is the two-step confirm's only UI, so without it ⌫⌫ bulk-deleted invisibly; Done there means clear, not toggle-select-mode-on. Esc = clear-then-exit was verified already present in App's page ladder under the scrim gate. Keyboard range-select per docs/research/a11y-interactions.md: roving tabindex over plates (preventScroll in the transform-panned canvas — review fix), Shift+Arrow feeds the same applyClick range fold as shift-click (one implementation), Space rides native button activation; the bare grid role was dropped (announces broken structure without row/gridcell) in favor of svelte-ignore until the a11y epic Archie-f260 lands the honest APG Grid triple. Gates post-merge: svelte-check 0/3, 421/421, build green.

title: Build the library home layout
description:
## Question
Build Archie-2308 in LibraryHome.svelte: SafetyState to header slot, project bar to one line, unified grouped search, Examples shelf with auto-collapse. Territory free (no other agent owns LibraryHome).
closeReason: Merged 2c47bdb (branch library/home-layout, commits 236ad90+82a199f; review: merge-ready, no blockers, 4 nits). The Library home now separates two questions that were previously tangled in one two-row project bar: will my work survive (SafetyState, promoted to the header, the same control every place mounts) and where does it live (one quiet line — 'Living in {location} · Open a library… · Close · Recents ▾' — demoted, no longer competing for attention; save-queue verbatim error line kept with role=alert). Search stopped silently scoping to whichever lens was active — a query now always shows both labeled groups, Exhibits (n) and Media (n), and the lens toggle hides while searching since it governs browsing only (viewPrefs untouched by search, so the persisted lens restores when the query clears). Examples are a structurally distinct collapsible shelf below the user's own work with the playground contract stated at shelf level, expanded only for zero-own-exhibit users (seed-once at mount via untrack; every first-own-exhibit path unmounts the home, so live collapse is unreachable). Pure helpers bindingLocationLabel/examplesDefaultOpen/partitionExhibits in library-home.ts with tests; one exhibitCard snippet renders all three grids. Gates post-merge: svelte-check 0/11, 350/350 tests, build green. Reviewer nits deferred: search-results mode drops the New-exhibit cell; disclosures lack aria-controls.

title: linearHead ignores mergeParents: resolved notes permanently uneditable; classifyLogical throws on logs with past resolutions
description:
## Bug (proven by characterization, ticket Archie-697c / B2)

linearHead (spine/log.ts:46-48) builds its referenced-set from `.parent` only, but resolveConflict (spine/merge.ts:251-252) records non-primary heads in `mergeParents`. After a resolution: headsOf correctly = 1 head, but linearHead still counts {merge node, non-primary head} = plural and THROWS. Consequences (both pinned by tests labelled "(OQ-1 pin, BUG)" in spine/merge-contract.test.ts, C4 ~l171 and C11 ~l332): (1) a resolved note is permanently uneditable/undeletable via appendEdit/appendDelete/session.edit; (2) classifyLogical throws on any log containing a past resolution — the async-zip merge path breaks post-resolve.

Fix shape (per B2 report): one-line — share parentsOf (mergeParents-aware, merge.ts:106-111) with linearHead. BEHAVIOR CHANGE: flip the two OQ-1-pin tests deliberately (they are labelled for exactly this), re-derive C4/C11 clauses in MERGE-CONTRACT.md, full spine suite must stay green otherwise.

Blocks: MergeReview flow (Archie-d71c) — resolve-then-edit is its immediate next action; spine gate (Archie-494c) — OQ-1 must be fixed before write primitives are reused for authored structure. See MERGE-CONTRACT.md "Open questions" for OQ-2..6 (recorded, lower stakes).
closeReason: FIXED, merged. parentsOf (primary parent + mergeParents) moved from merge.ts to log.ts as the ONE shared referenced-set builder; linearHead uses it — structural agreement with headsOf (they build the same set over the same filter; cannot disagree on any log). 2 pin-tests flipped as designed, 3 new regressions (resolve->edit, resolve->delete, post-resolution classify), MERGE-CONTRACT C4/C11 re-derived + OQ-1 marked resolved. 847/847 render-core, studio 342, archie-viewer 108, viewer 94, typecheck clean. Sibling sweep: linearHead was the only wrong parent-only build (lineage/withProvLink/deserialize verified deliberate). d71c inherits: resolved notes fully editable; resolve-live-then-delete sanctioned; resolved libraries round-trip the async-zip path.

title: Build the create/import dialog
description:
## Question
Build Archie-8482: the scrimmed three-path New-exhibit dialog (empty/folder/IIIF) with in-surface expansion, paste-triggered IIIF validation + preview, folder summary + subfolder-grouping disclosure, page-level folder drop opening it pre-populated; replaces LibraryHome grid-cell create trio. Scope-parameterizable for beb6. Prototype: prototypes/create-surface. After library/home-layout merges (same file) and after beb6 decides the shared-grammar scope.
closeReason: Merged 564f975 (branch create/import-dialog, commits c0abfe3+4bf2792, review fixes 08370b1; review: merge-ready). The Library's New-exhibit cell used to cram three unrelated affordances into one grid tile — a title input, a folder picker behind quiet text, and a raw window.prompt for IIIF links with no validation or preview. That's replaced by a single New-exhibit button opening one scrimmed dialog with three clearly-differentiated in-surface expanding paths, matching the reviewed Variant A prototype: folder imports show a live file-count summary and (for folders with subfolders) an explicit one-exhibit-or-one-per-subfolder choice; IIIF links validate as you paste (debounced, token-superseded, AbortController on close) with a manifest preview or plain-language ManifestImportError copy instead of a blind fetch. A folder dropped anywhere on the Library page opens the dialog pre-populated (per-entry-tolerant walker). Dismissal per CONTEXT.md: Esc/scrim-click close, Back returns in-surface, focus restored, no confirms; single-scrim holds both directions vs PropsDrawer. Scope-parameterizable (CreateSurfaceScope) for Archie-56cf. SHIP DEVIATION (reviewer-graded acceptable): folder/IIIF paths show the derived name read-only, not the prototype's editable title — callbacks carry no title and App.svelte was owned by a parallel agent; follow-up Archie-46bf threads it. Gates post-merge: svelte-check 0/11, 370/370, build green.

title: Unify add-media through the scoped chooser
description:
## Question
Build Archie-beb6: scope-parameterize the create dialog (into-exhibit mode: files/folder, IIIF, Map path absorbing AddMapModal), wire the overview Add-media plate + one editor object-zone-header Add-media button to it, delete the parked +Media/+Map pair and AddMapModal standalone mount. title: Self-hosted IIIF loop (GitHub-free publish to own server)
description:
## Notes

**Goal:** a GitHub-free authoring loop — a folder of collections on disk → generated IIIF manifests + web derivatives served from the user's own HTTP server → ingested into Archie **by reference** (zero image bytes copied; avoids the OPFS-quota failure that blocks local import of ~1000 images) → annotations/structure authored locally → published (written back) to the same server.

**STANDING CONSTRAINT (2026-07-19):** push the envelope on Archie **as a static app** — no custom server-side components anywhere in the loop. The server is off-the-shelf config only (static file serving, stock WebDAV, sync daemons). Any proposal requiring a bespoke service is out of bounds.

Charted 2026-07-19 from a design conversation that established the load-bearing constraints below (Notes-level facts, not closed tickets):

- IIIF-manifest ingest stores no bytes (apps/studio/src/ingest-flows.ts:469); local-file import copies masters into OPFS and hits quota.
- Write-back = publishing Archie's projection (itself IIIF P3) BESIDE the generated source manifests. Never mutate source manifests; never re-ingest to recover edits (iiif-import.ts reads only title/canvases/dims — annotations would be dropped).
- The working library is the sole home of authored truth; the server only ever holds a projection.
- Serving rules: honest 404s (no SPA rewrites over the tree), CORS; HTTPS whenever it leaves the LAN.
- Studio's existing web push is GitHub-only (apps/studio/src/deploy/deploy-flows.svelte.ts hardcodes api.github.com — 3 sites). publishLibrary writes through the Filesystem seam via MemoryFilesystem + collectFiles (publish-flows.svelte.ts), so a new destination replaces only the upload half.
- URL-as-identity hazards: renames orphan annotations; NFC/NFD filename normalization; EXIF-orientation dims mismatch silently skews all annotation geometry; TIFF doesn't decode in browsers → derivatives required.
- Server shape (grilling): home/LAN box, fully controlled, sync daemons fine; LAN-first, public later.

**Skills per session:** /grilling + /domain-modeling for decision tickets; /prototype for the generator. Repo rule: check Prior Art (fff over Archie/Prior Art) before committing to any approach.

**Key seams:** packages/render-core/src/fs/http.ts · publish/open.ts · publish/site.ts · apps/studio/src/ingest-flows.ts · iiif-import.ts · publish-flows.svelte.ts · deploy/deploy-flows.svelte.ts · store.ts · folder-backend.ts.

## Decisions so far

- [Decide publish tiling posture for referenced images (tileRemote)](Archie-df38) — pipeline generates derivatives + static tiles once, server-side; publishes are pure references (tileRemote unused).
- [Working-library platform & durability](Archie-aa69) — browser Studio + FSA folder-bound library; plain files on disk, normal backups.
- [Choose the write-back transport](Archie-7b1f) — static-envelope, both lanes: publish-to-folder onto the served docroot (mount/sync) now; in-app WebDAV destination as the button. No custom server processes.
- [Folder-drift strategy (manifest re-import dedup)](Archie-1e6d) — folder grows regularly → build dedup-by-source re-import (impl: Archie-12e3, gated on first ingest).

## Fog

- Collection-level bulk ingest (IIIF Collection → N exhibits in one paste) — sharpens after the first real ingest shows how much N pastes hurt.
- Publish performance & memory at 1000+ objects (MemoryFilesystem staging, publish duration, incremental publish) — measure after the first full publish; also whether per-file WebDAV PUT needs batching/throttling.
- Viewer performance against the derivative sizes the pipeline chooses — revisit after the derivative survey fixes sizes.
- URL-migration tooling (library-wide source rewrite) — ideally made moot by the URL-scheme decision; revisit only if the scheme fails.
- Multi-machine authoring over the server (zip/merge path, not re-ingest) — deferred until the single-machine loop works end to end.
- Bulk rights metadata (per-object requiredStatement sourced from folder metadata) — hangs on the rights-policy decision.
closeReason: Closed at user request 2026-07-19 — 'this is no longer what i want'. State at close: 7 decisions resolved (see Decisions so far), 9 tickets closed unresolved. Durable assets remain in-repo: ledgers/IIIF-LOOP-server-inventory.md, ledgers/IIIF-LOOP-derivative-survey.md (survey + adversarial review — folder census, level-0-only finding, EXIF rule; useful to ANY future serving effort regardless of shape).

title: Decide publish tiling posture for referenced images (tileRemote)
description:
## Question

At publish, tileRemote fetches every large CORS-reachable remote image and slices a tile pyramid into the published tree — self-contained + fast viewer, but slow publishes, a re-inflated tree, RAM pressure, and persists pixels (rights posture). Alternatives: pure references (small/fast publish, viewer depends on image server + full-size masters) or a selective/derivative-based middle. Which posture, and should it be a publish-time option?
closeReason: Pipeline tiles: the folder pipeline generates web derivatives + static deep-zoom tiles ONCE, server-side; Archie publishes pure references and tileRemote stays unused for this workflow (publishes stay small/fast; no pixel duplication onto the same host). Decided in grilling 2026-07-19.

title: Survey the folder + derivative pipeline requirements
description:
## Question

What is actually in the folder (formats — TIFF needs derivatives; sizes; EXIF orientation prevalence)? What must the derivative step produce: web-decodable masters (JPEG/WebP), post-EXIF-rotation dims, thumbnails/scaled sizes, and — per the tiling decision — STATIC deep-zoom tiles for the huge images (IIIF Image API level-0 vs DZI; how Archie's resolveTileSource ingests each). Survey tools (vips/sharp/static tile generators) and verify EXIF ground truth with a rotated fixture (browser/OSD rendered dims vs raw dims). Known (grilling 2026-07-19): mixed formats, some very large.
closeReason: Survey + adversarial review complete → ledgers/IIIF-LOOP-derivative-survey.md (review verdicts appended). Headline: IIIF Image API level-0 static tiles are the ONLY zero-code-change deep-zoom form (DZI-by-URL mis-resolves, resolve.ts:100); 1026 images (567 jpg ok, 375 TIFF + 84 NEF must convert), 1 image >30MP, 5 EXIF-rotated; EXIF rule = bake rotation into every derivative, dims from the derivative never raw EXIF; tooling = install libvips (dzsave --layout iiif3 --id <base>); ALL video → MP4 (MOV remux, AVI transcode); generator must ALSO write static full/240 + full/480 thumbnails per id (Archie derives those URLs). tiny-iiif = upstream clone, reuse its nginx topology only. Ports 80/443 occupied on this box — nginx config must pick a port.

title: Decide URL & filename scheme (identity policy)
description:
## Question

URLs are object identities forever: domain + path layout, slugification/normalization (NFC; spaces, ?, #), derivative naming relative to originals, and the rename-immutability rule. What scheme makes identities stable and migration unnecessary?

CONSTRAINT (grilling 2026-07-19): LAN-first but public later — choose the scheme AS IF public from day one; a LAN hostname baked into a thousand sources is the trap. Going public must be a DNS/serving change only.

title: Choose the write-back transport
description:
## Question

REVISED under the standing constraint (2026-07-19): Archie pushes its envelope as a STATIC app — no custom server-side components anywhere in the loop; the server is off-the-shelf config only. Static-compatible write-back transports: (a) publish-to-folder where the folder IS the served docroot (LAN mount or sync daemon — zero new code, exists today; marker-last ordering already covers torn writes); (b) a WebDAV destination in Studio (per-file PUT to nginx/Caddy stock config — in-app button, still no server code); (c) folder now, WebDAV later. Which?
closeReason: Static-envelope, both lanes: (1) NOW — publish-to-folder where the folder is the served docroot (LAN mount or sync daemon as the 'CI'); zero new code, marker-last covers torn writes. (2) BUILD — an in-app WebDAV publish destination (per-file PUT against stock nginx/Caddy config, archie.json last). No custom server-side processes anywhere — Archie stays a static app. Decided in grilling 2026-07-19 (revised from zip-receiver after the static-app constraint landed).

title: IIIF Collection ingest — collection paste unpacks into exhibits
description:
## Notes

Spec: ledgers/PLAN-collection-import.md (grilled 2026-07-19, 9 locked decisions). Glossary: CONTEXT.md §Ingest (Collection unpacking, Import batch). All work is studio-side; render-core untouched.
Standing gates: after any .svelte edit run `pnpm --filter @archie/studio run check`; tests per-app via `pnpm exec vitest` (root vitest breaks rune tests). Fetch stays in ingest-flows.ts (one fetch head: fetchManifestPlan); pure planners take injected fetchers.
Map children: `sd list --label map:collection-import`.

## Decisions so far

- [ADR 0025: collection-unpacks-into-exhibits — write it?](Archie-06a3) — yes; docs/adr/0025-collection-unpacks-into-exhibits.md (accepted): Collection unpacks into flat Exhibits, provenance-stamped; mega-manifest / single-picker / in-app grouping rejected.

- [Plural reducer: removeExhibitsIn(meta, slugs)](Archie-0dfe) — removeExhibitsIn + store removeExhibits: one patch/persist/signal, per-slug onDirty verified against its sole consumer; reviewer-approved, 529/529 green.

- [Pure IIIF layer: classifyIiifDocument + collection-import.ts](Archie-cc77) — capped injected-fetch traversal (depth 3, 25-doc attempt budget, 1000-manifest refusal w/ exact total, counted skips, label trails); reviewer-approved + 2 fixes landed; 530/530 green.

- [LibraryHome multi-select (overview-selection grammar)](Archie-d366) — shared grammar reused; select-all respects search, templates excluded; 3 review fixes (wall gate, scrim bail via modality store, prune-into-state); actions slot ready for bulk tickets; 534/534 green.

- [Ingest glue: fetchCollectionPreview + newExhibitsFromCollection](Archie-656a) — CollectionPreview contract (incl. silent aborted), pool-4 in-order batch w/ fatal-stop + orphan sweep, one fetch core; search extended to descriptions (provenance searchable); reviewer-approved after 2 fix rounds; 582/582 green.

- [Bulk rights edit (license + credit) over the selection](Archie-d2cc) — per-field gated dialog (never silently erases; blank-when-gated = clear, key-absence convention); plural patchExhibitsIn w/ clear only legal on optional keys (compile-pinned); reviewer-approved; 603/603 green.

- [Dialog: collection preview + checkbox picker](Archie-a9e2) — pure route/rows/hydration core + dormant-until-wired picker UI (all-checked, trail context, over-cap refusal, silent aborts); add-to-exhibit refusal verbatim; reviewer-approved with zero findings; 603/603 green.

- [Dialog: import progress, cancel, summary + Undo import](Archie-cbf6) — wired end-to-end + browser-verified (smoke caught the navigate-unmount bug; non-navigating mint added); 3-phase dialog, cancel-not-close while running, 4-tone summary, direct Undo (no confirm); reviewer-approved + 4 fixes; 642/642 green.

- [Bulk delete + rewire Undo-import to pre-select](Archie-ddaa) — two-step inline-morph delete in the selection bar; Critical catch: meta-only removal orphaned logs → ONE teardown seam (exhibit-teardown.ts) now backs singular delete, bulk delete AND undo-import; pre-select rewire dropped (direct Undo stands); 646/646 green.

- [Verify: published-collection round-trip e2e + 500-exhibit smoke](Archie-9422) — all 7 items pass in-browser incl. every deferred path + real remote collection; 500 exhibits: no chokepoints (import 14.1s, undo 296ms, bulk delete 489 in 340ms); full gate sweep green.

## Fog

- Durability of the import-batch memory: undo is in-session today ("remembered just long enough") — does it need to survive a reload, and if so where does the batch record live?
- ~~LibraryHome at 500+ exhibits~~ RESOLVED by Archie-9422: no chokepoints at 506 cards un-virtualized (grid 27–39ms, scroll ~305ms, search ~170ms) — no follow-up.
- Whether bulk-edit grows beyond rights (tags? covers?) once real bulk imports exist — wait for demand.
- Published-gallery provenance search (viewer side): apps/viewer gallery-view.ts has its own title-only filterExhibits and published cards don't carry summary — extending search there needs the published index to carry it. Studio-side search now matches descriptions (2026-07-19).
closeReason: MAP COMPLETE — 10/10 tickets closed (charted from ledgers/PLAN-collection-import.md; every implementation ticket ran an implementer+reviewer agent pair with fix rounds; final verify ticket proved the feature in-browser incl. a real remote collection and a 500-exhibit scale pass). Feature: pasting a IIIF Collection URL unpacks into exhibits (ADR-0025) with capped traversal, checkbox picker + label hydration, in-order pool-4 import with progress/cancel/fatal-stop, 4-tone summary + Undo (full per-slug teardown), bulk rights + bulk delete over multi-select, provenance searchable. Committed through 7ed7345 (pre-cbf6-fixes); later work uncommitted pending user ask. Remaining fog carried in description: import-batch durability across reload; bulk-edit growth; viewer-side published-gallery provenance search.

title: Wire a real conflict source: importChanges caller + gate bypasses + identity capture
description:
Cross-map follow-up from the collab surfaces merge (a2a67eb, tickets Archie-2bf1/Archie-90f1). The merge-review/edit-gate/attribution UI is complete but INERT: importChanges has zero production callers (flows.openZip REPLACES via replaceProjectFrom), so session.conflicts() is always empty. When the collab-readiness map (Archie-697c) wires zip-merge/live-sync, its acceptance criteria MUST absorb the reviewer's confirmed defects, all unreachable today: (S3a) canvas geometry drag bypasses the note-level C4 edit gate — onUpdate calls editNote by id, conflicted notes keep BOTH heads in workingAnnotations (duplicate logical ids fed to Annotorious), a drag on a conflicted note throws uncaught inside the Annotorious callback; (S3b) deleteObjectNotesAndMeta and bulkRemove tombstone every note via deleteNote — C4 throw mid-loop on a conflicted note aborts object removal HALF-DONE (partial tombstones, lib.removeObject never runs, unhandled rejection), and notes() visits a conflicted note once per head; (S4) AnnotationSession.editor is private readonly captured at open — a mid-session rename (Library Details field or the publish-trigger prompt) doesn't reach new stamps until the next exhibit open; needs a small core seam (editor thunk) or author-keyed session reopen; also the zip-open identity trigger names AFTER replaceProjectFrom already rebuilt sessions with the old author. Plus: route the dropped 'Added N notes from a colleague's copy' synced count into the import toast (the old MergeReview summary panel that carried it is gone), and memoize noteConflicts (unmemoized O(ids x log) scan per bump). This ticket is the acceptance-criteria rider for that wiring.

## Progress 2026-07-19 (two independent slivers shipped)
(1) conflicts() memoized in session.ts — keyed by log identity like headsCache, AND switched from per-id headsOf (O(ids×log)) to one headsByLogicalId pass (O(records)); tombstone-head semantics preserved (deliberately NOT derived from projectHeads, which drops deleted heads). (2) S4 editor seam: AnnotationSession constructor + load() accept ClientId | (() => ClientId); stamps resolve via stamp() at action time. exhibit-session.svelte.ts passes deps.author as the thunk (boot session, freshSeed, load) — a mid-session rename now reaches the very next stamp, and sessions rebuilt by replaceProjectFrom always see the live author. Pinned in session.test.ts (thunk rename + captured-ClientId contracts). REMAINING: everything gated on Archie-697c wiring importChanges (S3a canvas-drag gate bypass, S3b half-done bulk delete, synced-count toast).

Remaining work is unchanged and still real: S3a (canvas-drag bypass of the note-level C4 edit gate),

title: Dublin Core metadata
description:
## Notes

- Goal: descriptive metadata on Library / Exhibit / Object per Dublin Core (dc, 15 elements) + DCMI Terms (dcterms, the extended vocab). Charted 2026-07-19; spine decisions from the charting grill: scope = the three RightsFields levels (not sections/notes); purpose = viewer display AND interop/export AND preserve-on-import (all three); UI = pick-from-vocab (Tropy/Omeka style — default field set + add-field from the full vocab); values = repeatable plain strings (language tags deliberately deferred).
- Ground truth (metadata-surface survey 2026-07-19): model carries only title/summary + RightsFields (packages/render-core/src/model/model.ts:66 — rights, requiredStatement); a dormant seam already exists: IIIFRightsProps.metadata?: IIIFLabelValue[] (iiif/presentation.ts:36) is typed but never populated; apps/studio/src/iiif-import.ts drops third-party manifest metadata/rights/summary entirely; publish emits IIIF P3 + WADM, no DC anywhere; editing UI home = DetailsEditor.svelte + RightsEditor.svelte; any new model field is gated by carry sentinels (rule render-core-data-integrity — AObject 3 sites in publish/working.ts + iiif/manifest.ts, Exhibit 2, Library hand-maps in working.ts).
- Prior art anchors: Tropy (../tropy) ships res/vocab/dc.n3 + dcterms.n3 and a template system (res/ttp, src/ontology) — the pick-from-vocab model to study; IIIF metadata is deliberately non-semantic label/value display pairs. Repo rule: CHECK PRIOR ART and cite it on every ticket (fff over the Image/ dir).
- Skills: grilling tickets → /grill-with-docs (USER-INVOKED ONLY — ask the user to type it), companion /domain-modeling; prototypes → /prototype; UI text → product-copy; research → /research.
- Tickets carry label map:dc-metadata. Claim (assignee + status in_progress) before any work. Frontier: sd ready filtered to the label. Conventions: docs/agents/issue-tracker.md.

- MERGE POLICY (user directive 2026-07-19): merge each branch automatically once its review is green (full gates for app-code branches) — no per-branch ask. Prototypes merged: 80a209d (panel, Archie-0ba5) + 9f12bea (editor, Archie-e100), reactions pending; pipeline branch wf/metadata-pipeline merges after review + gates.

## Decisions so far

- Survey dc/dcterms vocab and prior-art metadata models (Archie-a58e, closed) — asset docs/research/dublin-core-vocab.md; dc 15 + dcterms 55; native title/summary/rights/requiredStatement ARE the IIIF typed slots, so the DC layer excludes them; IIIF metadata[] is display-only; prior-art defaults are narrow (Tropy generic 10 / Omeka 2), URI decoupled from display label.
- Model home and record shape for descriptive metadata (Archie-8176, closed) — RightsFields gains metadata?: MetadataEntry[] ({ property: "dcterms:x", value }), ordered, repeats as entries; dcterms:-only canonical prefix; DISJOINT from native title/summary/rights (exclusion list → default-field-set ticket); entry widened in the batched grill to { property?; label?; value } (≥1 of property/label); named hazard: studio rightsOf reconstructors must not drop the new field.

- IIIF import: preserve third-party manifest metadata (Archie-bbad, closed) — map-when-confident (original label kept as override), verbatim otherwise; manifest rights/attribution/summary fill natives; excluded-property labels stay verbatim.
- Publish projection (Archie-246c, closed) — metadata[] populated at all three IIIF levels (lang-map none, same-label repeats merged); raw entries round-trip via archieMetadata extension property; exhibits.json carries entries for the viewer panel; JSON-LD/meta-tags deferred to fog.

- Studio metadata editor → MERGED (Archie-458e, closed) — MetadataEditor.svelte + metadata-rows.ts, tabbed into DetailsEditor at all three levels; keyed partial patches only.
- Viewer metadata panel → MERGED (Archie-b50f, closed) — metadata-display.ts + MetadataList/MetadataRun, Notes|Details tablist + exhibit-header run.

title: Survey dc/dcterms vocab and prior-art metadata models (Tropy, Omeka S, IIIF)
description:
## Question

What exactly is in dc (15 elements) and dcterms (extended), and how do the prior-art tools model pick-from-vocab metadata? Produce docs/research/dublin-core-vocab.md covering: (a) a property inventory — URI, label, comment per property — read from Tropy's local authoritative copies ../tropy/res/vocab/dc.n3 and dcterms.n3; (b) how Tropy templates (res/ttp, src/ontology) select a working subset and type values; (c) how Omeka S resource templates and IIIF's metadata guidance (non-semantic label/value pairs) handle the same problem; (d) a recommended default field set per level (Library / Exhibit / Object) to seed the later grilling. Inventory + recommendation only — no model decisions here.
closeReason: Asset: docs/research/dublin-core-vocab.md. dc=15, dcterms=55 (15 same-name refinements; long tail = date/relation/rights refinements), parsed from Tropy's bundled n3. Key findings: (1) Archie's native title/summary/rights/requiredStatement ARE IIIF P3's typed descriptive slots — a DC layer must exclude those properties, covering creator/date/subject/type/identifier/relations only; (2) IIIF P3 metadata (spec §3.1) is display-only label/value — property URIs don't survive to the viewer, so DC is an authoring/interchange convenience; (3) prior-art defaults are narrow (Omeka: title+description; Tropy generic template: 10 fields), both decouple property URI from display label and allow overrides; cardinality differs (Tropy single, Omeka repeatable). Recommended defaults: Library creator/publisher/date/identifier; Exhibit creator/date/subject; Object creator/date/subject/type/identifier/source (= Tropy generic).

title: Model home and record shape for descriptive metadata
description:
## Question

Where does descriptive metadata live in the model, and what is a record? closeReason: RESOLVED (grill with user, 2026-07-19): (1) MODEL HOME — extend RightsFields with metadata?: MetadataEntry[] (model.ts:66; its doc comment already reserved 'metadata' as additive). description:

title: IIIF import: preserve third-party manifest metadata
description:
## Question

What happens to a third-party IIIF manifest's metadata block on import? Its labels are arbitrary display strings, not DC properties. Decide: store verbatim (label/value alongside DC-keyed fields), map recognized labels onto dcterms, or both (map where confident, verbatim otherwise)? Also: per-canvas metadata → per-object metadata; and manifest rights / requiredStatement / summary → the existing model fields (apps/studio/src/iiif-import.ts currently drops all of it — see map Notes).
closeReason: RESOLVED (batched grill with user, 2026-07-19): MAP-WHEN-CONFIDENT, VERBATIM OTHERWISE. A pair whose label case-insensitively matches a dcterms preferred label (plus a small alias table, e.g. author→creator) imports as { property, label: original-when-different, value } — display byte-identical to the source manifest, semantics gained, mapping reversible. Unrecognized labels import verbatim { label, value } (enabled by the entry widening). RIDERS: manifest-level rights/requiredStatement/summary fill the NATIVE typed fields (all currently dropped by apps/studio/src/iiif-import.ts); per-canvas metadata → that object's entries, manifest-level metadata → the exhibit's; a label mapping to an EXCLUDED property (Title, License, …) is stored verbatim — never double-authored into metadata, never clobbering a native.

title: Publish projection: IIIF metadata[] and real dcterms emission
description:
## Question

How does metadata leave the system at publish? Decide: (1) populating the dormant IIIFRightsProps.metadata[] (label/value render of DC fields) in toManifest / collection — and the round-trip read back in objectsFromManifest; (2) whether to ALSO emit machine-readable dcterms URIs somewhere (JSON-LD in the published tree? meta/link tags on viewer pages?) or leave IIIF label/value as the only projection; (3) what Gallery/exhibits.json carries so the viewer panel can render without fetching manifests.
closeReason: RESOLVED (batched grill with user, 2026-07-19): (1) DISPLAY — populate metadata[] at Collection (library entries) / Manifest (exhibit) / Canvas (object): label = override ?? vocab default; values as IIIF language maps keyed 'none'; same-label repeats merged into one pair with multiple values. Pure IIIF viewers (Mirador) show it for free. (2) ROUND-TRIP — also emit raw entries as one extension property archieMetadata: [{property?, label?, value}] at the same three levels (P3 clients must ignore unknown properties); objectsFromManifest reads it back losslessly — the manifest stays the round-trip source, matching how summary/rights already return. (3) VIEWER — exhibits.json carries the entries pass-through (as rights/requiredStatement already mirror) so the viewer panel renders without fetching manifests. (4) Machine-readable beyond that (schema.org JSON-LD context, meta tags) stays in fog with the SEO item. TOUCH POINTS: iiif/manifest.ts toManifest/objectsFromManifest (+ carry sentinel :166), iiif/rights.ts or a sibling metadata projector, publish/site.ts exhibits.json writer, collection.ts.
