title: apps/viewer has no .svelte type gate — wire check:svelte into CI and burn down the baseline
description:
## Question

PROVEN by experiment during the Archie-b50f review: planting `const probe: number = notADefinedThing;` in a viewer .svelte component left `astro check` at 0/0/0 and `tsc --noEmit` at exit 0, while svelte-check went from 1 error to 2. So apps/viewer .svelte scripts have NO type gate in CI — astro check does not cover them. Pre-existing hole, not introduced by the metadata work (the metadata components add zero findings). Add a check:svelte script to apps/viewer, wire it into checks.yml, and burn down the standing baseline of 1 error / 10 warnings across 5 files (EmptyHall, NarrativeReader, NoteLightbox, Reader, SearchOverlay). Note: the svelte-no-typecheck-net rule was corrected on the panel branch (commit e44fa56) to document this gap accurately.
closeReason:
ALREADY DONE — shipped 2026-07-20, verified 2026-07-24. Every clause of the ticket is satisfied:

1. "Add a check:svelte script to apps/viewer" — apps/viewer/package.json:18 defines
   `"check:svelte": "svelte-check --workspace . --fail-on-warnings"` (with a `precheck:svelte`
   running `astro sync` at :17), and the package carries its own svelte-check devDependency.
2. "Wire it into checks.yml" — .github/workflows/checks.yml:131 runs
   `pnpm --filter @archie/viewer run check:svelte` as its own step beside studio's, with a comment
   recording the measurement that motivated it.
3. "Burn down the standing baseline of 1 error / 10 warnings across 5 files" — burned to zero. The
   error was a real unguarded indexed access in Reader.svelte's `stepObject`; the 10 warnings were 9
   intentional initial-capture sites converted to declared intent via
   `// svelte-ignore state_referenced_locally` with a WHY on each, plus one dead CSS selector.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE GATE, not by reading the config:
  pnpm --filter @archie/viewer run check:svelte
  → COMPLETED 1464 FILES 0 ERRORS 0 WARNINGS 0 FILES_WITH_PROBLEMS

Because the script passes --fail-on-warnings, the viewer now has the same regression discipline as
studio: a NEW warning fails CI, not just a new error.

The premise remains correct and is worth preserving: `astro check` diagnoses .astro files ONLY, so it
proves nothing about an island — the planted-probe experiment in the ticket is the evidence, and it is
recorded in .claude/rules/svelte-no-typecheck-net.md, which was updated the same day to document the
closure. That rule is the durable artifact; this ticket is superseded by it.

Closed as done-elsewhere during the Viewer UX audit charting session, on the user's instruction.

title: Decide: should the read boundary reject excluded dcterms properties, or display them?
description:

Decide: reject at the read boundary, keep-and-display (documenting the exception), or migrate such entries into the native field.

title: Section rev-log capability is half-enacted and ships dark behind an always-off flag
description:
## Question

Decide the disposition of the section rev-log build (evidence: PROBE-structure-revlog.md verdict PURSUE; feature-flags.ts; App.svelte:292-314,580-598,1864; ingest-flows.ts:263,1180,1197; publish-flows.svelte.ts:93-225; structure-session/reconcile/import.ts; render-core spine/structure*.ts). Pick ONE: (A) ENACT — give it an author UI + a real activation path, default the flag on, and close the export-vs-import asymmetry so a published history round-trips regardless of flag state; or (B) PARK+CUT — remove the flag and the studio machinery (keep or excise the render-core spine per its own owners), leaving a single ledger note. Done-when: the ledger records the choice with rationale, and if ENACT, structure-export-roundtrip.test.ts is exercised through a NON-flag path. Safety: READ-ONLY exploration first; do not touch .seeds/, HANDOFF.md, ISSUES.md; if cutting, run vitest + pnpm typecheck and check render-core consumers before deleting shared spine code.

## Evidence (verified)

~1,400 lines of production source (studio: structure-session.svelte.ts 215 + structure-reconcile.ts 190 + structure-import.ts 125; render-core spine/structure* 873) implement a full write->project->serialize->persist->publish->import capability for sections-as-merge-DAG-records. It is gated by structureRevlogEnabled() (feature-flags.ts:18), whose only activation path is a doc comment telling you to type localStorage.setItem into the console (feature-flags.ts:12) — no seed, prod, or UI path ever flips it (grep -a for setItem finds only the comment; every true is in a test file). createStructureSession is always constructed (App.svelte:293) but ensureLoaded/apply run only behind the flag (App.svelte:302,314). The PROBE-structure-revlog.md verdict was PURSUE, so this is a stalled build, not an abandoned experiment.

Rungs: L1<->L2<->L4 — the purpose doc never names 'section history', a built capability is invocable only from tests, and rev-logged history is persisted but never restored in any shipped config. Mismatch: a PURSUE-verdict feature was two-thirds built then parked with no activation path.
Why: This is the single largest surplus in the subsystem and it also hides a latent data-loss seam: the publish/export leg is UNCONDITIONAL ('deliberately NOT gated by the flag', publish-flows.svelte.ts:93-95,225) while the import leg is flag-gated (ingest-flows.ts:1180) — so a library published with the flag on carries structure/history pages that a default-flag reopen silently ignores. General lesson: a probe that concludes PURSUE must land with an activation decision, or the code becomes indistinguishable from dark surplus and quietly grows integrity gaps. NOT the same as the DECIDED 'version-history dark data' (DARKDATA.md:20 = annotation history + PROV consumer).

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed.

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-studio-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Grill verdict 2026-07-20: ENACT (probe's PURSUE honored; asymmetry closed as part of the work, not before it). Work ticket: Archie-b0b1 — Phase 3 of docs/plans/TEND-FLEET-2026-07-20.md, blocked behind Archie-fada (App.svelte/ingest-flows territory).

title: Delete the redundant DeploySession.persisted field (persistFailed already delivers the promised re-auth hint)
description:
## Question

Delete DeploySession.persisted: remove the field (deploy/types.ts:78-83), its three write sites (deploy-flows.svelte.ts:297,325; publish-machine.svelte.ts:351), and the doc promise. The documented 'sign in again next time' UX already ships via the parallel persistFailed flag (publish-machine.svelte.ts:352, exposed :495, rendered Publish.svelte:722-724, tested Publish.test.ts:243) — persisted is an unread duplicate of !persistFailed. Done when: vitest (deploy-flows.test.ts, Publish.test.ts) and pnpm typecheck pass with the field gone. Safety: do not touch persistFailed or its UI copy; do not touch .seeds/, HANDOFF.md, ISSUES.md.

## Evidence (verified)

DeploySession.persisted (deploy/types.ts:78-83) is documented as 'True iff the token was successfully saved to the OS keyring', with the promised consequence 'false = the scholar will have to sign in again next time' (types.ts:81-82). It is computed and written at three sites — deploy-flows.svelte.ts:297 (false), :325 (true), publish-machine.svelte.ts:351 (persisted: ok) — and read as a condition by zero code. grep -a '.persisted' across apps/studio/src outside those writes, the type decl, and deploy-flows.test.ts returns nothing; the machine exposes it via get session() (publish-machine.svelte.ts:480) but nothing branches on it. The documented UX does not exist.

Rungs: L1<->L4 — a purpose-level promise in a doc comment (behavior) with no L4 implementation. Mismatch: computed-and-persisted field whose entire reason for existing is a consequence that was never wired.
Why: Either the re-auth-awareness UX is worth building (small, high-signal to a scholar publishing to GitHub Pages) or the field is misleading dead weight that a future reader will trust. Both resolutions are cheap; leaving it half-there is the worst state. General lesson: a persisted field documented with a downstream consequence is a promise — grep its readers before believing it.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: corrected. Corrections: The title's central claim is wrong: the documented "you'll have to sign in again next time" UX IS implemented — not via `persisted`, but via the parallel flag `persistFailed` set from the same `ok` at publish-machine.svelte.ts:352, exposed at :495, and rendered in Publish.svelte:722-724 ("We couldn't keep you signed in on this computer — you'll sign in again next time."), with test coverage in Publish.test.ts:243. Also, the re-auth consequence is mechanically real independent of any flag (restoreSession finds no keyring token → null). What survives: the `persisted` field itself has zero readers (verified — only the 3 cited writes, the type decl, and test literals), making it a redundant duplicate of `!persistFailed`; the only sensible resolution is option B (delete the field), not option A.

title: The localStorage try/catch persistence idiom is re-hand-rolled in 6 non-App modules with no shared primitive
description:
## Question

Safety: do NOT modify App.svelte's copies (Issue 18 territory); keep the rune-$state shape for view-prefs (its reactivity is load-bearing) by wrapping the primitive, not replacing the singleton; one phase, <=5 files at a time.

## Evidence (verified)

There is no shared storage helper (grep -a for exported safe*/persisted*/readFlag finds nothing). The try { localStorage.getItem/setItem } catch {} idiom is independently re-derived in >=6 modules in three structurally different shapes: (A) inline module functions — canvas-first-use.ts:18-21, feature-flags.ts:18, import-freshness.ts:58-69; (B) rune $state singleton getters/setters — view-prefs.svelte.ts:48-127; (C) JSON-blob-by-id — deploy/deploy-flows.svelte.ts:122-132, binding.ts:145-196. The comments themselves admit the copy ('Same localStorage try/catch idiom as App.svelte's FIRST_ADD_KEY' — canvas-first-use.ts:6, import-freshness.ts:51, feature-flags.ts:1).

Rungs: L3<->L4 — a single storage-safety concern implemented >=3 ways (structure) with duplicated private-mode/quota defensive boilerplate that can drift (implementation). Mismatch: same primitive, six re-inventions, no seam.
Why: Each copy is a place a private-mode or quota-denied read can be mishandled differently; a persistedFlag/persistedString/persistedNumber (or safeGet/safeSet) primitive collapses them to one tested spot. This is distinct from Issue 18, which owns only App.svelte's inline copies — do not touch App.svelte here. General lesson: when comments say 'same idiom as X', the idiom wants to be a function.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed. Corrections: Minor: feature-flags.ts:1's comment says "the same metadata idiom as IDENTITY_KEY / archie.lastPlace.v1 (App.svelte)" rather than literally naming the try/catch idiom — substance identical. description:

## Evidence (verified)

store.ts (516 lines) mixes four unrelated concerns: id-scheme migration (:64,:95), OPFS dir openers (:108-141), library+pending-note metadata (:180-261), and asset-blob I/O. title: Two disagreeing enumerations of the exhibit route-set: sitemap 404s + third-party exhibits get no page
description:
## Question

Make [slug].astro getStaticPaths enumerate the SAME source the sitemap uses (og-image's exhibitSlugs / exhibits.json), keeping the existing META entries as per-slug overrides and defaulting title/description/og from each exhibits.json card for slugs without authored META. Done when: every slug in exhibits.json (incl. geo-map, screenshots) builds a static page, /sitemap.xml lists only buildable routes, and a synthetic extra slug in exhibits.json produces a page with card-derived meta. Guards: read-only outside apps/viewer/src/pages; run cd apps/viewer && pnpm exec vitest run and pnpm build; do not touch .seeds/, exhibits.json content, or curation of which slugs are published.

## Evidence (verified)

sitemap.xml.ts:3-6 derives routes from exhibitSlugs (all 7 slugs in public/published/exhibits.json), but [slug].astro:86 builds only the 5 hardcoded META slugs (getStaticPaths = Object.keys(META), not exhibitSlugs despite the :3-4 header claiming otherwise). So /sitemap.xml advertises geo-map/ and screenshots/ with no static page built, 404 for every crawler/unfurl; geo-map is a real gallery exhibit with no shareable OG page. A cloner's dropped-zip exhibits (supported, gen-published.mts:6-17) all silently lack pages, contradicting index.astro:4 'arbitrary published Library, no per-exhibit code'. Build stays green.

Rungs: L2 (sitemap advertises unbuilt routes) <-> L3 (route-set enumerated twice, hardcoded META vs computed exhibitSlugs) <-> L4 (getStaticPaths hardcodes samples). Mismatch: only one of the two enumerations is derived, so they drift silently.
Why: Fix = drive getStaticPaths from exhibitSlugs with META as an override and exhibits.json card title/description as the default; collapses two enumerations into one and makes the 'arbitrary library' purpose real. Lesson: derive every enumeration of a set from one source or it drifts behind a green build.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed. Corrections: Minor nuance only: [slug].astro:35-36 contains a second comment ("Only slugs carrying authored page-meta render a reader page") explicitly documenting the 5-slug META set as mirroring the old hand-written pages — so the restriction is partially deliberate, even though the header comment (lines 3-4) falsely claims exhibitSlugs is the source. The central mismatch (sitemap advertises 7 routes, only 5 built; geo-map and screenshots 404) is unaffected.

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-viewer-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Merged (wf/viewer-routes 706e33f): getStaticPaths enumerates exhibits.json cards (META as overrides, card-derived defaults, conditional about/license). title: WADM projection omits standard authorship/creation fields (creator, created) despite capturing the data
description:
## Question

In packages/render-core, emit WADM-standard `created` and `creator` on the note heads-page projection so a pure IIIF/WADM consumer sees authorship, not just `modified`. Today recordToAnnotation (spine/serialize.ts:108-119) emits only `modified` (from modifiedAt); the author identity flows only to `archie:lastEditor` on history pages. Done when: (a) the heads-page projection carries WADM `created` (derive from the logicalId's DAG-root record's modifiedAt) and `creator` (a WADM Agent {type:'Person',name} sourced from the head record's lastEditor); (b) `creator?: unknown` at wadm/types.ts:148 is tightened to the WADM Agent/string shape; (c) deserialize round-trips or harmlessly ignores them; (d) the serialize + working-projection carry sentinels (render-core-data-integrity rule #3, serialize.ts:45-62 and session.ts:59-76) get their entries. Decision (default, confirm if unsure): SUPPRESS creator for synthetic session ids (working-reader/viewer-live/anonymous — publish/working.ts:318, apps/viewer published.ts:147, App.svelte:113 fallback) so only real authored names get a creator. Safety: this changes manifest bytes for every note — update the byte-golden tests deliberately (publish/voynich-readings.test.ts, iiif/manifest.test.ts:157 pins the heads embed shape) and confirm both a pure-WADM consumer and Archie's own reload still parse; do NOT alter/remove `archie:lastEditor` (merge UI + collab banner read it). Verify: `cd packages/render-core && pnpm exec vitest run` then `pnpm -r typecheck`.

## Evidence (verified)

The interop purpose (wadm/types.ts:3-8, serialize.ts:3-5) is that a pure WADM/IIIF consumer gets standard fields for free. But recordToAnnotation (spine/serialize.ts:108-119) emits only `modified` — never WADM `created` nor `creator` — so the heads-page AnnotationPage a Mirador loads has a timestamp and zero authorship. The data exists: apps/studio App.svelte:113 derives a human author name that session.ts stamp() writes, but only into `archie:lastEditor` on history pages (per DARKDATA). `creator?: unknown` (wadm/types.ts:148) has zero write sites across render-core.

Rungs: L1<->L4 — the stated pure-consumer-fidelity purpose vs a projection boundary that under-emits the two fields whose data is already computed and persisted.
Why: Near-free win with real interop payoff: the author name and creation time already exist; this is 'emit two fields the model already holds', not new data flow. Distinct from DARKDATA (which censused lastEditor as app-facing and modifiedAt) — this is the untracked PUBLIC WADM emission. General lesson: a three-tier interop contract is only as honest as its least-emitted standard field.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed. Corrections: Minor citation drift only: (1) "serialize.ts:3-5" — there is no wadm/serialize.ts; the log+projection purpose comment is packages/render-core/src/spine/serialize.ts:1-10. (2) session.ts is packages/render-core/src/session/session.ts (stamp() at :110, lastEditor stamped at appends :148/:167/:183/:241; carry-sentinel drop entry at :74). Substance of every claim holds.

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-render-core-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Merged (wf/rc-wadm, head 76ecf11): heads-page projection emits WADM created (DAG-root modifiedAt, omitted-never-invented; plural-root tiebreak pinned) + creator ({type:Person,name} from lastEditor, suppressed for anonymous/working-reader/viewer-live/blank). W3CAgent per spec 3.2.2; deserialize ignores both (re-derivable, documented at parse sentinel); carry sentinels updated; ONE golden changed (voynich-readings snap, justified per-note); history/working surfaces byte-stable. Review: APPROVE, gates re-run independently; nit round landed truthful comment + tiebreak pins. Merged-tree: render-core vitest + tsc + viewer vitest all green.

title: Authorship as a first-class concept — creator plus Reading/exhibit ownership
description:
## Question

Pursue, park, or kill: Authorship as a first-class concept — creator plus Reading/exhibit ownership?

## Surplus (verified)

The model carries an untyped, unwritten WADM authorship slot (`creator?: unknown`, wadm/types.ts:148) and a first-class curated Reading (model.ts:207, published as its own AnnotationCollection) with name/description/colour but NO owner; Library and Exhibit (model.ts:220,247) likewise have RightsFields but no author. The identity data exists and is captured (App.svelte:113, collab-attribution.ts:23 — 'the stamp IS the chosen display name'), stamped on every append, yet no layer above the note models 'who authored this reading / this exhibit's annotations'.

Rungs: L1 over-provides (an authorship slot + a curated-pass concept are modeled) -> L2/L4 under-deliver (no attribution is ever written at the reading/exhibit level, and note-level creator is empty).
Who feels it: A multi-author or attributed-scholarship library today cannot credit who authored a given Reading or annotation set at any layer; the workaround is baking authorship into free-text prose or the requiredStatement, where it isn't structured or per-artifact.
Intent: designed-latent + forgotten-latent — repo evidence: `creator?: unknown` is a reserved-but-undesigned WADM slot (typed as the loosest possible type, zero writers), and DARKDATA's 'pursue' verdict on per-note lastEditor attribution is the app-facing sibling of this modeling gap. Whether authorship should be a first-class Archie concept (an Agent/Author entity referenced by notes/readings/exhibits) is a modeling decision the human should make, not a mechanical emit.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: corrected. Corrections: 1) RightsFields is not credit/license-only: it carries `metadata?: MetadataEntry[]`, and DEFAULT_METADATA_FIELDS (model/dcterms.ts:145) defaults `dcterms:creator` for library, exhibit, and object — a structured per-artifact author field exists at those layers, contradicting "the workaround is free-text prose or requiredStatement, where it isn't structured." The real gap narrows to: Reading has no metadata/owner field at all, and nothing ties annotation identity (lastEditor) to any layer's credits or the WADM creator slot. 2) The DARKDATA "pursue" verdict on per-note lastEditor is stale as evidence of a live gap: apps/studio/src/collab-attribution.ts (Archie-90f1) already implements per-note attribution chips. It remains valid only as prior-interest context.

Strength: Worth exploring · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-render-core-2026-07-20.md

## Decision 2026-07-20 (grill)

PARKED until Archie-3452 (WADM created/creator emit) lands. The mechanical emit likely closes the interop hole; revisit first-class Reading ownership only if a real multi-author library materializes. Do not start this ticket while the dependency is open.
closeReason: PARKED (grill verdict 2026-07-20, recorded pre-close in the ticket body): blocker Archie-3452 has landed, which likely satisfies the interop need. description:

A session on these tickets should read element.ts (#applyFragment / #openAvObject landing), target-resolve.ts + content-state.ts (the pure cite-ladder resolver that OVER-provides fragments the reader drops), read-overlay.ts + frame-overlay.ts (the two clickable-overlay shapes with divergent a11y), and read-mount.ts (ReadOnlyMountSurface, which omits the fitRegion its sibling MountSurface in surface.ts exposes). title: The embed image annotation overlay is a keyboard/AT dead end and announces raw ULIDs
description:
## Question

Make the embed's read-only annotation overlay keyboard- and screen-reader-accessible. In read-overlay.ts add tabindex=0 and a keydown (Enter/Space -> same emitSelect as click) to each region shape's focusable element; in frame-overlay.ts give the whole-object border role=button, an aria-label, tabindex, and keydown parity with its click. In reader.ts openObject, pass a labelFor derived from the object's annotations (first line of commentOfAnnotation for the id, plain text) so shapes announce a human name; the option already exists through createReadOnlyMount. Done when: keyboard Tab reaches every region + the whole-object frame, Enter/Space opens the note card, and aria-label reads the note text; read-overlay-security.test.ts + read-overlay-geometry.test.ts stay green with added a11y assertions. Safety: setAttribute-only for aria-label (never innerHTML — the no-markup rule in read-overlay.ts header stands); label text must be the sanitized/plain comment, not raw selector values; per-package 'cd packages/render-mount && pnpm exec vitest run' and 'cd packages/archie-viewer && pnpm exec vitest run'; keyboard focus/activation on a live OSD surface is browser-verify-owed (recipes/example.html).

## Evidence (verified)

In the read-only reader a keyboard/screen-reader visitor cannot select any region note. read-overlay.ts:128-146 sets role=button + aria-label on each region shape but NO tabindex and NO keydown — role=button alone isn't focusable, and there's no Enter/Space activation. The whole-object frame-overlay.ts:80-85 has no role/label/tabindex/keydown at all (bare click listener). And reader.ts:57-74 openObject never passes labelFor, so read-overlay.ts:130 falls back to 'annotation <rawULID>' as the accessible name. The AV cue band (av-player.ts:234-253) and the grids (element.ts:520-578) use real <button>s — only the image overlay is unreachable.

Rungs: L3<->L4 — a11y scaffolding is half-built (role+aria-label present, labelFor threaded read-mount.ts:55/239 -> read-overlay) but keyboard focus/activation and a human name are never actually delivered.
Why: The plumbing already exists (labelFor wired end-to-end; the element holds note bodies via noteBodyHtml/commentOfAnnotation to source a real label) — it's just never actuated, so the fix is small but the gap is total for AT users. Lesson: a role=button without tabindex+keydown is a false a11y signal; wiring an option end-to-end but passing it from zero call sites delivers nothing.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed.

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-embed-runtime-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Merged (wf/embed-a11y 4178a7b): region shapes + whole-object frame keyboard-reachable (tabindex, Enter/Space via the same activate path as click, preventDefault on Space), human aria-labels from first plain-text comment line via stripMarkdown with 160-char cap at the single setAttribute chokepoint, setAttribute-only. Review APPROVE after one round; browser-verified 10/10 on live OSD. Merged-tree: render-mount 143/143, archie-viewer 126/126.

title: The embed drops Section-region and explicit ?xywh deep-link fragments (README advertises them)
description:
## Question

Give the embed's read-only image reader a region-fit path so Section and explicit-xywh deep-links land on the region. Add fitRegion(fragment: string) to ReadOnlyMountSurface + createReadOnlyMount, delegating to the shared applyFitBounds(viewport, {type:FragmentSelector, value}) exactly as mount.ts:374-384 does for the image path (a t= value no-ops on a spatial surface — same contract as the editor). In element.ts #applyFragment, when resolved.fragment?.kind===xywh is present, call surface.fitRegion after (or instead of) the selectId fit; keep the whole-object degrade for off-image regions via the existing clamp. Update the PARTIAL doc comment to reflect what's wired. Done when: a Section xywh start and an explicit ?xywh note cite frame the region in the embed; target-resolve.test.ts + read-mount.test.ts cover fragment->fitRegion. Safety: don't touch fixtures; the map/mapRegion path from mount.ts is out of scope (read-only mount has no bounded-map handling — image path only); 'cd packages/render-mount && pnpm exec vitest run'; OSD fit behavior is browser-verify-owed.

## Evidence (verified)

README.md:282-288 advertises the full cite ladder on the embed including Note ?xywh=x,y,w,h regions and Section #/{slug}/s/<id>. target-resolve.ts:113-150 fully computes a fragment (xywh/t) for section starts and explicit route xywh, but element.ts:421-429 #applyFragment applies ONLY selectId (the note's own shape) and DROPS resolved.fragment — so a Section whose start is xywh=..., or an explicit ?xywh override on a note cite, opens the right object but lands whole-object, not the region. The honest doc comment there flags it PARTIAL. Root: ReadOnlyMountSurface (read-mount.ts:31-42) has no fitRegion, though the editor MountSurface (surface.ts:41-44) exposes one over the SAME applyFitBounds(viewport, selector) oracle already imported into read-mount.ts.

Rungs: L1<->L2<->L3 — documented purpose (README) over-claims; behavior lands whole-object; the structural cause is the read surface omitting a fitRegion its own layer already implements.
Why: The resolver is pure surplus here — it computes the exact fragment the reader throws away, and the missing surface method exists a few lines over in the sibling mount. Closing it is mostly wiring, not new machinery, and makes a README-advertised feature true. Lesson: when a pure resolver over-provides a value the imperative sink can't consume, the gap is a missing seam on the sink, not a resolver bug.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: corrected. Corrections: Finding says fitRegion delegates to "the SAME applyFitBounds(viewport, selector) oracle already imported into read-mount.ts". read-mount.ts:16 actually imports dispatchFitBounds (the id-keyed sibling) from fitbounds.js — applyFitBounds itself is not currently imported there; a fitRegion port would add that import. Same shared oracle module, so the substance (thin wiring, not new machinery) holds. All other cited evidence is accurate: README:~282 advertises ?xywh and Section deep-links; target-resolve.ts:113-150 computes section-start and explicit-xywh fragments; element.ts:421-429 #applyFragment applies only selectId and drops resolved.fragment (self-documented PARTIAL at 414-419); ReadOnlyMountSurface (read-mount.ts:31-42) lacks fitRegion while surface.ts:44 / mount.ts:374-384 have it.

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-embed-runtime-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Merged (wf/embed-deeplinks 8e55bcb): ReadOnlyMountSurface.fitRegion on both implementers, delegating to shared applyFitBounds exactly as the editor's image path; element.ts #applyFragment fits resolved xywh (explicit cite wins, synchronous-deterministic); PARTIAL doc comment now truthful. Review APPROVE (opus) incl. merged-preview; browser-verified: section-xywh landing frames region at 0.840 vs 0.139 control. Merged-tree: render-mount 146/146, archie-viewer 131/131. Upstream /a/{logicalId} emission gap tracked as Archie-b9f4.

title: AV deep-link to a timed note doesn't seek to or surface that note
description:
## Question

Make an /a/<noteId> deep-link to a timed AV note land on the moment. Either (a) extend target-resolve to carry a t fragment recovered from a note's own t= selector (mirror regionOfNote for time), or (b) pass resolved.selectId into mountAvPlayer and have it seek-paused to that cue's range.start + activate/show it on mount, reusing the existing click path (av-player.ts:246-249). Prefer whichever keeps the resolver pure and the seam thin; seek-paused only (no auto-play, section-142). Done when: an AV note cite opens paused at the cue, highlights it, and shows its note card; av-player.test.ts + target-resolve.test.ts cover it. Safety: don't auto-play; keep the offline gate; 'cd packages/archie-viewer && pnpm exec vitest run'; media loadedmetadata timing is browser-verify-owed.

## Evidence (verified)

element.ts:384-405 #openAvObject reads ONLY resolved.fragment?.kind===t for the initial paused seek and IGNORES resolved.selectId. For an /a/<cueId> cite to a timed AV note, target-resolve.ts regionOfNote (lines 82-96) recovers xywh= only — a note whose selector is t=start,end yields no fragment — so the AV object opens at head 0 with no seek, no active-cue highlight, and no note card, even though the resolver handed back the note's raw id. The image reader select+fits the equivalent note; the AV path doesn't.

Rungs: L2<->L4 — behavior lands one step short of the cited moment; the resolved selectId (and the cue's derivable start time) are computed but unused on the AV landing path.
Why: Same README claim as Issue 2 (Note cites work for every object) but a distinct code path and fix. The cue's time is already parseable (av-player.ts cuesOf -> parseMediaFragment), and the AV player already seeks+highlights+shows a cue on click — the landing just needs to drive that same path from the resolved selectId. Lesson: two media surfaces sharing one cite ladder must each consume the full resolved target, or one silently under-delivers.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed.

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-embed-runtime-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Merged (wf/embed-deeplinks 8d22f42): AV deep-link lands seek-PAUSED at the cited cue via initialSelect (seam b — resolver untouched), highlights it, opens its note card; initialSeek precedence pinned; zero play() calls; cached-media ordering verified. Review APPROVE (opus). Browser-verified with real WAV + loadedmetadata: ct=12, paused, cue active, card open. Merged-tree gates green.

title: The read-only surface exposes none of MountSurface's spatial-overview aids
description:
## Question

title: 'Open my site' (and every non-login external link) is silently dead in the desktop app - opener scope allows one URL
description:
## Question

Widen opener:allow-open-url in src-tauri/capabilities/default.json to cover the URLs the app actually opens: the published site (https://*.github.io/**), github.com, and the GitHub API host used by links - or broaden to https://** if that's the intended trust posture (grill the human on which). Route the Publish.svelte secondary anchors (commit/pages-settings/docs) through the same openUrl seam rather than raw target=_blank, since a webview won't open them. Done-when: on desktop 'Open my site' opens the live URL in the system browser and no external link is a silent no-op. Safety: capability change compiles into the binary via generate_context! - needs a tauri build to take effect (don't claim it verified without one; the a09d smoke can host the check). Do not loosen script-src or any CSP directive; this is opener scope only. Keep the token off any opened URL.

## Evidence (verified)

capabilities/default.json:24-27 scopes opener:allow-open-url to exactly https://github.com/login/device. But the primary success CTA - Publish.svelte:717 'Open my site' -> machine.openSite() -> openUrl(result.url) where result.url is the *.github.io site - is not in that scope, so the opener command rejects it, and publish-machine.svelte.ts:467 swallows the rejection with .catch(()=>{}). The button does nothing on desktop. The secondary <a target=_blank> links in Publish.svelte (commit, Pages settings, custom-domain docs) rely on default anchor behavior, also unreliable in a chromeless webview.

Rungs: L2<->L4 - a capability allow-list (L4) narrower than the app's actual external-link behavior (L2) turns the publish flow's payoff moment into a no-op.
Why: The whole publish journey exists to end with the author seeing their live site; the final click is dead only in the packaged product the feature ships in, and the swallow hides it. General lesson: a permission allow-list is a behavioral contract - scope it to what the code actually opens, and don't .catch(()=>{}) a security-scoped call whose denial is user-visible.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed.

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-tauri-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Merged (wf/publish-surface 6f3630d): opener capability widened to github.com/**, *.github.io/**, docs.github.com/** (never https://**) AND a seam-side https-only hostname allowlist in openExternal (reviewer-required — remote-response URLs reach the seam verbatim; glob can't pin wildcard hostnames); silent .catch removed, failures surface as non-fatal openUrlFailed; all 8 Publish anchors routed on desktop, web anchors structurally unchanged; token-hygiene pinned. title: Flatpak 'stay signed in' will fail silently - keyring can't reach the Secret Service D-Bus name in the sandbox
description:

Add --talk-name=org.freedesktop.secrets (and verify whether tauri-plugin-opener needs the OpenURI portal, i.e. --talk-name=org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop, for the issue above) to finish-args in src-tauri/flatpak/digital.compost.archie.yml. Don't broaden finish-args beyond what the keyring/opener actually need; --filesystem=home is already the write scope, leave it.

## Evidence (verified)

github.rs persists the OAuth token via keyring (sync-secret-service, which talks to org.freedesktop.secrets over the session bus). flatpak/digital.compost.archie.yml finish-args (lines 17-24) grant wayland/x11/pulseaudio/dri/ipc/network/--filesystem=home but share NO D-Bus access to the secret service (no --talk-name=org.freedesktop.secrets). Inside the sandbox the keyring call is denied, so gh_token_save returns false and gh_token_load returns None - the user is signed out every launch, exactly the 'stay signed in' feature failing where it's supposed to work. Cargo.toml:35-36 and PUBLISH-TO-WEB-PLAN.md Q-E4 both flag this as an unfinished packaging item.

Rungs: L2<->L4 - a manifest omission (L4) silently disables a shipped behavior (L2, stay-signed-in) only in the packaged artifact, where no dev-run would catch it.
Why: The token-custody feature is fully built and unit-tested in Rust, but the one environment it ships in can't reach the store - the leverage is that a two-line manifest gap defeats a whole subsystem. General lesson: a feature that depends on a host service must have its sandbox portal/permission wired in the SAME change as the code, or it's dark on delivery.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed. Corrections: Cargo.toml keyring comment/dep is lines 33-37 (cited as 35-36); manifest finish-args span lines 17-25 (cited 17-24). Both trivial off-by-a-few; substance intact.

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-tauri-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Merged 1cc1ee8 (wf/flatpak-pack 3d6bc69): --talk-name=org.freedesktop.secrets added to finish-args with rationale comment; opener needs NO portal talk-name (verified against tauri-plugin-opener 2.5.4 -> open crate -> xdg-open shim -> OpenURI portal, default-allowed; documented in-manifest). appstreamcli + YAML/XML gates pass. title: Flatpak listing polish: add screenshots + developer to metainfo (submission quality — validators pass today)
description:
## Question

Add a <screenshots> block (source from docs/screenshots/auto/*.png; Flathub needs reachable https URLs — raise the hosting question rather than inventing one) and a <developer> element to src-tauri/flatpak/digital.compost.archie.metainfo.xml. Done when: --strict infos addressed and a screenshots block with a caption exists; keep release version in sync with tauri.conf.json (1.0.0). Safety: metainfo (and desktop file if flagged) only; no builds.

## Evidence (verified)

src-tauri/flatpak/digital.compost.archie.metainfo.xml has a valid id/name/summary/description/categories/OARS/release, but no <screenshots> element and no <developer>. appstreamcli validate / the Flathub linter require at least one screenshot for a distributable listing, so the manifest that exists to make Archie installable is not actually submission-ready. The manifest is otherwise fully scaffolded (desktop file, icons, modules), which is what makes the gap look finished when it isn't.

Rungs: L1<->L4 - the packaging's stated purpose (a distributable, listable desktop app) vs. a metainfo file (L4) that fails the validation gate that purpose requires.
Why: Everything around it - binary install commands, icons, desktop entry, OARS rating - signals 'ready to ship,' so the missing screenshots read as done rather than absent; a packaging pass that trusts the scaffold ships an unlistable app. General lesson: for artifacts gated by an external validator, the gate (appstreamcli) is the definition of done, not the presence of the file.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: corrected. Corrections: 1) The claim "appstreamcli validate ... require[s] at least one screenshot" and that the file "fails the validation gate" is measured false: `appstreamcli validate` (AppStream 1.0.6, plain / --pedantic) PASSES with exit 0 on src-tauri/flatpak/digital.compost.archie.metainfo.xml — only two info-level notices (cid-maybe-not-rdns, developer-info-missing); missing screenshots is not flagged at all. The Flathub linter's own appstream check (`flatpak-builder-lint appstream`, v3.0.0) also passes, exit 0, same two infos. Only `--strict` fails (exit 3), and on those infos, not screenshots. 2) Consequently the finding's done-when ("appstreamcli validate passes with no errors") is already satisfied TODAY with zero changes — it is a broken acceptance criterion; the real gate for screenshots is Flathub's repo-level lint (appstream-missing-screenshots) / quality guidelines at submission time, which I could not run without a build. 3) `<developer>` missing is an info, not an error, in current appstream.

title: The native desktop backend is built but the working store still rides OPFS blobs - the reliable path is used only for export
description:
## Question

Pursue, park, or kill: The native desktop backend is built but the working store still rides OPFS blobs - the reliable path is used only for export?

## Surplus (verified)

packages/render-core/src/fs/tauri.ts header declares 'a native folder on disk is the canonical store, written in place' and warns OPFS/FSA are 'unreliable' under WebKitGTK - yet store.ts:38 mounts OPFS (navigator.storage.getDirectory) as the working store unconditionally on desktop. TauriFilesystem is used only for user-picked folder bindings (folder-backend.ts); defaultLibraryRoot() (tauri-fs.ts:36, appDataDir/library) is a DEAD export (zero importers); the $APPDATA/** fs:scope + assetProtocol scope + the protocol-asset cargo feature have no consumer (no convertFileSrc anywhere). README.md:44-48 still lists asset-protocol image loading as 'the real remaining work.'

Rungs: L4/L3 surplus (a whole native backend + capability scopes + a dead default-root helper) -> L2 under-delivery (the desktop working store, where all authoring lives before export, sits on the path the backend's own header calls unreliable).
Who feels it: A desktop user's entire session - every image, annotation, autosave - persists to OPFS inside WebKitGTK, the exact store the native backend was written to replace; if OPFS misbehaves under the packaged webview, work is at risk on the primary journey while the reliable native store is reserved for the export button.
Intent: designed-latent - the header text, the appDataDir helper, the $APPDATA capability scope, and the enabled assetProtocol all encode an intended 'native folder is canonical' design that the wiring never completed; it stalled at 'OPFS working store everywhere + native folder as an export sink.'

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: corrected. Corrections: 1) The "real remaining work" asset-protocol text is in src-tauri/README.md:44-48, not the root README.md (root README has no such section). 2) "Reliable path is used only for export" is slightly overstated: Tauri FolderBindings serve both the publish sink (publish-flows.svelte.ts:384) AND a one-shot open/import source (binding-store.svelte.ts:280 "loadLibrary ← FolderBinding.fs → replace OPFS project") — but in both cases the resident working store remains OPFS, so the substance is unchanged.

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-tauri-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Grill verdict: PURSUE NOW (declined the park-until-folder-AV default) — native folder becomes the canonical desktop store; folder-AV plan folds in. Work ticket: Archie-623e.

title: Native-http CORS/redirect bypass is applied to audio only - remote images have no escape hatch
description:
## Question

Pursue, park, or kill: Native-http CORS/redirect bypass is applied to audio only - remote images have no escape hatch?

## Surplus (verified)

tauri-fs.ts:67 fetchRemoteAsBlobUrl fetches via @tauri-apps/plugin-http (native, no webview CORS / cross-origin-redirect rules) and hands back a same-origin blob: URL, existing specifically because the webview's own fetch fails 'Load failed' on redirecting hosts (e.g. archive.org MP3 302s). It is consumed by exactly one caller: AvEditor.svelte:81. Remote images and IIIF (info.json + tiles) are fetched straight by the webview/OpenSeadragon - no native-fetch path (grep found no convertFileSrc / OSD ajax hooks in studio src).

Rungs: L3/L4 surplus (a proven native-fetch bridge) -> L2 under-delivery (remote-image ingest still rides the webview fetch the bridge exists to bypass).
Who feels it: An author adding a remote image or IIIF manifest from a host that CORS-restricts or 302-redirects gets the same 'Couldn't load this media item' the AV path already solved; their workaround is to download and re-upload the file, if they figure out why it failed.
Intent: unknown - the AV path was likely built reactively for a specific archive.org failure; whether images were deliberately scoped out or just never hit the same failure isn't recorded. Repo evidence: the tauri-csp.md rule notes remote IIIF loads are a first-class case (the default Voynich seed loads Yale IIIF), so the exposure is real even if unproven for a redirecting host.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed.

title: Four unshared Playwright 'drive-and-shoot' harnesses; two (verify-marginalia, verify-readings-rail) are silently broken and non-gating
description:
## Question

Read-only survey first. For verify-marginalia.mjs and verify-readings-rail.mjs, confirm whether the marginalia-reflow / readings-pen-independence behaviors they target are already asserted by unit tests (packages/render-svelte, packages/render-core/geometry) or the studio e2e suite. If covered: delete both scripts and their dead maxMarkFillOpacity. If not: fix the base URLs to match apps/studio/e2e/playwright.config.ts (/studio/ base, /viewer/ routes), promote drewIntoPen from WARN to a gating assert, and extract the duplicated assert/settle/launch into one shared module that capture-screenshots.mjs and seed-fixture.mjs also import. Done-when: no non-test driver hardcodes a wrong base; assert/settle/launch has a single home; the readings keystone and margin-reflow either assert or are gone. Guards: NEVER touch apps/studio/e2e (the CI gate); do not regress seed-fixture.mjs's server-discovery (it is the robust one); confirm feature coverage before any delete.

## Evidence (verified)

The 'seed a fixture, drive Studio/Viewer, act on the canvas' concern is implemented 4 ways outside tests - capture-screenshots.mjs, seed-fixture.mjs, verify-marginalia.mjs, verify-readings-rail.mjs - with copy-pasted assert/settle/launch (verify-marginalia.mjs:21-34 identical to verify-readings-rail.mjs:22-34) and a shared literal selector button.plate:not(.add) in all four (capture-screenshots.mjs:301, seed-fixture.mjs:176, verify-marginalia.mjs:45, verify-readings-rail.mjs:64). The two verify harnesses hardcode WRONG base URLs (verify-marginalia.mjs:16-17 and verify-readings-rail.mjs:17-18 use :5173/ with no /studio/ and :4321 with no /viewer/, so they 302/404), are marked 'parked, fails until...' in .scratch/plans/IMPROVEMENT-WORKLIST.md:59,71,86, and downgrade their keystone check to a non-gating WARN (verify-readings-rail.mjs:132-136 'drewIntoPen') with dead code left behind (verify-readings-rail.mjs:38-50 maxMarkFillOpacity, never called).

Rungs: L3<->L2 - one canonical page-object surface (apps/studio/e2e) re-derived four times by hand; two copies have already rotted to unrunnable and assert nothing.
Why: The app has exactly one selector/route/seed surface; four independent re-implementations of it drift the moment the UI changes, and two already have. Leverage: one shared driver module (or deletion of the rotted verifiers if unit/e2e already cover the feature) collapses the duplication and makes 'this harness can't even reach the app' impossible. Lesson: a verification script that can't reach the app, or that WARNs instead of asserts its own headline behavior, is worse than no script - it reports green over an unchecked surface.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: corrected. Corrections: IMPROVEMENT-WORKLIST.md marks only verify-marginalia.mjs as "(parked, fails until re-wired)" — at line 71 only. Line 59 is the original shipped-harness note for verify-marginalia; line 86 records verify-readings-rail as "9/9" passing (awaiting the B3 human comprehension gate), not parked. So "two are marked parked at :59,71,86" is wrong: one script is documented-parked; the other's brokenness is inferred (correctly) from its hardcoded :5173/ base lacking the mandatory /studio/ prefix plus the non-gating WARN. Minor: capture-screenshots.mjs uses the plate selector at 4 sites (301, 332, 367, 498), not just :301.

title: capture-screenshots.mjs feeds the README but never fails and never validates its output
description:
## Question

Add a post-run gate to capture-screenshots.mjs: after the sweep, assert every expected shot in the manifest wrote a file exceeding a small min-size floor and that skipped-count is 0; exit non-zero otherwise. Optionally add a manual/nightly CI job (NOT the fast PR gate - it needs both dev servers running) that runs the sweep and fails on any skip. Done-when: a deliberately-broken selector makes the script exit non-zero instead of silently skipping. Guards: keep it off the per-PR unit jobs (dev-server dependency); do not weaken the existing best-effort behavior for shots that are genuinely optional - gate only on the manifest's declared set.

## Evidence (verified)

Every failure path records a shot as 'skipped' and continues (capture-screenshots.mjs:99,277,313,349,515,529), and main (:629-643) exits 0 even if 100% of shots skipped. There is no dimension/pixel/readback check (shoot :81 writes and trusts blindly), and the 23-shot manifest.json it writes (:79-83) is read by nothing. The README embeds these PNGs as its front-page proof (README.md:5,92,104 -> docs/screenshots/auto/*.png). A selector or route rename therefore silently produces stale or blank documentation images on a green run.

Rungs: L2<->L1 - behavior is best-effort-never-fails, but the purpose is to keep the README/docs faithful to the running app; the pipeline stops one step short of verifying it produced valid, current images.
Why: This is the docs-truth generator, and it has no completeness or sanity gate, so doc-rot is invisible until a human happens to look at the rendered README. Leverage: a cheap post-run assertion (every manifest-declared shot wrote a file above a minimum byte size, and zero entries are 'skipped', else exit non-zero) converts silent rot into a signal. Lesson: any generator whose output humans trust needs a self-check, or 'the run was green' stops meaning 'the output is good'.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed. Corrections: Minor cite errors only: manifest.json is written at capture-screenshots.mjs:639 (in main), not ":79-83" — that range is shoot(), which writes the PNG and pushes the manifest entry. Also the README embeds a fourth auto shot (viewer-readings.desktop.png at README.md:98) beyond the three lines cited (5, 92, 104).

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-toolchain-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Merged (wf/toolchain-pipeline 329ee4d): capture gate (zero skips, per-viewport, >=10KB floor) with no exit-0 escape; wiring it exposed and fixed month-old rot (sunset /bidar route, three retired selectors, wrong-element .tile). Proven: exit 1 vs dead servers, 22 captured/0 skipped vs live stack. Kept off per-PR CI.

title: README links a docs/guide/ user guide that does not exist; the real guide is generated into gitignored .scratch/guide/
description:
## Question

Either (a) promote the guide from .scratch/guide/ into a tracked docs/guide/ and wire that promotion into whatever step builds it (it shares the screenshot pipeline of the capture-screenshots issue), or (b) if the guide is not meant to ship yet, correct the three README links to the real location or mark it as not-yet-published. ## Evidence (verified)

README.md presents docs/guide/ as the primary onboarding walkthrough in three places (README.md:11 'user guide', :108 'The user guide walks the whole arc', :364 docs table row). Why: A doc artifact promised in the README must land in a tracked path or the promise is empty. Leverage is small and the defect is fully verifiable. title: Root apps-dist size ratchet (bundle:check) is orphaned with a month-stale baseline, while its embed-bundle twin got wired into CI
description:
## Question

Refresh docs/bundle-size.json against current main (studio should reflect the post-lazy-Canvas numbers), then add `pnpm bundle:check` to the gh-pages-build job after the build step (dist is already present there). Done-when: an injected >10KB studio bundle bloat fails CI, and the baseline reflects current main. Guards: refresh the baseline in the SAME PR or the first CI run fails on a month of accumulated drift rather than a real regression; keep the check off the fast unit jobs (it needs built dist); do not fold it into the archie-viewer-artifact job (different bundle, different baseline).

## Evidence (verified)

scripts/bundle-size.mjs has a full --check ratchet (fails on >max(10%,10KB) gz growth vs docs/bundle-size.json) exposed as root bundle:check (package.json:15), but it is DISTINCT from the archie-viewer package's bundle:check (build.mjs --check) that CI actually runs (checks.yml:175). Grep confirms scripts/bundle-size.mjs runs in no workflow. The committed baseline is measuredAt 2026-06-22 (studio 443.9KB, viewer 356.6KB), predating the lazy-Canvas 340KB startup win, so it is both unwired and stale. A studio or viewer app-bundle regression ships silently.

Rungs: L4<->L2 - the ratchet and its baseline are fully built (implementation), but no gate consumes them so bundle growth is never caught (behavior); a size guard built to defend a hard-won perf win guards nothing.
Why: The gh-pages-build job (checks.yml:116-137) already builds both apps' dist, so wiring the ratchet is nearly one line; the maintainer wired the embed twin (checks.yml:174-175) but the apps twin was overlooked - the CI rationale comment (checks.yml:139-144) discusses sync-dist and the embed bundle but never mentions the apps ratchet. Lesson: when you wire one instance of a gate class, sweep for its siblings - a half-wired ratchet family gives false confidence.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed.

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-toolchain-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Merged (wf/toolchain-pipeline 12f7f6c): root bundle:check wired into gh-pages-build after the build step (not fast jobs, not embed artifact); baseline refreshed and RE-MEASURED on the merged Phase-1 tree: studio 558.8->560.3KB (+1.5, allowed +55.9), viewer 368.1->368.7 (+0.6, allowed +36.8) — ratchet holds, mechanism proven end-to-end by reviewer.

title: import-voynich.mjs is a deprecated, destructive dead script kept in scripts/
description:
## Question

Delete scripts/import-voynich.mjs. Before deleting, grep the repo (excluding .claude/worktrees and node_modules) for the filename and for its two helpers (pngDims, selectorToRect) to confirm no live caller. Done-when: the file is gone and no live reference dangles. Guards: this can ride along with the parallel-drivers issue's script cleanup; if any live path genuinely needs the JPEG/PNG header-dimension helper, extract it to a tested util first rather than keeping the whole importer.

## Evidence (verified)

scripts/import-voynich.mjs:1-6 header: 'DEPRECATED ... do not run ... It will OVERWRITE the hand-authored seed if re-run.' It targets a retired fixture schema, reads a sibling-relative ../anvil/... path that does not exist outside the author's checkout, and its only reusable logic (header-only pngDims/jpegDims :22-35, selectorToRect :43-55) is neither exported nor tested. It is invoked by nothing (manual-only, referenced only in .scratch planning notes).

Rungs: L3<->L1 - a script nothing would miss sitting in the live-tooling dir (structure), whose stated purpose ('kept as historical record') is already served by git history (purpose); meanwhile it is a loaded gun that corrupts apps/*/src/voynich.ts if anyone runs it.
Why: scripts/ should hold runnable tooling; a retired importer that silently overwrites hand-authored source is negative value - it can only cause harm or confusion. Leverage: deleting it removes a real footgun at zero cost (git preserves the history it claims to be). Lesson: 'kept for historical reference' is what version control is for; a destructive dead script in the tooling dir is a hazard, not documentation.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: corrected. title: The qa/ /goal ledger harness has converged and terminated but still exists as live machinery + a per-commit hook
description:
## Question

Pursue, park, or kill: The qa/ /goal ledger harness has converged and terminated but still exists as live machinery + a per-commit hook?

## Surplus (verified)

qa/ is a complete autonomous-loop subsystem - gate.mjs (exit-predicate math), add-features.mjs (dedupe + dry-streak), sync-csv.mjs, lib.mjs, an installed pre-commit hook that regenerates and git-adds features.csv every commit (qa/hooks/pre-commit), and a 46-row features.jsonl. qa/state.json = {turn:11, discoveryDryStreak:2, lastFeatureCount:46}: the dry-streak fixed point that PLAN.md:41-48 / gate.mjs:27 define as GOAL COMPLETE is already reached. The convergence machinery is built for an ongoing loop that has stopped.

Rungs: L2 over-provides (loop-termination + CSV-mirror + hook machinery still running) -> L1 under-delivers (the /goal loop it exists to drive is finished; its live role is now unclear).
Who feels it: Every committer on an installed clone pays a node invocation and a tracked features.csv churn per commit for a converged ledger nobody re-runs; a maintainer reading qa/ can't tell whether it is a living regression gate or a completed one-shot artifact.
Intent: designed-latent (built to be re-runnable) - but possibly forgotten-latent now that it has converged. Repo evidence: PLAN.md frames it as 'durable spec' and gate.mjs exits 0/1 'for CI callers', yet gate.mjs is in no workflow. Research/grill question: promote gate.mjs to an actual CI gate, or archive the harness and retire the per-commit hook. Note decided 'Issue 10 methodology doc drift' is about the docs - this is about the harness's live cost and role.

## Verification

Adversarial verify 2026-07-20: confirmed.

Strength: Strong · Ledger: ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-toolchain-2026-07-20.md
closeReason: Grill verdict: RETIRE. The /goal loop converged; archive the ledger, drop the per-commit hook. Work ticket: Archie-e8ef.

title: Freecut-informed optimization program
description:
## Notes

- Goal: the maximal optimization program distilled from the freecut study (memory, storage, import, export, transcoding). Charted 2026-07-20.
- Sources: docs/research/freecut-lessons.md (mind its erratum), docs/research/freecut-gaps.md, docs/research/freecut-unverified-claims.md (UNVERIFIED — verify before acting on any item), docs/research/browser-storage-quota.md; freecut source at "Prior Art/freecut" (commit a3ecfce).
- Already built — reference, don't re-propose: persist() + StorageBar absolute-usage UI (storage-quota.svelte.ts); attempt-and-catch ingest with no quota preflight (Issue 26, merge 847c6a8); TIFF→WebP transcode (tiff-transcode.ts); FSA/OPFS writes already atomic (createWritable is spec-atomic on close; only Tauri hand-rolls temp+rename); streamed publish (5725f02) — freecut's copy-don't-recompute guard is confirmatory, Archie always streams originals.
- Rejected by the grounding audit: SyncAccessHandle worker (zero jank evidence; folder-primary answers the same pressure better); HttpFilesystem range/prefetch (it only reads small published JSON — media never flows through it).
- Cross-tracker contracts: the storage-primary decision LIVES IN "Make the native folder the canonical desktop working store" (Archie-623e, grill verdict pursue-NOW, plan docs/plans/folder-av-originals.md) — feed it, never fork it. The AV poster plan lives in docs/thumbnail-mitigations.md gap 1. The tend backlog ISSUES.md is a separate system; don't mix.
- Tickets carry map:freecut-optimization + wayfinder:<type>. Claim (assignee + in_progress) before any work. Conventions: docs/agents/issue-tracker.md.

## Decisions so far

## Fog

- Frame-level AV features (scrubbing, annotation-time frame capture, WebCodecs export/transcode UI): parks the whole conditional discipline — runtime codec probing + fallback ladders, VideoFrame close()/transfer traps, decode batching + decoder backpressure, µs-vs-seconds units, idle-codec reclamation mid-job, awaitable flush(). Templates ready in freecut-lessons ranks 6–8 and unverified claims 6–13. Graduates only when a product decision wants frames.
- Studio general undo: the spine is a version DAG, not an undo buffer; freecut's gesture-scoped snapshot + reference-equality dedup + ring-buffer cap (freecut-gaps.md) is the how, product demand is the if.
- Import-validation depth: freecut Zod-gates its .freecut.zip on import; whether .archie.zip should validate beyond the marker sits in tension with render-core's per-item-tolerant read policy (unverified claim 18).
- On-device ML infra (Cache-Storage ONNX model cache, idle-evicted worker pools; freecut-gaps.md bonus) — only if transcription/semantic search ever lands.
- Server-side rendering/transcode (@mediabunny/server; freecut's warm-Chrome headless render service + Docker) — only if a server surface appears; the export-fidelity harness ticket is the near-term slice.

title: Add JSDoc composition context to every Studio component
description:
## Loop: claim-vs-reality diff

**Teaches:** documentation drift — documented context that isn't in the components is invisible to agents; every agent that opens a component file builds on incomplete context.

**Claims source:** `.interface-design/system.md` component table + surface/sibling descriptions + `design/_after-tokens.md`. The system.md names 18 components and describes their surface, siblings, and role. The code has none of this in the files themselves.

**Ledger:** ledgers/CLAIMS-composition.md — component | surface (claimed) | in file? | @composes documented? | resolution | commit | recheck

**Territory (documentation-only, zero code/logic/style changes):**
18 Svelte components in apps/studio/src/ — <script> JSDoc blocks only

**Phases:**
1. Extract every claim system.md makes about each component's surface, siblings, and role. Record claimed-vs-present for every component — fix nothing, finish the full diff first
2. Per row: add a JSDoc composition block immediately after `<script lang="ts">`:
   <!--
     @surface   canvas | paper | gallery | drawer | header | dialog
     @composes  sibling/slot components
     @variants  inline | popover | sidebar | card
     @constraint  when it should NOT render standalone
   -->
   One commit per component (or batch surface-aligned groups)
3. Re-run the diff — if any component still lacks its block, record and fix

**Surface map (from system.md):**
canvas: CanvasWorkspace · paper: NotesSidebar, NoteCard, NoteEditor, MetadataEditor, DetailsEditor, NarrativeEditor · gallery: GalleryWall, GalleryThumb, LibraryHome, ExhibitOverview · header: StudioHeader, SafetyState · drawer: Marginalia · dialog: PublishDialog, MergeReview, CmdK · overlay: CreateExhibitDialog, BulkRightsDialog, IdentityPrompt, HelpMenu

**Gates:** studio svelte-check 0/0, studio typecheck — doc-only, no code paths changed

**Done when:** re-running the full diff finds every component carrying its composition block, and svelte-check + typecheck are green.

title: Grill: reconcile shadow-rule contradiction — spec §7 vs tokens.css + atmosphere.css
description:
## Conversation card: pre-mortem

**Not a loop — a decision gate.** `design/_after-tokens.md` §7: "zero box-shadow." tokens.css defines 5 shadow tokens with the comment "kept from Soft Static." atmosphere.css and ~15 components use them. The spec and the code contradict each other. Someone needs to decide which one yields before any code moves.

**The contradiction:**
- Spec §7: "Still zero box-shadow. Elevation reads from the verdant bloom, the always-on grain, the vignette forest-shade at corners, and moss translucency tiers."
- tokens.css: --shadow-lift-low, --shadow-lift-mid, --shadow-signal-glow, --shadow-text-haze, --shadow-inset-fog
- atmosphere.css: .soft-card, .soft-btn:hover, .pixel-btn, .details-pencil:hover all use box-shadow
- Every dialog/modal (CreateExhibitDialog, BulkRightsDialog, IdentityPrompt, MergeReview, CmdK) uses box-shadow for elevation

**The question:** which option resolves the contradiction?
A. Amend §7 — accept shadows, document the soft-blur model as deliberate
B. Remove all shadows — replace with translucency tiers + borders per §6
C. Compromise — shadows only on floating surfaces (dialogs, popovers); remove from cards, buttons, hover states

**What to weigh:**
- Visual regression risk (B touches every elevated surface)
- The Soft Static legacy (tokens.css comment: "kept from Soft Static")
- Spec fidelity vs practical elevation (can translucency alone distinguish a dialog from a card?)
- Component churn per option

**Deliverable:** one decision recorded on this ticket — the chosen option + rationale. If B or C: a grep list of every selector that must change.

**Done when:** the decision is recorded. Implementation is a separate ticket.

---

## DECISION (2026-07-21): Option C — shadows only on floating surfaces

**Rationale:**

The authoritative spec is `.interface-design/system.md` § Depth, which predates and contradicts the current token values. It reads:

> "1–2px subtle shadows only where a surface floats above the canvas (popup, drawer); No heavy card shadows, no material-style elevation ramps."

This IS Option C — it was never a compromise, it is the spec the code drifted from. The current tokens (`--shadow-lift-low: 0 24px 48px -24px`, `--shadow-lift-mid: 0 40px 80px -32px`) are massive soft-blur shadows applied to cards, buttons, and hover states — precisely what the "no heavy card shadows" clause forbids.

**Why not A (amend the spec):** The Verdant Clearing identity thesis — "Depth is built from blur + light, never from a hard offset shadow" (atmosphere.css preamble) — is stronger than the convenience of keeping existing shadows. Amending the spec to accept them would make it a post-hoc description rather than a design constraint. Spec drift becomes precedent. The grain, bloom, vignette, and translucency tiers already carry elevation; shadows dilute the thesis.

**Why not B (remove all shadows):** Floating surfaces need plane separation. A scrimmed dialog over dark parchment without any shadow risks blending into the background. The spec itself carves out "popup, drawer" — those are floating surfaces that genuinely lift above the canvas. Translucency tiers distinguish a card from the canvas (same plane); they cannot distinguish a dialog from a card behind it (different planes). A 1–2px soft shadow on a scrim provides the necessary separation without becoming a material-design elevation ramp.

### Token classification

The five shadow tokens fall into four categories with distinct fates:

**Category 1: Lift shadows (`--shadow-lift-low`, `--shadow-lift-mid`) — elevation cues**
→ RESTRICT to floating surfaces only. Remove from all static surfaces, hover states, buttons, cards.
→ Token VALUES also need recalibration from 24-40px soft blur to spec-level 1-2px subtle lift (implementation ticket).

**Category 2: Signal glow (`--shadow-signal-glow`) — rationed attention signals**
→ KEEP. These are NOT elevation cues. They signal active/primary/selected states. The spec's restriction is on elevation, not on signal indicators. Uses:
  - `header > button.publish-signal` / `:hover` (App.svelte:2759-60) — the ONE rationed signal
  - `.create-add` (App.svelte:2905) — primary sidebar CTA
  - `.ns-start` (ExhibitOverview.svelte:1006) — "Start a narrative" CTA
  - `.frame-box.sel` (AvEditor.svelte:461) — selected frame indicator
  - `.capture-hint` (AvEditor.svelte:465) — capture-mode status
  - `.markbar .add` (AvEditor.svelte:496) — add-mark CTA
  - `.save` / `:hover` (NoteEditor.svelte:187-88) — Done button
  - `.primary` (IdentityPrompt.svelte:76, Publish.svelte:1111, SaveZipDialog.svelte:79)
  - `.signal-tile` (atmosphere.css:70) — primary card
  - `.swatch.on` (ReadingsEditor.svelte:74) — active reading dot
  - `.add button` (ReadingsEditor.svelte:101) — add reading CTA

**Category 3: Inset fog (`--shadow-inset-fog`) — recessed depth cues**
→ KEEP. These are depression, not elevation ("moss translucency tiers" per spec). Uses:
  - `.obj-thumb` (App.svelte:2972) — thumbnail inset
  - `main.drawing .canvas-plate::after` (App.svelte:3021) — draw-mode depth
  - `.vt-track` (AvEditor.svelte:470) — timeline track
  - `.cmd`, `.preview`, code blocks (Publish.svelte:1001,1025,1053) — inset code/preview

**Category 4: Text haze (`--shadow-text-haze`) — display text treatment**
→ KEEP. Used on headings (wordmark, stage h1, library h1, dialog h2). Not an elevation cue — it's a text rendering flourish.

title: Published-site deep links: should viewer URLs mirror Studio place grammar?
description:
## Question

Should published viewer deep links mirror Studio's place-addressable grammar (ADR-0024)?

Studio exposes `library/slug/slug+objectId` as real paths. The viewer reaches rungs below the
exhibit by **hash fragment**, and that is a deliberate, documented choice — not a defect.

## Correction (2026-07-20) — the "canonical URL drops deep rungs" framing was wrong

An earlier assessment proposed retargeting this ticket as a bug: that `/viewer/<slug>/` honours no
rung below the exhibit while `[slug].astro` calls itself the deep-link surface. Checked against the
files, that is not a defect:

- `apps/viewer/src/pages/sitemap.xml.ts:1-2` states the rule outright — "static pages only:
  hash-routed deep links can't appear (crawlers ignore fragments)" (Archie-b4f2, ADR-0013). Deep
  links are hash-routed BY DESIGN, and their absence from the sitemap is the correct consequence.
- The sitemap/`exhibitSlugs` vs `[slug].astro` `getStaticPaths` difference is also deliberate
  (Archie-77b2): every slug builds a page so an `unlisted` exhibit stays reachable by direct URL,
  while only the listed subset is advertised. The two enumerations are meant to differ.

So the real question is unchanged and still open: **should the viewer move from hash-routed to
path-routed deep links to mirror Studio's grammar?**

## What constrains the answer

- **ADR-0013** (canonical origin = GitHub Pages, static hosting): path-based deep rungs need either
  pre-rendering every object/note rung or a SPA fallback. That cost is the crux.
- **ADR-0024** (Studio place grammar) — the shape being mirrored.
- **ADR-0022** (IIIF content-state interop) — an existing external deep-link grammar the viewer may
  already owe compatibility to.
- Crawlability: the current hash scheme means no rung below the exhibit is indexable. Whether that
  matters is a product call, and it is the strongest argument for changing.
- Secondary scope: the `place.ts` / `route.ts` encode/decode asymmetry (unverified; check before use).

## Note on the dependency edge

The edge blocking this on Viewer parity (Archie-7aef) was cut: the URL-grammar question can be
framed and answered without first settling which surfaces propagate. Re-add it if that proves false.

## Input from the viewer-ux map (Archie-d5cd, 2026-07-25)

Stays on THIS map by decision — d5cd changes no grammar, so nothing pre-empts the Studio<->viewer
symmetry question. Measured input it now has:

- **V100 was never a grammar flaw.** route.ts parses every frozen rung correctly. The note rung
  failed because note-arrival.ts compared a URL ULID against a full published IRI. Fixed in
  Archie-67b6 without touching route.ts.
- **V24/V101** — the viewer READ four rungs it never WROTE; Archie-99b1 makes the address bar write
  every rung the grammar reads. So by the time this ticket is worked, the viewer side of the
  grammar is fully exercised in both directions, which is the state it should be compared from.
- route.ts remains the SINGLE definition; apps/studio/src/place.ts mirrors it (place.ts:27-31).

title: Viewer parity: which Studio decisions propagate to the viewer, at what fidelity?
description:
## Question

Which Studio redesign decisions must propagate to the published viewer, and at what fidelity?

This is a **scoping** ticket: its output is a decision about surface and fidelity, not a build.

## Scope the answer must cover

The candidate surface is the narrative reading surface plus the shared `NotePopup` — one component
used by both `Reader` (grid / steps-objects) and `NarrativeReader` (narrative / steps-sections).

Parity has **four** consumers, not two. Any decision must say what each gets:
1. `apps/viewer` (Astro + Svelte islands, read-only)
2. `packages/archie-viewer` (the embeddable bundle)
3. `packages/render-mount` (the framework-free mount seam)
4. the published static tree itself

## Governing prior decisions

- **ADR-0019** (embeddable read-only viewer) and **ADR-0021** (viewer target contract) — these
  constrain what the viewer is ALLOWED to grow. Read before proposing any propagation.
- The map's closed decisions are the input list; go through them one at a time and mark each
  Studio-authoring-only (must NOT propagate) or viewer-relevant.
- Reconcile with the two existing Phase 3 plans rather than inventing a parallel table.

## Why this matters beyond itself

It was the only bridge from the Studio overhaul to the viewer. Its edge to Published-site deep links
(Archie-33bf) has been cut — that question is answerable independently — so this ticket now blocks
nothing and can be taken whenever.
closeReason:
NO PARITY PROPAGATION from this map. The viewer is declared out of scope for the Studio UX overhaul, and gets its own audit as a separate wayfinder map (Viewer UX audit, label map:viewer-ux).

Rationale (user decision, grilling 2026-07-24):
- The map's declared source, ledgers/UX-AUDIT-studio-wireframes.md, has zero viewer mentions. Every closed decision on this map was reasoned about authoring affordances only. Propagating them to a read surface nobody audited is guesswork dressed as consistency.
- ADR-0019 forecloses visual parity anyway: the embed drops Annotorious/PixiJS and renders regions as a DOM-SVG overlay while Studio keeps Annotorious. Studio and the embed can never match at the marker layer; only contracts can.
- Most of this map's decisions have no read analogue at all (save vocabulary, create/import, add grammar, bulk selection, publish continuity, collaboration, editor chrome, Details affordance, narrative authoring locus).
- The couplings that do exist are already STRUCTURAL, not decisions to propagate: packages/render-core/src/query/marker-style.ts readingMarkerStyle is the single style source for App.svelte:1482 and ExhibitView.svelte:277; packages/render-core/src/url/route.ts is the single address grammar (and predates apps/studio/src/place.ts, which mirrors it).

CORRECTION recorded here, contradicting ledgers/MAP-READINESS-studio-ux-overhaul-2026-07-20.md:136-137: the viewer's ReadingLegend carrying no reading number is NOT a WCAG 1.4.1 gap. docs/research/a11y-interactions.md:102-104 names that exact component (ReadingLegend.svelte:38-39, swatch + name in role=radiogroup) as a surface that already satisfies 1.4.1, and :128-129 says don't touch it. The real 1.4.1 gap is the on-canvas marker, which is shared render-core code and therefore not a viewer-parity question.

Also dead, do not carry forward: the embed overlay keyboard/AT dead end, closed by Archie-9413 (merged 4178a7b); read-overlay.ts:184-191 sets role, aria-label, tabindex=0 and a keydown handler.

Successor: the Viewer UX audit map. Its first move is producing the read-side equivalent of UX-AUDIT-studio-wireframes.md; it must reconcile with docs/plans/EMBED-VIEWER-IMPLEMENTATION-STRATEGY.md:73-82 (Phase 3 route ladder) and docs/plans/SCALE-GALLERY-PLAN.md:100 (Phase 3 viewer parity) rather than inventing a parallel table.

description:
## Question

Which onboarding decks and empty-state cues went stale after the structural redesign wave?

## Path correction (2026-07-20)

This ticket originally named `apps/studio/decks/`. **That directory does not exist.** The canonical
source is **`docs/learn/`**, and it ships via build (`sync-learn`; the GH-Pages deploy bug was fixed
in b564ac2).

## What is already done — do not redo it

Archie-6595 (closed 2026-07-19) **already refreshed all seven decks against the shipped redesign**,
verifying every load-bearing claim against source before writing. Read its close reason first: it
records exactly what was rewritten and, importantly, that **five real-pixel screenshots could not be
honestly re-shot headlessly** — two structurally-wrong ones were removed (flagged in-file), three
conceptually-correct ones kept with re-shoot flags.

So the real question is narrower: **what landed after 2026-07-19 that invalidates a deck?**
Use `git log` since that date over `apps/studio/src` and `docs/learn`. One known item: **Deck 3 is
materially false on desktop after b7a747e** (unverified — confirm before rewriting).

## Governing inputs this ticket originally omitted

- **Archie-66b0's decision** — help is deck-centric: the tutorial deck IS the help investment,
  HelpMenu its only entry, and no new cue system is to be built. This bounds any answer here.
- **Archie-6595's close reason** — the state of the decks and the human re-shoot list.
- **Teach learning records 0006** (non-obvious-only filter) and **0007** (two-slides-per-step,
  container-fill) — the house rules for deck authoring.

## Scope note

Empty-state cues are the part 6595 did NOT cover. Grep the empty-state copy in `apps/studio/src`
and check which cues point at surfaces that moved or were deleted (MediaPicker, PublishDialog and
AddMapModal were all deleted during the wave).

## Split

The screenshot half is tracked separately and is blocked on the visual passes; this ticket is the
**prose** half and is actionable today.

title: Visual/design-system pass over surviving Studio chrome
description:
## Question

After the structural redesign wave, does the surviving Studio chrome hold together visually —
palette, spacing, typography, depth — across the reworked header, sidebar, rail, overview and
dialog surfaces? This is visual QA, not structure and not new features.

## This ticket now carries the shadow-rule implementation (absorbed from Archie-5c1d)

Archie-5c1d grilled the shadow-rule contradiction (spec §7 vs tokens.css + atmosphere.css) and
**recorded an Option C decision** with a concrete work list. Its promised `Archie-5c1d-impl` was
never filed; rather than file it separately, that work lands here.

From 5c1d's decision, roughly **65 selectors across ~18 files**, with `atmosphere.css` and
`App.svelte` the bulk:

- **Legacy 8-Bit Orbit aliases in tokens.css** now dead or needing re-evaluation:
  `--shadow-pixel`, `--shadow-pixel-strong`, `--shadow-pixel-cyan`, `--shadow-pixel-yellow`,
  `--shadow-pixel-btn`, `--shadow-pixel-btn-pink`, `--shadow-pixel-btn-active`.
- **Floating surfaces that KEEP lift shadows** after recalibration (shadow-lift-mid unless noted):
  BulkRightsDialog `.dialog`, CmdK palette, CreateExhibitDialog `.dialog`, HelpMenu `.help-menu`,
  IdentityPrompt dialog, MergeReview dialog, NotePicker popover, PropsDrawer drawer,
  Publish `.dialog`, ReadingsModal modal, SaveZipDialog `.dialog`, ShortcutsHelp sheet,
  TutorialModal modal, ExhibitOverview `.selection-tray`, MetadataEditor `.row-menu`,
  and Marginalia `.bucket` (shadow-lift-low).

## Added scope

- `atmosphere.css` in **both** apps (not just studio).
- `static-pages.ts:58`.

## Reading

- `design/_after-tokens.md` — the token system (Verdant Clearing); tokens are stable, the components
  wearing them were rewritten.
- `apps/studio/src/tokens.css`, `apps/studio/src/markers.css`.
- Archie-5c1d's full decision body for the selector list in its authoritative form.

## Open: how is a visual pass verified?

A visual QA pass with no artifact and no verification method is unresolvable. Decide the deliverable
before starting. Note: no visual-regression harness was found (grep for
`pixelmatch|toMatchSnapshot|visual.regression|baseline` across package.json, scripts/, apps/studio/e2e)
— but a harness under another name would not have surfaced, so confirm before concluding.

## Related

- Archie-c59a (tokenize markers.css) overlaps — check before duplicating. Its drop-shadow removal
  was the collision 5c1d was grilling.
- Blocks the screenshot half of the onboarding refresh.
