title: NoteEditor: adopt snippet-based composition for form sections
closeReason: Closed as speculative generality. Snippet-based slot overrides let CONSUMERS replace form sections - but NoteEditor has exactly ONE consumer (App.svelte:40 -> :2248 -> a single render at :2609), inside a snippet whose own comment says 'never forked (ADR-0006)'. There is no client for the extensibility, so the stated benefit cannot be realised. The contract is also self-contradictory (it promises no caller changes AND an API reduction, while adding snippet props to the existing 28). Prior art points the same way: anvil's 632-line AnnotationForm keeps flat props as the terminal shape. The Astryx corpus that motivated this contains zero occurrences of 'svelte' or 'snippet' - it is React+StyleX. PROVENANCE: see ledgers/PROVENANCE-astryx-tickets-2026-07-20.md. REAL DEFECT UNDERNEATH, worth its own ticket if it bites: commentEl = $bindable() lets App reach into NoteEditor's textarea (NoteEditor.svelte:32-33, :98). Snippets would not fix that.

title: Extract NoteEditor sub-primitives as importable Svelte components
description:
## Question

NoteEditor.svelte's internal sections — EmphasisField, TimeRangeField, ScopeToggle, CoLocatedStackCycler, ReadingSelect — are inline markup. Extract each as a standalone Svelte component. SafetyState.svelte is the model: small, one concern, exported.

## Scope

Extract from NoteEditor.svelte:
- EmphasisField.svelte — emphasis radio (normal/reduced/removed)
- TimeRangeField.svelte — AV mm:ss start/end inputs
- ScopeToggle.svelte — whole-object vs region toggle (ADR-0018)
- CoLocatedStackCycler.svelte — 1-of-N stack navigator
- ReadingSelect.svelte — reading dropdown (reuses reading-index.js)

Each component: own `<script>`, own `<style>` (or inherits from parent), own JSDoc composition block.

## Contract

- 5 new .svelte files in apps/studio/src/
- NoteEditor.svelte imports them, API unchanged to callers
- Gate: svelte-check 0/0, studio typecheck, studio vitest

## Context

Astryx component audit 2026-07-20. Studio map (Archie-21b1) Fog item.
closeReason: Closed as fragmentation, not deepening. NoteEditor.svelte is 199 lines with ~28 props; extracting five components from it fails the repo's own extraction bar (ZipExportFields.svelte was extracted at THREE consumers; none of these five clears one), and contradicts the TEND-EXPLORE-studio-2026-07-20 finding. Two of the five named sections were misdescribed by the source: the 'emphasis radio (normal/reduced/removed)' is a <select> over muted|normal|strong (NoteEditor.svelte:128-134), and ScopeToggle would re-add a toggle ADR-0018 deliberately rejected. The real decomposition target is App.svelte at 3147 lines. PROVENANCE: the 'Astryx component audit 2026-07-20' does not exist as an artifact - see ledgers/PROVENANCE-astryx-tickets-2026-07-20.md. CARRIED FORWARD (small, real, do these): the dead .note-popover rule and stale '@surface {popover}' docstring; the duplicated fmtMMSS; the stale line reference in e2e/loop.spec.ts.

title: tldraw → Archie architecture adoption
description:
## Notes

Domain: evaluating which of tldraw's static-app architecture patterns to adopt in Archie's render-core stack. Source: `ledgers/LEARN-tldraw-merged-2026-07-22.md`. Research: `ledgers/RESEARCH-tldraw-source-scout-2026-07-22.md` (source-backed).

Skills every session should consult: `wayfinder`, `seeds`, `domain-codebooks` (distributed-state/sync patterns for undo), `brainstorming` (for design tradeoffs).

Standing preference: prefer minimal, incrementally-adoptable solutions over full rewrites. The annotation spine is already solid — changes should compose with it, not replace it.

## Decisions so far

- [Research: tldraw signals internals](#) — Resolved. Minimal Archie signals API = ~500 LOC: atom (~140), computed core (~200), transact (~100), capture (~60). Key patterns: global epoch for change detection, lazy computed with 3-condition cache-hit, transact with rollback via initialAtomValues snapshot. Source-backed from tldraw main.
- [Research: tldraw HistoryManager + RecordsDiff](#) — Resolved. RecordsDiff = {added,updated,removed} + reverseRecordsDiff + squashRecordDiffsMutable. HistoryManager = 2-stack mark-based system (mark/bailToMark/squashToMark/batch, 3 modes). Maps cleanly to Archie: undo stack on top of append-only log as UI projection layer. Source-backed from tldraw main + docs.

## Fog

- **Manager decomposition boundaries** — when session.ts exceeds ~800 LOC, which concerns to extract into managers and what the manager interface looks like. Depends on signals + undo decisions.
- **Geometry objects with behavior** — when Archie adds a 3rd annotation shape type (maps, audio regions), adopt Geometry2d-style classes with hitTest/nearestPoint. Premature to spec now.
- **Self-contained export pipeline** — tldraw's StyleEmbedder + FontEmbedder + embedMedia pattern for single-file HTML. Research ticket Archie-5582 still open.

title: Grilling: schema version in archie.json marker
description:
## Question

Should Archie embed a schema version in `archie.json` (the .archie.zip self-ID marker) so loaders can auto-migrate old data? What would the migration runner look like?

## Context

tldraw embeds `schema: SerializedSchema` in every `StoreSnapshot` — old data loads cleanly after schema changes because the loader runs migrations automatically. Archie's migration system (`migrate/`) works but doesn't version the artifact itself.

Currently `archie.json` identifies the archive as Archie's format but carries no version number. Adding one would be ~20 lines.

## Open questions

1. What's the current schema version? Is there an implicit version number anywhere?
2. Where would the migration runner live — in `@render/core/migrate/`? In `@render/core/publish/open.ts`?
3. Should we add it now (preemptively) or wait for the next schema-breaking change?
4. Does this interact with the existing `migrate/object-ids.ts` engine?

## Acceptance

A close reason recording the decision + any resulting task tickets.

title: Research: tldraw signals internals
description:
## Question

What is the minimal signals API Archie needs from tldraw's @tldraw/state? Study the source to extract the core primitives (Atom, Computed, transactions) and identify what's essential vs what's tldraw-specific.

## Scope

Read from https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw:
- `packages/state/src/lib/Atom.ts` — atom implementation
- `packages/state/src/lib/Computed.ts` — computed/derived signals
- `packages/state/src/lib/transactions.ts` — batching
- `packages/state/src/lib/capture.ts` — dependency tracking
- `packages/state/src/lib/EffectScheduler.ts` — reactions
- `packages/state-react/src/` — the React bridge (to understand what the framework adapter looks like)

## Acceptance

A markdown summary in ledgers/ covering:
1. The core API surface (atom, computed, react, transact, unsafe__withoutCapture)
2. The dependency tracking mechanism (capture parents, global epoch)
3. What a Svelte 5 bridge would look like (analogous to state-react)
4. What tldraw does that Archie does NOT need (diff history, WhyAmIRunning debug)
5. Estimated LOC for a minimal Archie signals layer
closeReason: Resolved: source-scouted tldraw signals layer from GitHub main. Minimal Archie API: atom (~140 LOC) + computed core (~200 LOC) + transact (~100 LOC) + capture (~60 LOC) = ~500 LOC. Key patterns: global epoch for change detection, lazy computed with 3-condition cache-hit, transact with rollback via initialAtomValues snapshot. Full findings: ledgers/RESEARCH-tldraw-source-scout-2026-07-22.md §1.

title: Research: tldraw HistoryManager + RecordsDiff
description:
## Question

How does tldraw's HistoryManager use RecordsDiff for undo/redo, and how would this pattern compose with Archie's append-only annotation log?

## Scope

Read from https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw:
- `packages/editor/src/lib/editor/managers/HistoryManager/HistoryManager.ts` — the full implementation
- `packages/store/src/lib/RecordsDiff.ts` — the diff primitives (reverseRecordsDiff, squashRecordDiffsMutable)
- `packages/store/src/lib/Store.ts` — how the store emits diffs to subscribers

## Acceptance

A markdown summary in ledgers/ covering:
1. The RecordsDiff data structure and its operations
2. How HistoryManager accumulates diffs, creates marks, and replays
3. The batch/transact integration
4. How this would compose with Archie's immutable log (diff stack for UI undo, log stays append-only)
5. Estimated LOC for a minimal AnnotationUndoManager
closeReason: Resolved: scouted RecordsDiff (181 LOC) + HistoryManager pattern. Core: {added,updated,removed} + reverseRecordsDiff + squashRecordDiffsMutable (perf: for-in, in-place tuple mutation, no Object.entries allocation). History: 2-stack mark-based — mark, bailToMark, squashToMark, batch, 3 modes (Recording/RecordingPreserveRedoStack/Paused). Maps cleanly to Archie: undo stack sits ON TOP of append-only log as UI projection layer. Full findings: ledgers/RESEARCH-tldraw-source-scout-2026-07-22.md §2.

title: Prototype: minimal signals layer for render-core
description:
## Question

Can a minimal signals layer (~300 LOC) in @render/core replace the imperative state management in AnnotationSession with declarative derived state?

## What to build

Based on the research ticket (Archie-a7bd) findings:

1. Implement `atom`, `computed`, `transact` in a new `@render/core/src/state/` module
2. Wire into `AnnotationSession`: replace manual `workingAnnotations()` with a `computed`
3. Verify: derived state auto-invalidates on log changes
4. Verify: `transact` batches multiple appends into one recomputation
5. Verify: headless testability — `heads.get()` works in vitest without Svelte

## Acceptance

- A working prototype branch with the signals layer
- A test showing `computed` auto-updates when the log changes
- A test showing `transact` batches updates
- A note on whether the Svelte adapter becomes simpler (fewer manual `$effect` calls)
- Decision: adopt, iterate, or reject

title: Prototype: diff-based undo on append-only log
description:
## Question

Can a RecordsDiff-based undo stack on top of the append-only log provide O(1) undo/redo without compromising the log's immutability?

## What to build

Based on the research ticket (Archie-aeaf) findings:

1. Implement `RecordsDiff` + `reverseRecordsDiff` + `squashRecordDiffsMutable`
2. Build `AnnotationUndoManager` that wraps `AnnotationSession`
3. Support `mark(id)` and `bailToMark(id)` for composite operations
4. Verify: undo removes the UI projection of a note without deleting it from the log
5. Verify: redo restores the UI projection

## Acceptance

- A working prototype branch
- A test showing undo/redo cycle: create → undo (note gone from projection) → redo (note back)
- A test showing bailToMark: create A, mark, create B, bailToMark → only A remains
- A test showing the log still contains all versions after undo
- Decision: adopt, iterate, or reject

title: Task: embed schema version in archie.json marker
description:
## Question

Add a version field to the .archie.zip marker so loaders can auto-migrate old data.

## What to do

Based on the grilling ticket (Archie-fc75) decision:

1. Add `"version": <N>` to the `archie.json` marker structure
2. Update `validateArchieMarker` in `@render/core/publish/marker.ts` to read the version
3. Update `ZipFilesystem.fromZip` in `@render/core/publish/open.ts` to check version and run migrations
4. Wire the existing migration runner (`migrate/migrate.ts`) to the version check
5. Update tests for marker validation and version-gated loading

## Acceptance

- `archie.json` carries a version number
- Loading an older `.archie.zip` runs migrations automatically
- Loading a future version produces a clear error (not silent corruption)
- Tests cover: current version loads, older version migrates, future version errors

title: Prototype: single-file Archie exhibit export
description:
## Question

Can Archie produce a single self-contained HTML file that renders a full exhibit (image + annotations) with zero external dependencies?

## What to build

Based on the research ticket findings:

1. Start with a single-object exhibit (one canvas, its annotations)
2. Render the annotated image to a canvas (OSD + Annotorious → pixel output)
3. Inline all dependencies: fonts as base64, CSS as inline styles, JS as a single bundle
4. Output: one `.html` file that opens in any browser and shows the annotated exhibit
5. Verify: the file renders correctly when opened from disk with no network access

## Acceptance

- A working prototype producing a single `.html` file
- The file renders an annotated exhibit with no network requests
- Fonts, styles, and images are all self-contained
- Decision: adopt, iterate, or reject

title: Research: tldraw self-contained export pipeline
description:
## Question

How does tldraw's SVG/PNG export pipeline produce a fully self-contained artifact (no external fonts, images, or stylesheets)? What would a single-file HTML export look like for an Archie exhibit?

## Scope

Read from https://github.com/tldraw/tldraw:
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/exportToSvg.tsx` — the main pipeline
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/getSvgJsx.tsx` — JSX → SVG conversion
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/StyleEmbedder.ts` — computed style inlining
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/FontEmbedder.ts` — @font-face → base64 embedding
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/embedMedia.ts` — image/video → data URI
- `packages/editor/src/lib/exports/getSvgAsImage.ts` — SVG → PNG rasterization

## Acceptance

A markdown summary in ledgers/ covering:
1. The full pipeline: render-to-real-DOM → read computed styles → inline fonts/media → extract
2. How StyleEmbedder reads computed styles and writes inline attributes
3. How FontEmbedder discovers and embeds @font-face declarations
4. What a single-file Archie exhibit export would look like (HTML page with all CSS/JS/fonts inlined, annotations burned into the image)
5. What's transferable vs what's tldraw-specific (React-based rendering)
6. Estimated effort for a minimal single-file Archie export

title: Studio undo: gesture-scoped snapshots from freecut pattern
description:
The spine is a version DAG, not an undo buffer. Freecut's pattern (gesture-scoped snapshot + reference-equality dedup + ring-buffer cap — docs/research/freecut-gaps.md) is the documented how. Research scope: map the pattern onto Archie's spine API, estimate effort, identify blockers (signals layer? manager decomposition?). Deliverable: a plan or a "blocked on X" finding.

Note: product demand (whether to BUILD it) is the separate if — this ticket is the technical feasibility assessment only.

title: Viewer UX audit
description:
## Notes - **Origin:** Archie-7aef (Studio UX overhaul, Archie-21b1) resolved as NO PARITY — the viewer was declared out of scope for that map and handed its own audit. Read 7aef's close reason first; it carries the corrections this map must not re-derive. - **Domain:** Archie's read-only surfaces. Parity has **four consumers**, and every decision here must say what each one gets: 1. `apps/viewer` — Astro + 23 Svelte islands. ONE shell, TWO auto-detected data modes (ADR-0008): hosted (baked published tree) and portable (an opened `.archie.zip`, seam in `published.ts`, ADR-0010). Hosted and portable are one consumer, not two. 2. `packages/archie-viewer` — the embeddable `` bundle. Its markup was **ported, not imported** (`element.ts:9-10`), so it drifts silently from the shell. 3. `packages/render-mount` — the framework-free mount seam; `read-overlay.ts` is the shared read-only overlay and has its own package gate. 4. the published static tree itself (ADR-0014 self-describing artifact). - **Governing ADRs — read before proposing anything:** 0008 (one shell, dual mode), 0010 (portable read seam), 0014 (self-describing artifact), 0019 (embeddable read-only viewer), 0021 (target contract: full cite ladder + degrade-upward). 0019 and 0021 bound what the viewer is ALLOWED to grow. - **The hard constraint:** ADR-0019 drops `@annotorious/openseadragon` + PixiJS from the embed and renders regions as a DOM-SVG overlay, while Studio keeps Annotorious. The embed and Studio can never match at the marker layer. Only *contracts* (what is selectable, what a select does, what is reachable by keyboard) can be held in common — never pixels. - **Parity that is already structural, and must not be re-litigated as a "decision":** `packages/render-core/src/query/marker-style.ts` `readingMarkerStyle` is the single style source for both `apps/studio/src/App.svelte:1482` and `apps/viewer/src/components/ExhibitView.svelte:277`; `packages/render-core/src/url/route.ts` is the single address grammar and PREDATES `apps/studio/src/place.ts`, which mirrors it (see `place.ts:27-31`). - **Known duplication / live drift risk:** `apps/studio/src/markers.css` and `apps/viewer/src/markers.css` are byte-identical with a sync warning at `:7`; `tokens.css` / `atmosphere.css` are duplicated the same way and both pairs have already drifted. - **Reconcile, do not fork:** two Phase 3 plans already stake claims on this ground — `docs/plans/EMBED-VIEWER-IMPLEMENTATION-STRATEGY.md:73-82` (route ladder + degrade-upward) and `docs/plans/SCALE-GALLERY-PLAN.md:100` (Phase 3 — library-level Gallery incl. viewer parity). `docs/IMPLEMENTATION-STRATEGY.md:72` names brainstorming-first as the method for Phase 3 invention. - **Gates:** `pnpm --filter @archie/viewer run check:svelte` (svelte-check `--fail-on-warnings`, baseline 0/0 — a new warning fails CI). `astro check` covers `.astro` pages ONLY and proves nothing about an island. Per-app vitest via `pnpm exec vitest`. - **Dead claims — do not carry forward.** (a) The embed overlay keyboard/AT dead end was closed by Archie-9413 (merged `4178a7b`); `read-overlay.ts:184-191` sets `role`, `aria-label`, `tabindex="0"` and a keydown handler. (b) The viewer's `ReadingLegend` carrying no reading number is NOT a WCAG 1.4.1 gap — `docs/research/a11y-interactions.md:102-104` names that exact component as already satisfying 1.4.1 and `:128-129` says don't touch it; the real 1.4.1 gap is the on-canvas marker, which is shared render-core code. `ledgers/MAP-READINESS-studio-ux-overhaul-2026-07-20.md:136-137` is wrong on this point. - **Standing rules:** CHECK PRIOR ART before any approach (fff / `Prior Art/`), and cite it per decision. WWWWH-first copy. User-story template. Grilling tickets use `/grill-with-docs` — USER-INVOKED ONLY, ask the user to type it. Companions: `/domain-modeling`, `/prototype`, `product-copy`, `interface-design`, `shadow-walk` (read-surface walks are its exact shape). - **Adoptable open tickets living elsewhere** — decide whether each moves under this map: Archie-33bf (published-site deep links / viewer URL grammar, currently on the Studio map), Archie-eec7 (screen-reader walk), Archie-cf4a (touch design pass). - Tickets carry label `map:viewer-ux`. Claim (assignee + in_progress) before work. Frontier: `sd ready`. Conventions: `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md`. ### Charting decisions (grilling 2026-07-24 — settled, do not re-litigate) - **Method:** the Studio pipeline (tldraw board `archie-viewer-wireframes` → numbered findings naming surface / weakness / principle strained, per `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-studio-wireframes.md`), but wireframes built from a **real browser drive** rather than from reading markup — the four consumers drift silently, and only a drive catches it. - **Scope:** all four consumers, render-mount included. - **Slicing: VERTICAL, not horizontal** (user call). Each ticket takes one reader-journey vertical and audits it through shell, embed and seam TOGETHER, so drift surfaces inline. Slicing by consumer was rejected: three of four would independently re-derive the same shell findings. - **Judging standard — ratified, inherited from `docs/GOAL.md`, not this map's to decide.** The reader is *a first-time visitor opening a published Archie exhibit* (`:11-13`). With no users, evidence = an agent driving a real browser producing NUMBERS (`:15-18`). Priorities rank Look > Feel > Performance > Features (`:20-24`). - **The six verticals** (V-number ranges reserved so parallel sessions don't collide): 1. [Arrival](Archie-0cf5) V1–V19 · 2. [Browsing an exhibit](Archie-57dc) V20–V39 · 3. [Reading an object](Archie-c743) V40–V59 · 4. [The note](Archie-0f44) V60–V79 · 5. [The narrative](Archie-d143) V80–V99 · 6. [Leaving with something](Archie-18d0) V100–V119. - **Sequencing:** Arrival is first and the other five block on it — it is what the reader meets first, so the shared apparatus (board, roll-up index `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer.md`, the four-consumer drive recipe) falls out of doing real work rather than being invented by a scaffolding ticket. The five unblock together and may then run in parallel. - **Ledger layout:** one findings file per vertical, `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-.md`; the roll-up index is the only shared write (one line per vertical). Separate files because five sessions run in parallel. ### File territory — do not run concurrently (issued 2026-07-25) - **`packages/archie-viewer/` is CONTESTED.** A concurrent session was editing `element.ts`, `index.ts`, `reader.ts` and adding `reader-guards.ts` as of 2026-07-24 19:55, and rebuilt the bundle twice. Check `git log` and the working tree before claiming it. Two tickets write there — embed fidelity (`Archie-52a9`) and the embed pointer fix (`Archie-64ef`); don't run them as concurrent worktree agents. - **`packages/render-core/src/url/route.ts` is SHARED with Studio.** It is the single definition of the address grammar and predates `apps/studio/src/place.ts`, which mirrors it (`place.ts:27-31`). The addressing decision (`Archie-d5cd`) therefore has Studio-side consequences and cross-references `Archie-33bf` on the Studio map. - **`packages/render-core/src/query/marker-style.ts` is SHARED.** `readingMarkerStyle` is called by both `App.svelte:1482` and `ExhibitView.svelte:277`. The canvas-selection decision (`Archie-ed50`) must not treat it as viewer-local. - **`packages/render-mount/src/read-overlay.ts`** is written by `Archie-64ef` and read by `Archie-ed50`. ### Graduation shape (2026-07-25) The 76 findings graduated into **4 decisions + 9 defect tasks**, deliberately NOT 76 tickets — the findings cluster, and the clusters are where the thinking is. No blocking edges were wired: every decision is takeable now, and every defect task is fixable without waiting on one. The implementation tickets that WILL depend on the decisions don't exist yet; they graduate as each grilling closes. Two findings stayed in Fog rather than being forced into a ticket (see below). ## Decisions so far - [Audit vertical 1 — Arrival](Archie-0cf5) — 12 findings (V1–V12) in `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-arrival.md`; index + drive recipe in `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer.md`; board `archie-viewer-wireframes` (7 screens). HIGH: V1 empty hall is a one-way door (its only control is 'Open a library…'; Escape inert) · V2 Back restores the address but not the view · V3 degrade-upward announces itself on 2 of 3 rungs, slug rung silent · V9 embed and shell are visually unrelated products. MEDIUM: V4 dead address persists on 2 rungs, rewritten on the third · V6 mode-dependent search = Studio's W7 verbatim, fixed in Studio (Archie-2308) and never propagated · V7 no cover fallback (Studio has one) · V8 portable mode loses the lens toggle, against ADR-0008 · V11 embed resolves no thumbnails from a zip. SURPLUS V10: the embed's failed-src copy is the model the shell's failed-target path is missing — the fix already exists in-repo. Two overclaims cleared: the 'assets' card is a genuinely published exhibit, and the Report-a-Bug/Inspect/Audit links are Astro's DEV TOOLBAR — filter `astro-dev-toolbar` from all DOM queries. - [Audit vertical 2 — Browsing an exhibit](Archie-57dc) — 12 findings (V20–V31) in `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-browse.md`. HIGH: V24 the viewer reads an object address it never writes · V30 the embed offers no way to move between objects at all. Also V27 the filmstrip is 12 consecutive tab stops in a repo that ratified roving tabindex for this exact component (Archie-f260) · V23 four nav affordances agree where you are and disagree what you're looking at · V29 video is the only object type whose plate can render blank and its one guard cannot fire. - [Audit vertical 4 — The note](Archie-0f44) — 12 findings (V60–V71) in `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-note.md`. HIGH: V63 the reading sheet declares `aria-modal="true"` and implements none of it · V66 the author's alt text is deleted at the model boundary · V68 in the embed a note opens with the keyboard but not the mouse (PROVISIONAL — re-verify). Also V60 selecting a note shows it twice, expanding shows it three times · V69/V70 the embed's marker is a 1.5px near-black hairline with no reading colour, and there is no note list, so that invisible marker is the only door. - [Audit vertical 5 — The narrative](Archie-d143) — 12 findings (V80–V91) in `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-narrative.md`. HIGH: V81 the mode's central promise — "read down the page … the image follows along" — is NOT IMPLEMENTED · V80 canvas chrome renders on top of the spine · V82 a section cite lands the camera but strands the prose off-screen · V83 hiding the spine is sticky, global and near-irreversible · V84 stepping to the index and back loses your place, and the index has no address · V88 the embed drops the narrative entirely (prose in, thumbnail grid out). - [Audit vertical 6 — Leaving with something](Archie-18d0) — 11 findings (V100–V110) in `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-leaving.md`. HIGH: V100 the note rung of the cite ladder is UNSATISFIABLE — published note ids contain `/` and the route grammar is `/`-delimited, so an ADR-0021-frozen public contract cannot be honoured as written · V102 there is NO way to copy anything: zero clipboard or share affordances in the whole read surface · V101 five reader states share one URL · V105 the embed shows no attribution, licence or metadata (legal exposure) · V107 the crawler's page ships 31 characters of body text · V110 the archival page omits the narrative. Also V109 the sitemap enumerates 2 of 7 exhibits (extends TEND-EXPLORE I-V1). - [Audit vertical 3 — Reading an object](Archie-c743) — 17 findings (V40–V56) in `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-read-object.md`, AUDIT PHASE COMPLETE (6/6). HIGH: V40 the canvas zoom readout is painted 264px inside the notes panel · V43 select-to-zoom fits the region edge-to-edge so the selected thing leaves the frame · V44 selection has no on-canvas representation in EITHER consumer · V49 the AV surface's one novel affordance ships fully covered by the item strip · V50 the audio object is 860×700 of empty cream with a browser-default scrubber · V52 ADR-0021's `t=` landing seek is correctly built and structurally unreachable. EMBED RE-VERIFICATION against dist mtime 2026-07-24 19:52:37: all six provisional findings (V68, V69, V70, V30, V88, V105) STILL TRUE, no verdict flipped — V30 now confirmed on a 12-object exhibit, V69 measured as stroke rgb(42,35,32)/1.5px/no fill, V105 rests on the published tree (neither test zip carries rights, so absence there proves nothing). V68's mechanism pinned: the listener works (synthetic click opens the card); pointer events never reach the element, and the swallowed click produces ZERO feedback — bbox and zoom byte-identical after one and two clicks. Also corrected my own brief: recipes/try.html scripts the LOCAL dist (its jsDelivr line is commented), so only the numbered recipes pin the CDN. - [Fix arrival: give the empty hall an exit, and the slug rung its notice](Archie-4635) — V1–V5 fixed, on branch `fix/arrival-recoverable` (`0c55b0f` fix + `1b245ff` audit ledgers, off `c551367`), NOT yet merged. The chooser is now a dismissible surface over an intact library (Cancel + Escape) instead of a teardown; `sync()` dismisses it on navigation, which is what Back was missing; the slug rung announces itself using the shell-level twin of ExhibitView's `.arrival`; all four rungs normalize the address via `history.replaceState` (assigning the hash would remount ExhibitView through the `{#key}` and wipe the notice); the note-rung copy no longer asserts a deletion. Verified in real Chromium 14/14, zero page errors; svelte-check 1465/0/0, 136 tests. METHOD: svelte-check passed 0/0 against a build where `oncancel` was in EmptyHall's prop TYPE but missing from its destructuring — the Cancel button silently never rendered and only the browser drive caught it. - [Restore the author's alt text at the model boundary](Archie-ff79) — V66/V67 fixed, branch `fix/note-alt-text` (`91720fe`, off `f0cacbf`), NOT yet merged. `splitNoteMedia`'s MD_IMAGE regex matched the alt and captured only the URL — the description died in the parser, so no consumer could recover it. `alt?: string` now captured from markdown images, media-link labels and HTML `alt=` (order-independent), and carried into the tile name, the lightbox dialog label and its ``. ABSENT when unwritten, never `""` — `alt=""` claims 'decorative', which is the opposite of 'unknown'. Measured on the audit's own note: tile `"Open image"` → `"Open image: f1r — a related folio"`. Three pre-existing assertions encoded the lossy shape and were updated; 6 new tests, red-green confirmed. Gates: 1118 render-core + 136 viewer tests, svelte-check 1464/0/0, studio typecheck clean; Chromium 5/5. - [Gallery parity with Studio's redesigned LibraryHome](Archie-a897) — V6/V7/V20/V21 fixed, branch `fix/gallery-parity` (`2da06cb`), NOT yet merged. V6 is the map's thesis case and it held: Studio's W7 rule (lens browses, search finds everything — Archie-2308) ported to the read side, both counted groups render regardless of lens, lens hides while searching. V7's stated cause was the SMALLER half — the card's cover was declared AND on disk; tree-relative refs were rendered raw and 404'd against the page (new `publishedAssetUrl`); the missing Studio-style cover fallback was real too (`coverFallbacks`) but could not have fixed the seeded card alone, since that exhibit has 21 index entries and zero thumbnails. V20/V21 were MISFILED by me at graduation (they are ObjectGrid, not Gallery) — done here anyway: default density was the one showing fewest, and the selected toggle was the only accent fill on an exhibit's front page. **V8 is an OVERCLAIM and was not fixed**: the lens toggle tracks whether a tree carries `images.json` (ADR-0023 degradation, stated at Gallery.svelte:6), not the data mode — the audit compared two libraries and blamed the wrong variable. V11/V31 scoped out (embed = contested territory); V11 is plausibly the portable twin of the V7 path bug. Gates: 144 viewer tests, svelte-check 1464/0/0; Chromium 7/7. - MERGE WAVE 1 (2026-07-25): all three read-surface fixes merged to `main` — audit ledgers `ae4bd8d`, arrival `e513823`, note alt-text `b6a514e`, gallery parity `e725c2d`. HAZARD CAUGHT AT MERGE TIME: `fix/arrival-recoverable` was 5 commits ahead of main, and THREE of them belonged to a concurrent session (studio DZI perf, render-core head-index, an archie-viewer dist rebuild, plus a `.claude/rules/tauri-csp.md` edit) — the branch was cut from a local HEAD that was ahead of `main`, and merging it as-is would have dragged their in-flight perf work into main behind a UX commit message. Resolved by cherry-picking only my two commits onto main in a dedicated `merge-main` worktree, so the other session's checkout was never touched. LESSON for this map's territory rule: when the primary tree is on someone else's branch, cut from `main` by name, never from `HEAD`. Post-merge gates all green: svelte-check 1464/0/0, viewer 144 + render-core 1118 + studio 919 = 2181 tests, studio typecheck clean, astro check 0/0/0, and a combined Chromium drive of all three fixes coexisting 7/7 with zero page errors. - [Read-surface a11y sweep](Archie-c831) — V63/V61/V62/V27/V28 fixed, merged `cc83768`. ReadingSheet claimed `aria-modal` and implemented none of it while the shared `use:dialog` action sat one import away; the note card had no role, name or focus behaviour (deliberately made a named REGION, not a modal — it floats beside a usable canvas); the filmstrip's twelve tab stops got the roving tabindex this repo ratified for that exact component in `Archie-f260`. V45/V90/V25/V26 deferred to `Archie-ed50` (they are canvas-focus-ownership questions) and V42 to `Archie-9a81`. Chromium 10/10 asserting behaviour, not attributes. - [The published tree's public face](Archie-c405) — V107/V108/V110 fixed, merged `3c82bfc`. The crawler's page went from **31 to 752 characters** of body text (static summary + real object list, dropped on hydration by a MutationObserver); the ADR-0014 archival page gained the narrative it had never had (`grep -n sections` returned nothing — 13,491 chars of notes and zero of the six sections' prose); the app page now links to its archival twin. **V109 is largely an OVERCLAIM**: robots.txt advertises the DERIVED sitemap, which enumerates 7 of 7 — the stale 2-of-7 file is a seed artifact robots never points at. V103/V104 deferred to the Dublin Core map, which owns rights display. - [Chrome occlusion sweep](Archie-9a81) — V40/V80 + the Archie-4635 follow-up fixed, merged. **V40 and V80 were ONE bug in two components** — the sweep framing found that; a per-finding fix would have missed it. Both anchored 'canvas chrome' to the flex ROW holding canvas AND text column, so `right:` measured from the sidebar's edge: the zoom cue rendered at x=1188 in a 924px canvas (264px inside the aside, on the object title), the narrative's chrome at x=1045 in an 860px canvas (on the spine). Moving each inside its own `
` is the whole fix. The degrade notice moved to bottom-right on the gallery — right-aligning only moved the collision, since a 640px title leaves no safe top anchor. V22/V87/V48/V71 deferred as placement DECISIONS (floating-by-design, not container bugs) that belong with `Archie-ed50`; V55 is embed territory. - [Copy pass on the read surface](Archie-f08e) — V91/V86 fixed, merged. Four labels for two places became one vocabulary ("All items" ⇄ "Back to the reading", matching the destination's own "ITEMS"), with CONTEXT.md's Exhibit definition as the authority rather than a new coinage; the spine label's separator moved into CSS because the markup space was being trimmed at COMPILE time, and the division name is no longer said twice in one line. V23/V60/V64/V65 deferred — each is a design question wearing copy's clothes (which surface owns "what am I looking at", what each card should CONTAIN, what the stepper should step) and belongs with `Archie-ed50`. - MERGE WAVE 2 (2026-07-25): main PUSHED — 29 commits that had never seen CI, plus the viewer browser gate. CI came back 8/9: gh-pages-build and embed-smoke, the two jobs my local gates could not run, both PASSED; the one failure was archie-viewer-artifact, a root dist/ mirror left un-resynced by the concurrent session's dist rebuild (fixed, 65a9175). TWO ARTIFACTS WERE NEVER REGENERATED, and the unit tests could not tell: V110's sections block was merged in 3c82bfc with a passing unit test, but grep -c "The narrative" over the shipped dist/published/screenshots/index.html returned **0** until the tree was rebuilt (716cf39, +106 lines of narrative prose). The function was proven; the output was not. Same epistemic shape as the unbound-prop bug, one layer out. - [The viewer gets a browser gate](apps/viewer/e2e) — 17 specs, wired into CI's e2e job. Closes the audit's largest durable gap: every behavioural assertion from seven fix tickets was an ad-hoc script, written and thrown away, while apps/studio/e2e existed with its own CI job. PROVEN RED-GREEN, not merely green: reverting the oncancel destructuring, the grid-density default and the static shell's object list failed exactly the 6 specs that guard them and no others — and with the Cancel button broken, svelte-check still reported **1496 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings**. Serves BUILT output (the static shell is emitted at build time; a dev-server gate could not see it) and aborts every non-localhost request (all seed exhibits are remote-sourced, so this keeps CI off third-party uptime AND proves grid/filmstrip/chrome render from the local manifest). apps/viewer/vitest.config.ts was required, not incidental: vitest's default **/*.spec.* sweeps up Playwright specs and fails all four at collection. - [How the canvas shows what is selected](Archie-ed50) — DECIDED: a contrasting HALO (reading colour keeps "which reading", the halo answers "which one"), deliberately distinct from hover; plus a 0.15 breathing-room margin in fitBoundsRect. Rejected spotlight/dim-the-rest (it fights the COMPARING outline-only regime) and reusing `highlighted` (collapses hover and selection into one look). The mechanism finding is the load-bearing one: NEITHER consumer's style channel can express two strokes — MarkerStyle is a single fill/stroke and Annotorious 3 has no per-shape SVG node — so the halo is an OSD **overlay element** in @render/mount, modelled on the existing FrameOverlay, which satisfies "expressible in the poorer renderer" by construction. The embed already sets `data-selected` (read-overlay.ts:253) and NOTHING in the repo styles it: the hook was built and never painted. Graduated into [Archie-52a0]; the 13 findings parked behind this ticket across three sessions turned out to be three unrelated clusters, now [Archie-40fe] (occlusion), [Archie-3d55] (canvas keyboard) and [Archie-c982] (where a note lives). - [Paint the selected mark](Archie-52a0) — SHIPPED 36ce001. Halo is a THIRD OSD overlay layer drawn identically by both renderers (three strokes: shadow / contrast ink by WCAG luminance / the mark colour, so the ring never SPENDS reading identity to answer "which one"). Prior art decisive: annomea viewer.ts:161 swaps the selected mark to a fixed accent — right there, wrong here. Also V44 fit margin 0.15 applied BEFORE the sidebar reservation, V47 legend swatch drawn from the same readingMarkerStyle call the canvas uses, V41 frame dashed vs solid region mark (with a separate solid hit rect — a dash gaps are not hit-testable), V46 frame survives Hide-all. GAP RECORDED: apps/viewer/e2e runs offline and every annotated seed exhibit is remote-sourced, so NO canvas overlay is assertable there; the canvas proof is recipes/smoke.mjs. - [Where a note lives](Archie-c982) — DECIDED: the note has ONE home and the sheet is that home LARGER. Sidebar list = index (locates, never re-reads); NotePopup = the note, the only content renderer; ReadingSheet = a shell (scrim + focus trap) rendering NotePopup at size="sheet"; canvas mark = which one (the halo, which is what REMOVED the pressure that produced the triplication). V64 then dies by construction — one renderer cannot have two headers. Prior art decisive: annomea NarrativePane (ADR-0021) is ONE pane at mini/half/full, and ADR-0007 is explicit that the popup IS the note surface, popup OR drawer, one at a time; Archie had drifted to popup AND drawer AND list. V65 decided separately: the stepper LEAVES the note card — it steps objects/sections, never notes, and only migrated there because collapsing the aside took the real nav with it; object/section nav moves to the canvas chrome, visible in both states, noun spoken visibly. Graduated into [Archie-dbbc] (one note surface) and [Archie-01a6] (nav to the chrome). - [Floating chrome covers what the reader came to look at](Archie-40fe) — SHIPPED 75bc949. The bottom band had NO source of truth: --topbar-h exists so top-escaping surfaces clear it identically, and nothing mirrored it, so the finder pill and note card were pinned INSIDE the filmstrip. Added --strip-h (published LIVE by Filmstrip — the band collapses to a handle, so a static token is wrong in one state) + --finder-h. V87 got WORSE when the pill was lifted for V22, so the spine reserves the whole footprint. V48 is the CAMERA half: fitBoundsRect now reserves BOTH flanks, capping the TOTAL. DISCOVERY: getFitOptions, the reservation seam, had existed since the anvil delamination and the viewer NEVER PASSED IT — every fit ran on PLAIN_FIT. - [The canvas is reachable, nameable and escapable](Archie-3d55) — SHIPPED d917a40. V90 needed OPPOSITE fixes for its two stops: the OSD canvas IS a control (name it, and say which keys it owns — that is V25 too), Annotorious layer is NOT (WebGL, no focusable shape; it leaves the tab order). V45 DECIDED: the consumers cannot share a mechanism (no per-shape node to focus is a fact, not a preference) so they share the GUARANTEE — every note reachable and named — shell via the notes list, embed via ONE roving tab stop instead of N. V26: Escape is a ladder, smallest rung first. Canvas assertions are NOT in e2e (offline a failed mount tears its own canvas out of the DOM); driven online by hand. - [The address grammar and taking something away](Archie-d5cd) — DECIDED, and the headline is a REFRAME: V100 was never a grammar problem. route.ts parses every frozen rung correctly and buildNoteDeepLink already builds #/a/; the RESOLVER compares a URL ULID against the whole published IRI. No ADR-0021 change, no new id form. Then: the address bar WRITES every rung it already reads (replaceState), which is what makes copy-a-link truthful and what unblocks V84 and V52 (working code no address could reach). And taking away = THREE GRAINS AT EQUAL WEIGHT — link, formatted citation (quire donor: CSL-JSON→MLA/Chicago), IIIF Content State (codec already exists UNUSED in deeplink.ts) — as a DIALOG, not new floating chrome, or it re-opens V48 the week after it closed. Archie-33bf STAYS on the Studio map and takes V100/V101/V24 as input. Graduated into [Archie-67b6], [Archie-99b1], [Archie-3ea1]. - [What fidelity the embed owes the shell](Archie-52a9) — DECIDED. The reframe: parity and the weight budget are BARELY OPPOSED. ADR-0019 budgets eagerGzKB (32.9, ratcheted), and every missing capability is lazy behind the boundary reader.ts already uses — rights ~0KB (the manifest already carries requiredStatement), nav ~1KB, note list ~2KB, readings ~2KB, narrative ~8KB and only for exhibits WITH sections. ADR-0019 sanctions dropping PixiJS, not dropping function. So: parity by default; V105 rights NON-NEGOTIABLE (legal). Enforcement = a capability CONTRACT in ADR-0019 using annomea EMBED-AUDIT vocabulary (PORT/ADAPT/DROP-justified/DEFER-tracked/ABSENT) + smoke asserting every MUST row — capability-driven precisely because annomea proved a FILE-driven audit makes a missing capability invisible by construction, which is how Archie lost readings/nav/rights/narrative with every test green. Rejected a shared component layer (embed is framework-free by design, shell is Svelte). Shared tokens, not duplicated CSS. Graduated into [Archie-b681], [Archie-f90d], [Archie-c314]. - [What the narrative mode promises](Archie-e902) — DECIDED: exactly what its copy already claims — read down the page, the image follows along. Scroll-coupled, BOTH directions. Reachable now, which the ticket did not assume: all beats are already rendered in one scrollable column (scrollHeight 2255 vs clientHeight 720, six
  • each with its own prose), so the mode is ONE observer away from its premise. Mechanism: IntersectionObserver over the beats → activeIndex → the existing fitRegion path; prior art exact and in-corpus (scrollama, built on IntersectionObserver in favor of scroll events). V82 is the SAME coupling backwards — activation must also scroll the prose, so both halves arrive whichever door the reader came in by. Rejected beat-stepped and fix-the-copy: both honest, both abandon the interaction that makes narrative a MODE rather than a styled list. The copy was not wrong; the code was missing. Graduated into [Archie-0d6c], [Archie-c5cb]. - [One note surface: NotePopup is the note, the sheet is it at a larger size](Archie-dbbc) — merged `273bea7`. Expanding a note then clicking a tag chip put TWO `aria-modal` dialogs on screen; the old sheet also took only `text`, so media and tags vanished on expand. One rule replaces three judgements: an affordance is withheld at sheet size only when it is MEANINGLESS there (the expand glyph offers to expand what is already expanded); everything else is kept, and anything modal it opens REPLACES the sheet. Follow-up Archie-0cc6 — the `onmedia` half is correct but unfalsifiable, since no fixture note is both expandable and media-bearing. - [Object/section nav belongs in the canvas chrome, not inside a note card](Archie-01a6) — merged `273bea7`. `stepIntoReading` existed only because the stepper lived INSIDE the note card and stepping had to keep it mounted under the reader's cursor — machinery, not a reading feature; moving nav to chrome dissolved its justification. MediaPlayer deliberately keeps the sidebar stepper (an AV object has no canvas chrome) and is byte-identical to base. Follow-ups: Archie-5185 (flip-and-read vanished as an unasked-for consequence — recorded as a decision, with the one test to invert) and Archie-d6e9. ## Fog - **What each decision's implementation looks like.** Meta-planning: graduates into impl tickets as `Archie-52a9` / `d5cd` / `ed50` / `e902` close. Deliberately unwritten — the Studio map's pattern was decision-then-impl-ticket, and inventing the impl before the decision inverts it. - **Whether the Studio side needs the mirror of any of this.** `route.ts` and `marker-style.ts` are shared, so two of the four decisions can propagate INTO Studio — the reverse direction from the one `Archie-7aef` refused. That's a real question and it can't be phrased sharply until the decisions land. - **V54 — not one polygon region exists in the whole corpus**, so `SvgSelector` handling in BOTH overlays (Annotorious in the shell, DOM-SVG in the embed) is content-untested. ADR-0019 explicitly requires the embed overlay to reproduce *both* `xywh` Fragment AND `SvgSelector` polygon regions. This is a fixture / showroom gap, not a UX defect: the fix is authoring a polygon into the seed so the path is exercised at all. Belongs with whoever owns the showroom corpus (`ledgers/SHOWROOM.md`). - **V12 — arrival states nothing about what the collection is or who assembled it.** Recorded in the ledger as judgment rather than defect, and left here on purpose: the library-level description field may simply be unset in the seed, so it needs verifying against a library that sets one before anyone designs an orientation surface. If it turns out the field exists and is rendered, this patch dissolves. - **Whether the read surface's a11y subset folds into `Archie-eec7`** (screen-reader walk, open-backlog map) or eec7 narrows to Studio. Named in `Archie-c831`'s body as a resolution-time call; kept here so it isn't lost if that ticket is reshaped.

title: Audit vertical 1 — Arrival
description:
## Question

What does a first-time visitor meet in the first ten seconds, across every way of arriving, and where
does it fail them?

## Surfaces

`apps/viewer/src/pages/index.astro`, `ViewerShell.svelte` (427 lines — the shell that auto-detects its
data mode), `EmptyHall.svelte` (the portable drop screen), `Gallery.svelte`. On the embed side: `src=`
boot, the no-`src` local-drop screen, and `offline` (ADR-0019's attribute set, frozen by ADR-0021).

## Also in scope for this vertical specifically

- **Degrade-upward messaging.** ADR-0021 mandates that an unresolvable `target` degrades upward and
  NEVER errors — missing note → its exhibit, missing exhibit → the gallery. What the reader is TOLD
  when that happens is unspecified, and silent redirection is its own usability problem.
- **Failure states.** TEND-EXPLORE I-V2: a corrupt deployment surfaces to the reader as "check your
  connection" — a wrong diagnosis pointing at the wrong fixer.

## Question

reach, and how far do the shell and the embed diverge?

in ways that change what the reader can DO — hit-testing, `fitBounds`-on-select (the ADR-0006 nav
contract), marker labels, both `xywh` Fragment and `SvgSelector` polygon regions.

  `apps/studio/src/App.svelte:1482` and `apps/viewer/src/components/ExhibitView.svelte:277`. Fixing it
  lands on both apps at once. It is not a viewer-parity question.
- `ReadingLegend`'s swatch+name pairing ALREADY satisfies 1.4.1 (`a11y-interactions.md:102-104`), and
  `:128-129` says explicitly: don't touch it.
- The embed overlay keyboard/AT dead end is CLOSED (Archie-9413, merged `4178a7b`) —
  `read-overlay.ts:184-191` sets `role`, `aria-label`, `tabindex="0"` and a keydown handler.

## AV

ADR-0021 requires `t=` to seek PAUSED at an offset and must not reuse the play-coupled `seekTo`.
Whether that reads correctly to a visitor is this vertical's call.

Findings file: `ledgers/UX-AUDIT-viewer-read-object.md`. Reserved finding numbers: **V40–V59**.

(2) The legend's 2/1/1/1 counts against 'Notes . 2' is not a contradiction -- counts are additive per layer, measured 2->3 on selecting Cipher. (3) The dark icon pill at the bottom of every canvas screenshot is Astro's dev toolbar, not clipped OSD controls. (4) The exclusive-radio legend is ratified (archie-ux Q-2). (5) The Rosettes note's leaked authoring prose is a seed-content issue, not a UX defect. title: Decide: what fidelity does the embed owe the shell, and how is it enforced?
description:
## Question

The audit's clearest pattern: the embed did not lose polish, it lost FUNCTION. What does
`<archie-viewer>` owe the shell, and what mechanism keeps it owing it?

## What the audit measured (all re-verified 2026-07-25 against dist mtime 19:52:37 — no verdict flipped)

- **V30** no way to move between objects AT ALL — confirmed on a 12-object exhibit, not just a
  single-object one. The object view's complete visible control set is `["← The Whole Manuscript"]`.
- **V56** readings dropped entirely — three readings in the library, zero coloured marks, no legend.
- **V70** no note list, so the (near-invisible, V69) marker is the only door to a note.
- **V88** the narrative dropped — `voynich-reading` renders 12 thumbnails, zero prose, no sections, no spine.
- **V105** no attribution, licence or metadata at gallery OR object level, against a published tree
  whose manifests DO carry `requiredStatement` (the shell shows it on the same object). This is legal
  exposure, not a gap.
- **V9 / V31 / V69** the visual divergence vertical 1 first saw: white + system-ui + orange + square
  cards + a 1.5px near-black hairline marker, against the shell's green atmosphere, display face and
  reading colours.

## Why this is a decision and not a bug list

ADR-0019 says "a thin shell over the SAME `@render/core` — one engine, not a fork", and the divergence
it SANCTIONS is precise: Annotorious/PixiJS dropped for a geometry-only DOM-SVG overlay, to shed
~194 KB gz and the `unsafe-eval` grant. Nothing in it sanctions dropping readings, navigation or
rights. `element.ts:9-10` records the mechanism of the drift — the markup was **ported, not imported**.

So the question is two questions:
1. **Scope.** Which of the shell's capabilities are part of the embed's contract? (Rights and
   attribution are the strongest candidate for "non-negotiable" — an embed that strips a required
   statement is worse than no embed.) Weigh each against ADR-0019's weight budget: the embed's whole
   reason to exist is a ~5–15 KB gz eager core.
2. **Enforcement.** Today parity is convention only, which is why ported markup drifts silently. Is
   the answer a shared component layer, a conformance test, a CI gate, or an explicit written
   non-goal per capability? Graduated from this map's Fog, where it was the "cross-consumer fidelity
   policy" patch.

The related structural question — whether the viewer should consume shared tokens or whether the
duplicated `markers.css`/`tokens.css`/`atmosphere.css` copies are the right boundary for an
independently-versioned embed — is in scope here, since it is the same "what is shared" call.

## Prior art to consult first

`clover-iiif` and `canvas-panel` both ship this exact shape (ADR-0019 cites them); `anvil` ADR-0006
("Web Component + iframe, nothing else"); `annomea`'s `EMBED-AUDIT.md`, which is the cautionary tale
ADR-0019 was written against.

## Follow-on tickets (filed)

- Archie-b681 — Embed ships rights, attribution and licence (V105) — LEGAL, ship first
- Archie-f90d — ADR-0019 gains a capability contract, and smoke enforces it
- Archie-c314 — Embed parity: object nav, note list, readings, narrative, shared tokens

Order: b681 first (legal); f90d before or with c314, so each capability is asserted as it arrives.
closeReason:
DECIDED. The reframe that settles the scope question: PARITY AND THE WEIGHT BUDGET ARE BARELY OPPOSED. ADR-0019's budget is enforced on eagerGzKB (32.9 today, ratcheted by build.mjs --check), and EVERY capability the audit found missing is lazy-loadable behind the boundary reader.ts already uses. Measured shape: rights ~0KB (the manifest already carries requiredStatement — the shell renders it from the same bytes), nav ~1KB, note list ~2KB, readings+legend ~2KB, narrative ~8KB and only for exhibits that HAVE sections. None of it lands in the eager path. So the trade the ticket assumed — function vs weight — mostly is not one, and ADR-0019 sanctions dropping PixiJS, not dropping function.

SCOPE: parity by default for every READING capability. V105 (rights/attribution/licence) is NON-NEGOTIABLE and separately urgent — an embed that strips a required statement from a manifest that carries one is legal exposure, not a gap. V30 (object nav), V70 (note list), V56 (readings + legend), V88 (narrative) and V9/V31/V69 (the visual language — SHARED tokens, not copied ones) all follow.

ENFORCEMENT: a capability CONTRACT plus a CI conformance drive. Prior art is decisive and doubly so: annomea's EMBED-AUDIT.md is both the cautionary tale AND the instrument. Its Channel-3 Web Component 'evaporated silently' because the prior audit was FILE-driven and annomea had no embed/ directory — every anvil embed file 'had zero counterpart to compare against and was invisible by construction'. That is exactly how Archie's embed lost readings, nav, rights and the narrative while every test stayed green. The fix is annomea's own answer: a per-capability verdict table (PORT / ADAPT / DROP-justified / DEFER-tracked / ABSENT) written into ADR-0019 as the contract, with each MUST row asserted by recipes/smoke.mjs against the BUILT bundle. Capability-driven, so a missing capability cannot go invisible the way a missing file did. A new DROP row becomes a deliberate, reviewable act.

Rejected: a shared framework-free component layer. It is the strongest guarantee and the wrong cost here — the embed is framework-free BY DESIGN (ADR-0019) and the shell is Svelte, so it means either shipping a framework in the embed or rewriting the shell's UI. The contract+gate gets most of the guarantee for none of that.

Also in scope and now decided: the duplicated markers.css / tokens.css / atmosphere.css copies are NOT the right boundary. Shared tokens, because V9/V31/V69 are precisely the drift that duplication produced.

Graduated into: Archie-<rights> (V105, ship first — legal), Archie-<contract> (the ADR-0019 table + smoke gate), Archie-<parity> (nav, note list, readings, narrative).

title: Decide: the address grammar and the act of taking something away
description:
## Question

A reader found something worth keeping. What can they address, and how do they take it with them?

## What the audit measured

- **V100** the note rung of the cite ladder is **UNSATISFIABLE**. Independently verified twice: all
  144 published note ids are multi-segment IRIs; `route.ts:42-44` takes exactly one segment from
  `path.split("/")`; `note-arrival.ts:29,33` matches by exact string equality; there is no
  `decodeURIComponent` on that segment. Five spellings of a REAL id were driven (last segment, bare
  ULID, `ULID/v1`, percent-encoded IRI, raw IRI) — every one lands on the degrade path. No string
  satisfies the rung. ADR-0021 froze this ladder as public API.
- **V102** there is **no way to copy anything** — zero clipboard or share affordances in the entire
  read surface. For a tool whose purpose is citable annotation, this is the headline finding of the
  whole audit.
- **V101** five distinct reader states share one URL; the address bar stops at the exhibit.
- **V52** ADR-0021's `t=` landing seek (seek PAUSED at an offset, deliberately not the play-coupled
  `seekTo`) is correctly built and **structurally unreachable** — working code no address can reach.
- **V106** the finder returns text with no address, no locus and no count.
- **V84** the narrative's section index has no address at all, so stepping out and back loses your place.

## The shape of the decision

These are one question, not six. The ladder (CONTEXT §244: Exhibit / Object / Note / region / Section)
is frozen as public API by ADR-0021 — so the fix is constrained: a note id form that survives a
`/`-delimited grammar, chosen without breaking addresses already in the wild (though V100 proves NO
note address has ever resolved, which is unusual latitude — nothing to break on that rung).

Then: what is the ACT of taking something away? A copy-link button, a formatted citation, an
IIIF Content State export (ADR-0022; the codec already exists in `@render/core` `deeplink.ts`), or all
three at different grains.

## Cross-map coordination — settle this explicitly

`Archie-33bf` "Published-site deep links: should viewer URLs mirror Studio place grammar?" sits on the
**Studio UX overhaul** map (`Archie-21b1`) and owns the URL-grammar decision. Vertical 6 audited the
reader's experience without pre-empting it. Part of this ticket's job is to decide whether 33bf moves
under this map or stays and takes V100/V101 as input. Do not fork the decision across two tickets.

Also note `packages/render-core/src/url/route.ts` is the SINGLE definition of the grammar and predates
`apps/studio/src/place.ts`, which mirrors it (`place.ts:27-31`) — a change here propagates to Studio.

## Prior art

`quire` and `juncture` are the on-point donors for scholarly citation and static publishing;
`canvases-annotations-sharing` for the IIIF Content State route.

## Also carried by this decision

- **V24 (HIGH)** — the viewer **reads an object address it never writes**. It will honour
  `#/{slug}/o/{id}` on arrival but never puts that address in the bar, so the rung exists for inbound
  links and is invisible to the reader who might share one. Same shape as V101 (five reader states,
  one URL): the grammar is richer than the address bar admits. Decide the write side and the read side
  together, or the ladder stays half-real.


## Follow-on tickets (filed)

- Archie-67b6 — The note rung resolves: match by logicalId, not by full IRI (V100)
- Archie-99b1 — The address bar writes every rung the grammar already reads (V101, V24, V84, V52)
- Archie-3ea1 — Cite panel: link, citation, IIIF Content State at equal weight (V102, V106)

Order: 67b6 → 99b1 → 3ea1. Each depends on the one before being TRUE, not merely merged.
closeReason:
DECIDED, and the headline is a reframe: V100 IS NOT A GRAMMAR PROBLEM. route.ts already parses every rung of the frozen ladder correctly (/o/, /a/, /s/, ?xywh, ?t), buildNoteDeepLink already builds '#/a/<logicalId>', and brand.ts already owns the logicalId/versionId split. What is broken is the RESOLVER: published note ids are '{base}{slug}/annotations/{ULID}/v{n}' and resolveNoteArrival (note-arrival.ts:29,33) compares the URL's single segment to that WHOLE IRI with ===. So the ladder was right the entire time and the comparison was wrong. No ADR-0021 change, no new id form, no encoding scheme. Verified: all 51 voynich note ids are multi-segment IRIs of exactly that shape; the ULID is one segment and URL-safe by construction.

THREE DECISIONS:

1. THE ADDRESS BAR WRITES EVERY RUNG IT ALREADY READS. The viewer honours /o/, /a/, /s/, ?xywh and ?t inbound and writes NONE of them (V24: reads an address it never writes; V101: five reader states, one URL). It now tracks the deepest rung currently open, via replaceState so back-history stays clean. This is what makes copy-a-link truthful rather than a second, parallel implementation of 'where am I', and it is what unblocks V84 (the section index had no address, so stepping out and back lost your place) and V52 (ADR-0021's t= landing seek is correctly built and structurally unreachable — working code no address can reach).

2. TAKING SOMETHING AWAY = THREE GRAINS, EQUAL WEIGHT. A cite panel offering Link, formatted Citation, and IIIF Content State side by side. Not a menu behind a copy button — the three are for different readers and hiding two of them under a default answers only the easiest case. For a tool whose stated purpose is citable annotation, zero clipboard affordances anywhere in the read surface (V102) is the audit's headline finding; the reply should be proportionate. Prior art: quire renders CSL-JSON into MLA/Chicago (packages/11ty/_includes/components/citation) — that is the citation grain's donor; the Content State codec ALREADY EXISTS unused in render-core deeplink.ts (encodeContentState/decodeContentState, ADR-0022).

   CONSTRAINT CARRIED FORWARD: Archie-40fe just spent a ticket clearing floating chrome off the canvas. The cite panel must be a DIALOG (the ReadingSheet/use:dialog shape — scrim, focus trap, Escape), not a new persistent floating surface, or it re-opens V48/V22 the week after they closed.

3. ARCHIE-33BF STAYS ON THE STUDIO MAP (Archie-21b1) and takes V100/V101/V24 as measured input. Since this ticket changes NO grammar — route.ts is untouched — there is nothing here that pre-empts its actual question, which is Studio<->viewer place-grammar symmetry. Not forked: d5cd owns what you can copy and what the bar says; 33bf owns whether the two grammars are one.

Graduated into: Archie-<fix> (resolver), Archie-<addr> (address writing), Archie-<cite> (the panel).

title: Decide: how the canvas shows the reader what is selected
description:
## Question

At the moment of closest looking, what does the canvas do to show the reader what they selected?

## What the audit measured

- **V44** selection has **no on-canvas representation, in EITHER consumer**. You select a note and the
  image does not show you what you selected.
- **V43** select-to-zoom fits the region edge-to-edge, so the selected thing leaves the frame at the
  exact moment the reader asked to look closer. ADR-0006's `fitBounds`-on-select nav contract is
  honoured literally and defeated in effect.
- **V47** the legend's General-notes swatch is not the colour the canvas paints General notes with —
  the legend and the marks disagree.
- **V41** two nested green rectangles at fit-width mean two different things and look identical.
- **V46** "Hide all" also removes the whole-object frame, which is the canvas's only named tab stop —
  a declutter control that silently removes keyboard access.

## Why this is a decision

V43 and V44 pull in opposite directions: the camera answer (how tightly to fit) and the mark answer
(what persists on the image to say "this one"). Fixing either alone can make the other worse — fit
looser and the mark matters more; add a persistent selected-mark and the fit can stay tight. They must
be decided together.

## Constraints that bound the answer

- The mark must work in BOTH overlay implementations — Annotorious/PixiJS in the shell, the
  geometry-only DOM-SVG `read-overlay.ts` in the embed. Whatever is decided has to be expressible in
  the poorer of the two (ADR-0019).
- **Do not** re-open the colour-independent-coding question: the on-canvas marker's colour-only coding
  is a real WCAG 1.4.1 gap, but it lives in SHARED code
  (`packages/render-core/src/query/marker-style.ts` `readingMarkerStyle`, called by
  `App.svelte:1482` AND `ExhibitView.svelte:277`), so it is not viewer-specific and its recommended
  pattern is already written in `docs/research/a11y-interactions.md:117-133`. Consume that, don't redo it.
- `ReadingLegend`'s swatch+name pairing already satisfies 1.4.1 — `a11y-interactions.md:128-129` says
  don't touch it. V47 is about the swatch being the WRONG colour, not about adding one.
closeReason:
DECIDED: selection is a CONTRASTING HALO around the selected mark, and the camera
leaves the selected region breathing room.

## The mark (V44)

The selected annotation keeps its reading colour and gains a second, outer ring in a
neutral contrast (white or near-black, chosen by the mark colour's luminance). Hue
still answers "which reading"; the halo answers "which ONE". Deliberately distinct
from hover, which keeps the existing `highlighted` treatment — the two states must not
collapse into one look, or moving the pointer over the list makes marks flicker
between two meanings.

Rejected: reusing `highlighted` for selection (cheapest, but conflates hover and
selection); spotlight/dim-the-rest (strongest signal, but it fights the COMPARING
regime — 2+ readings visible is deliberately outline-only so no fill can lie about
identity — and rewrites the whole canvas on every click).

## The mechanism — an overlay element, NOT a marker style

Measured while deciding: NEITHER consumer's style channel can express two strokes.
`MarkerStyle` (render-mount/src/surface.ts:16-22) is a single fill/stroke/width, and
Annotorious 3 paints to a WebGL canvas with no per-shape SVG node (the same fact that
made the old `.a9s-annotation` CSS match zero elements for a month).

But both consumers run OSD and both already call `viewer.addOverlay` — the embed's
DOM-SVG overlay does it per shape (read-overlay.ts drawShape), and the shell already
has non-Annotorious overlay precedent in `FrameOverlay` (surface.ts:24-28, the
whole-object coverage border).

So the halo is ONE implementation in @render/mount: an OSD overlay element drawn at
the selected annotation's geometry, above the mark layer. The reading-coloured mark
underneath keeps being painted by whichever renderer owns it — Annotorious in the
shell, the `<polygon>`/`<rect>` in the embed. This satisfies the ticket's binding
constraint by construction: the mark is expressed in the POORER renderer's mechanism,
promoted to both, rather than in a style channel one of them lacks.

The embed already has the state hook — `read-overlay.ts:253` sets `data-selected` on
every shape — and a repo-wide grep finds NO CSS matching it. The hook was built and
never painted; that is the whole of V44 on that side.

## The camera (V43)

`fitBoundsRect` (render-mount/src/fitbounds.ts) returns the annotation's own bbox
verbatim — the ONLY widening in the function is the sidebar reservation. That is why
select-to-zoom puts the selected thing edge-to-edge and its own stroke lands on the
frame boundary.

Fix: inflate the returned box by a margin fraction so the region sits INSIDE the
frame with visible context. Default 0.15 (15% on each axis) unless a drive says
otherwise. Pure function, one call site for both consumers, directly unit-testable —
and with a persistent selected-mark now carrying the "this one" signal, the fit no
longer has to be tight to be legible. This is the half of the ticket that made V43
and V44 inseparable, resolved in the direction the ticket predicted: looser fit,
stronger mark.

## The three that follow mechanically

- V47 — the legend's General-notes swatch must be sourced from the SAME
  `readingMarkerStyle` call the canvas paints with, not a hand-written literal. The
  legend/canvas disagreement is a duplicated constant, not a design question.
- V41 — the two nested green rectangles get disambiguated by the whole-object frame
  adopting a visibly different treatment from a region mark (it is already a distinct
  mechanism — `FrameOverlay` — so this is a paint change, not a structural one).
- V46 — "Hide all" must not remove the whole-object frame, because it is the canvas's
  only named tab stop. Declutter hides REGION marks; the frame is keyboard
  infrastructure, not clutter.

title: Decide: what the narrative reading mode actually promises
description:
## Question

The narrative mode's central promise is unbuilt. What should it promise, and what does that make the
spine?

## What the audit measured

- **V81** "Read down the page … the image follows along" is **NOT IMPLEMENTED**. The mode's stated
  premise, in its own copy, does not happen.
- **V82** a section cite lands the camera but strands the prose off-screen — the two halves of the
  mode do not arrive together.
- **V83** hiding the spine is sticky, global and near-irreversible.
- **V85** the prose column shows one beat at a time and never numbers them.
- **V80** canvas chrome renders on top of the spine (layout, but it shapes what the mode can be).

## Why this is a decision and not a bug

ADR-0016 frames narrative as an **emergent** reading mode, and `docs/IMPLEMENTATION-STRATEGY.md:72`
names the method for Phase 3 invention work: brainstorming first. "The image follows along" is a
scroll-coupled camera — a genuinely invented interaction with real prior art in the corpus
(`scrollama`, `hyperaudio-lite`), several plausible shapes (scroll-driven vs beat-stepped vs
manual-advance), and consequences for V82's arrival behaviour and V85's beat presentation.

Anchors: ADR-0005 (narrative section model), ADR-0016 + its 2026-07-19 amendment (mandatory Overview
supersedes single-emergent auto-open), ADR-0017 (section as supplementing annotation). Also
`Archie-da38` on the Studio map already settled WHERE the narrative is edited (beats authored on
canvas, overview spine read-only) — this is the read-side counterpart, not a re-litigation.

The narrative's addressing problems (V84, the section index has no address) belong to the addressing
decision, not here.

## Follow-on tickets (filed)

- Archie-0d6c — The image follows along: couple the spine and the camera, both directions (V81, V82, V85)
- Archie-c5cb — Hiding the narrative spine is per-exhibit and plainly reversible (V83)

V80 was already fixed by Archie-40fe reservation work — re-measure, do not re-fix.
V84 belongs to the addressing decision (Archie-d5cd) and is filed inside Archie-99b1.
closeReason:
DECIDED: the narrative mode promises exactly what its copy already claims — read down the page, and the image follows along. Scroll-coupled, both directions.

WHY THIS IS REACHABLE, which the ticket did not assume: all beats are ALREADY rendered in one scrollable column (measured — the spine's aside has scrollHeight 2255 against clientHeight 720, with all six <li> present and each carrying its own <div class="prose">). Nothing hides non-active beats. So the mode is one observer away from its own premise; there is no restructuring to do first.

THE MECHANISM: an IntersectionObserver over the beat <li>s drives activeIndex, and the camera follows via the existing fitRegion(section.start) path. Prior art is exact and sits in the corpus: scrollama, which is explicitly built on "IntersectionObserver in favor of scroll events" — the same choice, for the same reason (scroll events fire far more often than the state actually changes). Do not hand-roll scroll math.

AND IN REVERSE — this is V82's fix, not a separate one. A section cite lands the camera but strands the prose off-screen because activation only ever drove one half. Activation must ALSO scroll the prose to its beat. One coupling, two directions: scroll → camera, activate → scroll + camera. That is what makes both halves of the mode arrive together no matter which door the reader came in by.

CONSEQUENCES the implementation must handle, all of them created by the coupling itself:
- Programmatic scroll (from activation) must not re-trigger the observer into a fight with itself. Suppress the observer for the duration of a programmatic scroll, or compare against the intended target.
- V85's beat numbering becomes meaningful once the active beat moves under the reader: number them, so "where am I" has an answer that is not just typographic emphasis.
- V83 (hiding the spine is sticky, global and near-irreversible) gets worse under a scroll-coupled mode, because the spine is now the input device, not just a panel. Hiding it must be per-exhibit and plainly reversible.
- V80 (canvas chrome renders on top of the spine) was already addressed by Archie-40fe's reservation work; re-measure rather than re-fix.

REJECTED: beat-stepped Next/Prev, and keep-manual-advance-and-fix-the-copy. Both are honest, and both abandon the interaction that makes narrative a MODE rather than a styled list — ADR-0016 frames it as emergent, and this is the thing that makes it emerge. The copy was not wrong; the code was missing.

NOT IN SCOPE, by the ticket's own boundary: V84 (the section index has no address) belongs to the addressing decision, Archie-d5cd, and is filed as part of Archie-99b1.

Graduated into: Archie-<scroll> (the coupling, both directions, + numbering) and Archie-<spine> (V83's sticky hide).

title: Fix arrival: give the empty hall an exit, and the slug rung its notice
description:
## Question

Nothing to decide — the fix pattern already exists in this repo. Make arrival recoverable.

## The defects (vertical 1)

- **V1** the empty hall is a one-way door. Reached from the top-right OPEN ANOTHER LIBRARY link, its
  only app control is "Open a library…" (measured in light DOM with `astro-dev-toolbar` filtered).
  Escape is inert. ADR-0008 put that affordance in both modes so a collapse "can't trap the reader" —
  as built, the mitigation IS the trap.
- **V2** browser Back sets the address to `#/{slug}` while the hall stays on screen; only a reload
  recovers. The router does not re-render on `popstate`.
- **V3** the slug rung of degrade-upward is silent, while the object and note rungs both show a
  dismissible notice. One rung not using a component that exists and works.
- **V4** after degrading, the dead address persists on the object/note rungs but IS rewritten on the
  slug rung — two opposite policies in one ladder.
- **V5** "That note isn't here anymore" asserts deletion the system cannot know; the object rung's
  "That item isn't in this exhibit" is accurate about the same failure class. Route through `product-copy`.

## The model to copy — V10

The embed already does this correctly for a failed `src`: *"Couldn't open the library. The link may be
broken or the file unavailable."* — in place, plain language, beside the still-usable recovery control.
Copy that shape inward rather than designing a new one.

Gate after editing: `pnpm --filter @archie/viewer run check:svelte` (baseline 0/0, `--fail-on-warnings`).

## One more degrade case

- **V89** — a bad SECTION cite degrades identically to the others in the shell, but **silently in the
  embed**. Same defect class as V3 (the slug rung's silence), on a different consumer. Fix both here so
  the ladder behaves one way everywhere; the embed's own V10 copy pattern is the model on both sides.
closeReason:
DONE on branch fix/arrival-recoverable (commits 0c55b0f fix + 1b245ff audit ledgers, based off c551367). NOT YET MERGED to main — merge is the user's call.

All five findings fixed and verified by driving the running app in real Chromium: 14/14 assertions, zero page errors. Gates: svelte-check 1465 files / 0 errors / 0 warnings (--fail-on-warnings), 136 viewer tests green.

- V1 — the chooser no longer destroys what it's offering to replace. `openAnother()` used to call closePortableLibrary() + gallery=null + phase="empty" BEFORE showing the hall, so no Cancel could exist even in principle: there was nothing left to return to. Now a separate `choosing` state renders the hall over an intact library, with a "Never mind — keep reading this library" control and Escape (the ratified dismissal contract, Archie-389f). Deferring the teardown is leak-free — openPortableLibrary() already closes the previous fs before adopting a new one.
- V2 — `sync()` only ever assigned `route`, never `phase`. That is precisely why browser Back moved the address while the hall stayed on screen and only a reload reconciled them. It now dismisses the chooser on any navigation.
- V3 — the slug rung now announces itself: "That exhibit isn't in this library — showing the library instead · DISMISS". The notice lives in the SHELL because this rung lands on the Gallery, which ExhibitView never renders; it reuses ExhibitView's `.arrival` idiom so one degrade has one appearance whichever rung produced it.
- V4 — all four rungs normalize the address to the exhibit actually landed on, via history.replaceState rather than `location.hash =`. Two reasons, both load-bearing: assigning the hash fires hashchange, which remounts ExhibitView through the shell's {#key} and would wipe the very notice being raised; and replaceState leaves no history entry, so Back returns where the reader came from instead of bouncing off the dead target.
- V5 — "That note isn't here anymore" asserted a deletion the system cannot know. Now "That note isn't in this exhibit", matching the object/section rungs which were already accurate.

METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING: svelte-check passed 0 errors / 0 warnings against a version where `oncancel` was declared in EmptyHall's prop TYPE but omitted from its destructuring — an unbound identifier in the template, so the Cancel button silently never rendered. Escape worked (shell code), which made it look fine. ONLY the browser drive caught it. This is a second instance of the .claude/rules/svelte-no-typecheck-net.md lesson: the gate is necessary and not sufficient; drive the app.

FOLLOW-UP, deliberately not fixed here: the new notice uses ExhibitView's established top-center `.arrival` placement, and on the Gallery its bottom edge grazes the top of the "Archie Library" title — the same occlusion class as V40/V22/V48. Matching the shipped idiom beat inventing a one-off; placement belongs to the chrome-occlusion sweep Archie-9a81, which owns that class.

title: Fix the embed's dead pointer path on annotation regions
description:
## Question

In the embed, a note opens with the keyboard but not with the mouse. The mechanism is pinned — fix it.

## What is already known (V68, re-verified 2026-07-25, mechanism isolated)

| Attempt | Note card opens |
| --- | --- |
| real `mouse.click` at the region centre (636, 375) | **no** |
| slow press–release (130 ms) on the region's stroke edge | **no** |
| synthetic `click` dispatched on the geometry element | **yes** |
| focus the `svg[role="button"]`, press Enter | **yes**, with focus ring |

- **The listener is fine.** A synthetic click opens the card, so `styleGeometry`'s handler
  (`read-overlay.ts:209-212`) and the whole `emitSelect` → `onSelect` → `noteCard.show` chain work.
- **The defect is hit-testing.** `shadowRoot.elementFromPoint` at the region's own centre returns an
  unnamed `DIV` — something is over the geometry.
- **Nothing happens at all.** OSD's click-to-zoom does not eat it either: region bbox is byte-identical
  after one click and after two (`401×552` → `401×552` → `401×552`, zoom factor 1.000). The click is
  swallowed with ZERO feedback, which is worse than a wrong response.

Related, same surface, likely same sitting: **V69** the marker is `stroke: rgb(42,35,32)`,
`stroke-width: 1.5`, `fill: rgba(0,0,0,0)` — invisible over parchment, and carrying no reading colour.
Whether V69 is fixed here or under the embed-fidelity decision depends on whether reading colours are
in the embed's contract; the bare visibility of a mark is not a fidelity question and can be fixed now.

**Coordinate before starting:** a concurrent session was rewriting `packages/archie-viewer/src/`
(`element.ts`, `index.ts`, `reader.ts`, `reader-guards.ts`) as of 2026-07-24 19:55. Check `git log` and
