the working tree before claiming this file territory.

---

**Correction:** the V11 follow-up filed at resolution is **Archie-84e0** (a placeholder id was written into the close reason by mistake).
closeReason:
FIXED, merged as d973f42. The mechanism was not the listener and not the geometry —
it was OpenSeadragon's own injected wrapper, plus its pointer capture.

## What it actually was

`viewer.addOverlay({element})` does NOT place your element in the DOM. OSD 5.0.1 creates
a plain `<div>` around it (openseadragon.js:19044, `Overlay.elementWrapper`) and sizes THAT
to the overlay's box. It carries no styling, so it sits at the default
`pointer-events: auto` — an opaque rectangle over its whole box.

Both overlay layers were written correctly and both were defeated by it:

- `read-overlay.ts` sets the region `<svg>` to `none` and only the geometry to `all`, so the
  image stays draggable between regions. Each wrapper re-covered its box, so one region's
  wrapper shielded its neighbour's geometry.
- `frame-overlay.ts` sets its border rects to `pointer-events: stroke` SPECIFICALLY so the
  frame's interior stays free for pan/zoom. Its wrapper is sized to the WHOLE object, so it
  blanketed the entire image and every region overlay beneath it. **This was the bigger
  half** — and it explains the audit's most puzzling observation, that OSD's own
  click-to-zoom didn't fire either. The wrapper is not OSD's canvas, so the gesture never
  reached the tracker at all.

A second, independent half: OSD binds a MouseTracker to the canvas/container and takes
POINTER CAPTURE on `pointerdown`. Once captured the sequence is retargeted, so the browser
never dispatches `click` on the geometry — which is exactly why the audit found Enter and a
synthetic `click()` both working while a real mouse click did nothing.

Measured with each half disabled in turn against the built bundle: half 1 alone FAILS,
half 2 alone FAILS, both together work. Neither is redundant.

## Also fixed in the same pass

- **Duplicate ids.** OSD names the wrapper after your element and falls back to the bare
  literal `overlay-wrapper` when it has none (the `else` at :19051) — so every overlay
  shared one id. Now `archie-region-<n>` and `archie-object-frame`.
- **A wrapper leak.** `clear()` called `svg.remove()`, which detaches only OUR element; if
  `removeOverlay` threw, OSD's wrapper stayed behind as an empty div, once per shape, on
  every `setAnnotations`.

## The gate

Three assertions in `recipes/smoke.mjs` (CI's `embed-smoke`), proven red-green — 4/7 with
the fix disabled, 7/7 with it. It has to live there and nowhere cheaper: keyboard Enter and
a synthetic dispatched click BOTH succeed against the broken code, and jsdom has no layout
to hit-test with. Only a driven pointer sequence against the BUILT bundle can see this.

Note the smoke now navigates to `voynich` explicitly: the first gallery card is an exhibit
with **zero notes**, so the check would otherwise pass vacuously — which is how I nearly
mis-read the first drive as "the embed renders no regions at all."

## Not done here

**V69** (mark is `stroke: currentColor` → rgb(42,35,32), 1.5px, invisible over parchment)
deliberately left to [Archie-52a0]. `currentColor` is worse than the audit recorded — it
binds the mark's colour to the HOST PAGE's text colour, so a dark-themed host gets an
invisible mark. But the fix for legibility is a casing/halo, and Archie-ed50 just decided
the halo means SELECTED; adding a permanent casing here would make the selection state
harder to distinguish. Both marks should be painted in one pass, by 52a0.

## Found on the way, unrelated to this ticket

`HTTP 404 /recipes/screenshots/assets/o1-e1-embed.png` — the embed resolved a tree-relative
asset ref against the HOST PAGE's directory rather than the library base. That is V11, the
portable twin of the V7 path bug the gallery ticket fixed, now measured rather than
suspected. Filed as [Archie-72c5].

title: Restore the author's alt text at the model boundary
description:
## Question

An author wrote alt text and the pipeline deletes it. Find the drop site and carry it through.

## The defects (vertical 4)

- **V66** the author's alt text is deleted at the model boundary — authored accessibility content, lost
  in transit. High severity: it is both an a11y failure and silent data loss.
- **V67** every media tile in a note carries the same accessible name (latent today, compounding once
  V66 is fixed).

## Why this is likely a carry-sentinel case

`.claude/rules/render-core-data-integrity.md` §3 documents the mechanism built precisely for this bug
class: every boundary that hand-maps model fields carries a co-located
`satisfies Record<keyof Source, CarryDisposition>` sentinel in `model/carry.ts`, so "added a field,
forgot a copy site" is a compile error rather than a silent drop. The same rule lists prior casualties
of exactly this shape (cover/format/originalName, sections/readings, note-copy emphasis/geo).

So the fix has two halves: carry the field, AND add or correct the sentinel at the boundary that
dropped it — otherwise the next field goes the same way. A deliberate drop must be a NAMED exclusion in
the sentinel, never silence.
closeReason: DONE on branch fix/note-alt-text (commit 91720fe, off main f0cacbf). NOT YET MERGED. ROOT CAUSE, at the model boundary as the finding said: `splitNoteMedia`'s MD_IMAGE regex was `/!\[[^\]]*\]\(\s*([^)\s]+)…\)/` — it MATCHED the author's alt text and captured only the URL, so the description was destroyed during parsing. `NoteMediaItem` was `{ kind, url }`, so no consumer could recover it however well-written. FIX: `alt?: string` on NoteMediaItem, captured from all three syntaxes — markdown image `![alt](url)`, media-link label `[label](url)` (a link's label IS the author describing it), and HTML `alt=` read off the whole matched tag so attribute ORDER doesn't matter. Carried into NoteMedia's tile name and NoteLightbox's dialog label + ``. Measured on the audit's own note (`published/sampler` embeds `![f1r — a related folio](…)`), the table in the finding is now inverted: tile accessible name "Open image" -> "Open image: f1r — a related folio" lightbox aria-label "Note" -> "Note: f1r — a related folio" lightbox "" -> "f1r — a related folio" V67 ("every media tile carries the same accessible name") falls out with it: names are now per-item, so several tiles in one note are distinguishable. TWO DELIBERATE DECISIONS worth keeping: - `alt` is ABSENT when the author wrote none, never `""`. `alt=""` is a positive claim that an image is DECORATIVE and should be skipped by AT — the opposite of "we don't know". Absence lets each consumer choose its fallback. Whitespace-only counts as nothing written. Tested explicitly. - The tile's inner `` KEEPS `alt=""`. The button wrapping it already carries the name; labelling both would make AT announce the same text twice. The lightbox's `` does take the alt, because there it is the labelled thing. TEST CHANGES, flagged rather than buried: three PRE-EXISTING assertions expected `{kind,url}` for inputs that DO carry alt text (`![a](u1.jpg)`, `[♪ audio](track.mp3)`, `[clip](v.mp4)`) — they encoded the bug, and now expect the carried description. Six new tests cover capture across all three syntaxes, per-item independence, the absent-vs-empty rule, and that a bracketed alt can't break the split. Red-green confirmed: 4 of the 6 failed before the parser change. CARRY-SENTINEL NOTE: `.claude/rules/render-core-data-integrity.md` §3 requires a `satisfies Record` sentinel at boundaries that hand-map MODEL fields. This site is a parser over free-text markdown, not a model mapper, so no sentinel applies — but the bug is the same shape the sentinels exist to prevent, and a reviewer should confirm that judgement rather than take it from me. GATES: render-core 1118 tests, viewer 136 tests, svelte-check 1464 files 0 errors 0 warnings (--fail-on-warnings), apps/studio typecheck clean (render-core is shared, and the added field is optional/additive). Driven in real Chromium: 5/5, zero page errors.

title: Read-surface a11y sweep
description:
## Question

Close the read surface's accessibility defects, and make the claims it already makes true.

## The defects

- **V63** the reading sheet declares `aria-modal="true"` and implements none of it. A false ARIA claim
  is worse than an absent one — assistive tech acts on the assertion. HIGH.
- **V27** the filmstrip is twelve consecutive tab stops, in a repo that ratified roving tabindex for
  this exact component (`Archie-f260`, pattern in `docs/research/a11y-interactions.md`).
- **V61** a note opened from the image is announced to nobody.
- **V45** in the shell an individual region is not keyboard-reachable; in the embed every region is —
  the poorer overlay is the more accessible one.
- **V42** canvas chrome text has no contrast floor: the same breadcrumb measures 5.2:1 and 3.3:1 in one
  screenshot, because it sits over image content.
- **V90** two unnamed tab stops on the canvas (shared code, not narrative-specific).
- **V28** filmstrip frames are unlabelled and, for a manuscript, near-identical.

## Coordination

`Archie-eec7` (screen-reader walk) and `Archie-cf4a` (touch design pass) are open on the open-backlog
map (`Archie-c548`) and cover the whole product. This ticket is the READ surface's evidenced subset —
decide at resolution whether it folds into eec7 or eec7 narrows to Studio. Don't do the work twice.

Do NOT re-open the marker colour-only question: shared render-core code, pattern already specified
(`a11y-interactions.md:117-133`), and `ReadingLegend` is explicitly don't-touch (`:128-129`).

Gate: `pnpm --filter @archie/viewer run check:svelte` — `--fail-on-warnings`, baseline 0/0, so a new
a11y warning fails CI.

## Also in this sweep — the dismissal contract

- **V26** — there is no Escape ladder inside an exhibit.
- **V62** — Escape returns focus to the trigger, but the card's own `×` drops it on the floor.
- **V25** — the keyboard object-step stops working the moment the reader touches the image (focus is
  lost to the canvas and never re-homed).

Studio ratified exactly this contract in `Archie-389f` (single-scrim invariant, strict Esc ladder,
scrim-click = Esc, focus return, no close-confirms) and implemented it in `Archie-5968` behind one
helper. Read that resolution first — the read surface needs the same contract, not a new one, and the
helper may be liftable rather than reimplementable.
closeReason:
DONE for the five findings it could honestly close; four deferred with reasons. Branch fix/read-a11y (dddf6d1), MERGED to main.

FIXED — V63, V61, V62, V27, V28.

- V63 (HIGH) — ReadingSheet declared `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` and implemented NONE of it, while the shared `use:dialog` action — whose own header names "the NoteLightbox and the SearchOverlay" as its users — sat one import away. Now uses the action, and its own window Esc handler was REMOVED because the action owns Esc (keeping both would double-close). Driven: focus moves into the sheet on open, Tab is actually trapped, Escape closes.
- V61/V62 — the note card had no role, no accessible name, no focus behaviour; on the MARKER path activeElement stayed on the canvas, so activating a marker announced nothing, and the `×` dropped focus on document.body while Escape happened to return it. DELIBERATELY NOT MADE A MODAL: the card floats beside a still-usable canvas, so aria-modal + a trap would be a lie in the other direction. It is now a named region that takes programmatic focus ONLY when the trigger was the canvas (the path that was silent), leaving the sidebar keyboard flow untouched, and returns focus on ANY dismissal rather than only the one that worked by accident.
- V27/V28 — the filmstrip was twelve consecutive tab stops. This repo had ALREADY RATIFIED roving tabindex for this exact component (docs/research/a11y-interactions.md; adopted in Studio as Archie-f260) and the viewer never received it — another instance of this map's thesis. One frame is in the tab sequence, and it is the CURRENT object's, so tabbing in lands where the reader actually is rather than at frame one. Arrows + Home/End move between frames. Frames carried only `title`, a tooltip and not an accessible name; each now reads "{label} — item N of M", because for a manuscript the thumbnails are near-identical and position is what orients.

DEFERRED, each for a reason, not for convenience:
- V45 (in the shell an individual region is not keyboard-reachable; in the embed every region is) — making shell regions focusable is a CANVAS SELECTION decision, not a mechanical a11y fix: it changes what a Tab press means on the image and interacts directly with what a selected mark looks like. Belongs with Archie-ed50, which owns exactly that pair.
- V90 (two unnamed tab stops on the canvas) — same surface, same reason, and the ledger already flags it as shared code rather than narrative-specific.
- V25 (keyboard object-step stops working once the reader touches the image) and V26 (no Escape ladder inside an exhibit) — both are focus-ownership questions between OpenSeadragon and the shell. OSD owns the arrow keys for panning (Reader.svelte says so explicitly), so re-homing focus after a canvas interaction needs the same decision as V45/V90. Doing them piecemeal here would have meant guessing the contract twice.
- V42 (canvas chrome text has no contrast floor — the same breadcrumb measures 5.2:1 and 3.3:1 in one screenshot because it sits over image content) — this is a Look fix on chrome that Archie-9a81 (chrome occlusion sweep) is already moving; fixing contrast on elements that ticket may reposition would be work done twice.

RECOMMENDATION: fold V45/V90/V25/V26 into Archie-ed50's implementation once that decision closes, and V42 into Archie-9a81. Neither needs a new ticket.

GATES: viewer 144 tests, svelte-check 1464 files 0 errors 0 warnings (--fail-on-warnings). Driven in real Chromium 10/10, zero page errors — asserting behaviour (Tab actually trapped, ArrowRight/End actually moving) rather than attribute presence. Post-merge on main: svelte-check 1464/0/0, 144 viewer tests.

title: The AV reading surface
description: ## Question Audio and video are first-class objects with a second-class surface. Bring the AV reader up to the image reader. ## The defects (vertical 3) - **V50** the audio object is 860×700 of empty cream with a browser-default scrubber. HIGH — Look is GOAL.md's first priority. - **V49** the AV surface's one novel affordance ships fully covered by the item strip. - **V53** the AV reader drops four affordances the image reader has, with no notice to the reader. - **V29** video is the only object type whose plate can render blank, and its one guard cannot fire. - **V51** paused at 0:00, the first transcript line is already lit as "the line being spoken". ## Scoped OUT of this ticket **V52** — ADR-0021's `t=` landing seek is correctly built and structurally unreachable. The seek implementation is fine; what is missing is an address that can reach it, which belongs to the addressing decision. Don't rebuild the seek; it works. ## Prior art, and it is close at hand `osd-audio-video`, `videojs-annotation` and `hyperaudio-lite` sit beside this repo and are direct donors for the transcript-plus-media reading surface. `wavesurfer.js` is already a dependency — check `mcp__context__get_docs` before hand-rolling a waveform. --- ## Partial progress 2026-07-25 (0cc79ca) — V51 and V29 done, three remain The two DEFECTS are fixed and driven; the three DESIGN items are untouched and are what this ticket now is. **V51 done.** `activeNoteIndex` was correct — it answers 'which range contains t', and a cue starting at 0:00 legitimately contains 0. Added the missing precondition `started` (playback began, or the playhead moved). NOT `!paused`: a `t=` deep-link landing sets currentTime while staying paused, and lighting the line there is right. **V29 done.** `

title: The published tree's public face
description:
## Question

An exhibit's public, archival and machine-readable faces are all thinner than the app's. Fix what the
world outside the SPA can see.

## The defects (vertical 6)

- **V107** the page a crawler is sent to ships **31 characters of body text**. HIGH — this is the reach
  of the entire project.
- **V110** the archival page omits the narrative entirely.
- **V108** every exhibit has two web faces and neither points at the other.
- **V109** the published tree's own sitemap enumerates **2 of its 7** exhibits. This extends
  `ledgers/TEND-EXPLORE-viewer-2026-07-20.md` I-V1 (two disagreeing enumerations of the exhibit
  route-set; third-party exhibits get no page) — read that finding first, it has the diagnosis.
- **V104** the Dublin Core metadata surfaces render nothing, anywhere in the corpus. Cross-reference the
  Dublin Core map (`Archie-c6bf`), which is otherwise complete — this may be its missing read half.

## Anchors

ADR-0014 (self-describing published artifact), ADR-0013 (canonical origin GitHub Pages). `quire` is the
prior-art donor for static scholarly publishing with a real crawlable surface.

## Also here — the rights ladder

- **V103** — the licence ladder is inverted: the OBJECT is licensed, the exhibit is not, and the library
  carries nothing at all. A reader looking for "may I use this" finds the answer at the deepest level
  and nothing at the level they'd actually cite.

This overlaps the Dublin Core map (`Archie-c6bf`), whose `RightsFields` model carries `rights`,
`requiredStatement` and `metadata` at all three levels — so the model supports what the surface doesn't
show. `.claude/rules/metadata-rights-keyed-writebacks.md` is binding if any write-back is touched:
rights patches must be KEYED, never whole-object reconstructions, or they clobber `metadata`.
closeReason:
DONE for V107, V108, V110. V109 is largely an OVERCLAIM. V103/V104 deferred. Branch fix/public-face (3c82bfc), MERGED to main.

V107 (HIGH) — the page a crawler is sent to shipped 31 characters of body text. The reader is `client:only` (OSD touches `document` at import, so there is no SSR path), and while meta/OG/JSON-LD were already rich, the BODY was empty: search engines, link previews, archive crawlers and readers with JS off all saw an empty exhibit. The page now carries a static summary — title, description, and the exhibit's REAL object list read from its published manifest at build time — removed by a MutationObserver once the island has actually mounted (watched, not timed, so a slow bundle can't flash the reader over the fallback or clear it too early). Measured: voynich 31 -> 752, voynich-reading 31 -> 772, geo-map 45 -> 388, sampler 25 -> 457.
  IMPLEMENTATION NOTE worth keeping: the manifests are pulled in with an EAGER VITE GLOB, not a runtime fs read. Astro extracts getStaticPaths into its own prerender chunk, so `readFileSync` there resolves against the wrong root, and module-scope consts are not hoisted into it — the file's own header comment says exactly this about a closed-over `META`. My first two attempts both silently produced EMPTY object lists and the build stayed green; only measuring the built HTML caught it. Same lesson as the svelte-check prop-wiring case: the gate proves the thing compiles, not that it carries what you think.

V110 (HIGH) — `grep -n sections` over static-pages.ts returned NOTHING. The ADR-0014 archival page had no concept of a section, so a narrative exhibit's authored prose never reached the durable artifact: 13,491 characters of body text on the seed and zero of the six sections'. Every note was there; the argument tying them together was not. Sections now LEAD the page (in a narrative exhibit the spine is the reading and the notes are what it cites), each with a deep link on the cite ladder's section rung. Three new render-core tests.

V108 — an exhibit has two web faces. Measured: the archival page ALREADY links to the app page (static-pages.ts renders "Open this exhibit in the interactive viewer"), so "neither points at the other" was half wrong. The missing direction was app -> archival, which meant the durable, no-JS, fully-crawlable copy of an exhibit was unreachable from the face readers actually land on. Added.

V109 — LARGELY AN OVERCLAIM, and not fixed. The finding says the published tree's sitemap enumerates 2 of its 7 exhibits. True of the file `public/published/sitemap.xml` — but `robots.txt` advertises `${CANONICAL_BASE}sitemap.xml`, the DERIVED route (`src/pages/sitemap.xml.ts`), and the built output of that route enumerates SEVEN URLs: the gallery plus all six listed exhibits. So the sitemap crawlers are actually sent is complete. The stale 2-of-7 file is a seed artifact inside the tree, which the ledger itself already attributes to the repo's two seed sources rather than to the generator, and which robots never points at. It would matter only for a published tree deployed standalone — a real scenario, but a different one, and a fix belongs with whoever owns the gen pipeline, not here.

V103 (licence ladder inverted — object licensed, exhibit not, library nothing) and V104 (Dublin Core metadata surfaces render nothing anywhere) — DEFERRED to the Dublin Core map (Archie-c6bf), which owns the RightsFields model at all three levels and has exactly one ticket left. Fixing the display here without that map's decision would guess at which level should carry what.

GATES: render-core 1121 tests, viewer 144, svelte-check 1464/0/0, astro check 0/0/0, viewer build clean. Post-merge on main: svelte-check 1464/0/0.

title: Chrome occlusion sweep: things that ship covering other things
description:
## Question

Seven measured cases where one surface is painted over another. Fix them as one pass — they share a
cause (fixed-position chrome with no layout awareness) more than they share a screen.

## The defects

- **V40** the canvas's zoom readout is painted 264 px INSIDE the notes panel. HIGH.
- **V22** the floating finder pill covers two of the twelve filmstrip frames.
- **V87** the floating finder occludes the last card in the spine.
- **V48** at the moment of closest looking, two cards cover the canvas's left flank.
- **V71** an open note hides half the filmstrip.
- **V55** the embed's note card lands on top of the locator minimap.
- **V80** canvas chrome renders on top of the spine, not on the canvas. HIGH.

## Note on ordering

V80 and V48 touch surfaces the narrative decision may reshape; V40, V22, V55, V71 do not. If the
narrative decision is in flight, do the independent four and say so rather than blocking the sweep.
closeReason:
DONE for V40, V80 and the Archie-4635 follow-up. V22/V87/V48/V71 deferred; V55 out of territory. Branch fix/chrome-occlusion, MERGED to main.

V40 AND V80 TURNED OUT TO BE ONE BUG IN TWO COMPONENTS, which the sweep framing surfaced and a per-finding fix would have missed. Both put "canvas chrome" in a container that was not the canvas: an absolutely-positioned element whose nearest positioned ancestor was the flex ROW holding the canvas AND the text column, so `right:` measured from the sidebar's right edge.
- Reader `.scale-cue` rendered at x=1188 in a 924px canvas — 264px inside the notes aside, on the object title. Its own comment ALREADY claimed "top-right — the one corner this reader's canvas overlays don't already use"; it just wasn't in a container that could give it one.
- NarrativeReader `.canvas-chrome-right` (grid-index escape + zoom cue) rendered at x=1045 in an 860px canvas — on the prose spine.
Moving each inside its own `<main>` is the whole fix; NarrativeReader's `main` also needed `position: relative` (Reader's already had it). Measured after: cue right=904 in canvas right=924; chrome right=840 in canvas right=860. Neither overlaps its text column.

ARCHIE-4635 FOLLOW-UP CLOSED: the slug-rung degrade notice borrowed ExhibitView's top-centre `.arrival` placement and grazed the gallery's display title. Right-aligning only MOVED the collision — the title is 640px wide, so no top anchor is safe at every library-title length. On the gallery the notice now sits bottom-right (genuinely empty; the drift badge owns bottom-centre); in an exhibit the top band stays correct, because there the canvas fills the viewport and bottom-right is the locator minimap.

DEFERRED, and these are NOT the same class as V40/V80:
- V22 (finder pill covers two filmstrip frames) and V87 (finder occludes the last spine card) — the finder pill is deliberately floating over content; its placement is a design tradeoff about which content may be covered, not a container mistake. Fixing it means deciding where a persistent affordance lives, which is worth doing with the canvas-selection decision (Archie-ed50) that is already reshaping this surface.
- V48 (two cards cover the canvas's left flank at closest looking) and V71 (an open note hides half the filmstrip) — same shape: the note card is SUPPOSED to float over the canvas; the complaint is about how much and when. That is a layout decision, not a bug, and it interacts directly with what a selected mark looks like (V43/V44 in Archie-ed50).
- V55 (embed note card lands on the locator minimap) — embed-side; `packages/archie-viewer` is contested territory this cycle per the map's Notes.

METHOD NOTE: the first measurement run showed the fix having NO effect — source correct, live DOM still showing the old parent. The dev server was serving stale modules; a RESTART (not a reload) fixed it, exactly as .claude/rules/viewer-optimizedeps-bare-includes.md documents. Had I trusted the first run I would have concluded the fix was wrong and gone looking for a second cause.

GATES: viewer 144 tests, svelte-check 1464 files 0 errors 0 warnings. Verified by measuring bounding boxes in Chromium, not by eye: 6/6.

title: Gallery parity with Studio's redesigned LibraryHome
description:
## Question

The read gallery kept behaviours Studio's redesign deliberately fixed. Bring across the ones that apply.

## The defects

- **V6** mode-dependent search: the EXHIBITS/ALL IMAGES toggle silently changes what search searches;
  only the placeholder signals it. **This is Studio's W7 verbatim**, fixed there by `Archie-2308`'s
  unified grouped search (lens browses, search finds everything), merged `2c47bdb`, never propagated.
- **V7** no cover fallback: an exhibit without an explicit cover renders title-only — and in the seed it
  sits FIRST, top-left, where the eye lands. Studio does "explicit cover else first object's thumb via
  `readThumbUrl`" (`Archie-2308`; `docs/plans/SCALE-GALLERY-PLAN.md` P3b).
- **V11** the embed's gallery resolves no thumbnails at all from a zip source — possibly the same absent
  fallback, possibly ADR-0010's portable rewrite not covering covers. Diagnose before fixing.
- **V8** the shell's chrome changes with its data mode: portable loses the lens toggle entirely, against
  ADR-0008's one-shell-two-sources contract.
- **V20** the survey surface shows 3 of 12 items, and its default density is the one that shows fewest.
- **V21** the loudest mark on the overview is a viewing preference.
- **V31** the embed's card grid has ragged bottoms; the shell's does not.

## The useful precedent

`Archie-2308` is the Studio decision these mostly mirror; read its resolution on the Studio UX map
before designing anything. This ticket is the clearest instance of the pattern that justified this whole
map — a decision made on one surface, never carried to the other.
closeReason:
DONE on branch fix/gallery-parity (commit 2da06cb, off main f0cacbf). NOT YET MERGED.

FIXED: V6, V7, V20, V21. NOT FIXED, with reasons: V8 (overclaim), V11 + V31 (contested territory).

V6 — the thesis case, and it holds. The lens governed what the search box searched, signalled only by a placeholder swap ("Search exhibits…" / "Search images…"). This is Studio's W7 verbatim; W7 was fixed in Studio by Archie-2308 (merged 2c47bdb) and never carried across. Ported the same rule — the lens BROWSES, the search FINDS EVERYTHING: a live query filters both corpora and renders both counted groups regardless of lens, and the lens hides while a search is live because nothing is left for it to govern. Verified by driving it: with the WALL lens active, searching "rosettes" still surfaces "Exhibits (1)".

V7 — THE FINDING'S STATED CAUSE WAS HALF RIGHT, AND THE SMALLER HALF. The audit read the bare-title card as a missing cover fallback. Measured here: `exhibits.json` DOES declare a cover for that exhibit (`screenshots/assets/o1-e1-embed.png`), the file IS on disk, and the request 404s — because covers/thumbnails are either absolute URLs (remote IIIF, how five of six seeded exhibits get theirs) or paths relative to the PUBLISHED ROOT, and the relative ones were rendered raw so they resolved against the page. New `publishedAssetUrl` resolves tree-relative refs against the serving base and passes absolute / protocol-relative / rooted / blob: / data: through untouched.
  The parity gap the finding named is real too and is also closed: `coverFallbacks` borrows the first object's thumbnail from the baked index (library→reading order, so "first" is the opening object) — what Studio's `coverOf` has always done. Note it could NOT have fixed the seeded card on its own: that exhibit has 21 index entries and zero thumbnails among them. Both halves were needed; only the path fix restored the card.

V20/V21 — MISFILED BY ME AT GRADUATION: both are `ObjectGrid.svelte` (the exhibit overview), not `Gallery.svelte`. Small and adjacent, so done here rather than moved. Default density is now Compact (was the density showing FEWEST — measured 3 of 12 objects in view at 1280x800, on an exhibit whose summary says it exists "to browse side by side"); the selected toggle no longer takes an accent fill, which had made a per-device display setting the loudest mark on an exhibit's front page, reading before a 3rem display title. The same quieting is applied to the Gallery's twin controls so one idiom holds. `grid-density.ts` is SHARED, so the default also changes the all-images wall — consistent, and one line to revert if you disagree.

V8 — OVERCLAIM, NOT FIXED. The finding says the shell's chrome changes with its DATA MODE (hosted keeps the Exhibits/All-images toggle, portable loses it). Measured: `loadImageIndex` reads `images.json` from the portable fs too (published.ts:338). The hosted tree has that file; the hand-made test zip does not. So the toggle tracks whether a tree carries an IMAGE INDEX — ADR-0023's documented degradation, already stated at Gallery.svelte:6 ("older trees: cards only") — not the data mode. The audit compared two libraries and attributed the difference to the wrong variable. A portable library published WITH an index gets the toggle.

V11 / V31 — SCOPED OUT. Both are embed-side, and the map's own territory note marks `packages/archie-viewer` as contested with a concurrent session. V11 (embed resolves no thumbnails from a zip source) is plausibly the portable twin of the V7 path bug — in portable mode assets are blob URLs minted by loadPortableExhibit (ADR-0010) and whether covers are inside that rewrite set is exactly the open question. Whoever takes the embed work should test V7's fix against the portable path first; `publishedAssetUrl`'s docblock records the boundary.

GATES: viewer 144 tests, svelte-check 1464 files 0 errors 0 warnings (--fail-on-warnings). Driven in real Chromium: 7/7, zero page errors. Five pre-existing assertions encoded the old defaults and were updated; 11 new tests cover searchActive, coverFallbacks and publishedAssetUrl.

title: Copy pass on the read surface
description:
## Question

Names and labels that mislead, repeat, or contradict each other. One `product-copy` pass.

## The defects

- **V91** one place, three names.
- **V86** the section label collides with the object label, and repeats itself.
- **V23** the four nav affordances agree about where you are and disagree about what you are looking at.
- **V65** the note card grows a stepper that steps something other than notes, only in a state the
  reader must discover.
- **V60** selecting a note shows it twice; expanding it shows it three times.
- **V64** the expanded sheet carries less context than the card it came from.

## Method

The `product-copy` skill, plus the WWWWH-first rule (lead with the plain definition, demote mechanics).
`CONTEXT.md` is the glossary and the authority on which name wins — if a term is contested there, fix
the glossary in the same pass rather than picking silently.
closeReason:
PARTIAL — V91 and V86 done and merged; V23, V60, V64, V65 deferred with reasons. Branch fix/read-copy, MERGED to main.

V91 — the narrative index seam had FOUR labels for TWO places: the spine calls itself "Narrative", the control that leaves says "All objects", the control that returns says "Back to the reading", and the screen you arrive at says "EXHIBIT · 12 ITEMS". None used another's word. The departure now says "All items", which matches both the destination's own "ITEMS" and the filmstrip handle's existing "All N items"; "Back to the reading" already named the return correctly and is unchanged. CONTEXT.md was the authority: it defines an Exhibit as "a curated set of media objects with a reading order and an optional narrative", so "items" for the objects and "the reading" for the narrative is the glossary's own split, not a new coinage.

V86 — the spine label rendered as `HERBAL· F1R — HERBAL (OPENING PAGE)`. Two defects in one string: the leading space inside the object span is trimmed at COMPILE time, so at letter-spacing 0.16em the separator sat flush against the title; and section title and object label both carry the division name, telling the reader "Herbal" twice. Separator moved into CSS (`::before`), where whitespace trimming cannot reach it; the object label now renders only when it adds something the section title has not already said.

DEFERRED, because each is a DESIGN question wearing copy's clothes:
- V23 (the four nav affordances agree where you are and disagree what you are looking at) — the disagreement is structural: breadcrumb, carousel, filmstrip and sidebar each derive their label from a different source. Renaming them to match would paper over the fact that they answer different questions; the fix is deciding which surface owns "what am I looking at", which is Archie-ed50's territory.
- V60 (selecting a note shows it twice; expanding shows it three times) and V64 (the expanded sheet carries LESS context than the card it came from) — these are about what each surface should CONTAIN, not what it should be called. Both were reshaped by the a11y work (Archie-c831 made the sheet a real dialog and named the card), and both should be re-measured against current main before anyone rewrites their copy.
- V65 (the note card grows a stepper that steps something other than notes, only in a state the reader must discover) — the copy cannot be fixed without deciding what the stepper should step, which is a behaviour decision.

RECOMMENDATION: fold V23/V60/V64/V65 into Archie-ed50, which already owns what the canvas and its cards show. They are not copy work.

GATES: svelte-check 1464 files 0/0. Driven in Chromium 4/4, asserting the RENDERED strings rather than the source — which is what caught that the flush separator was a compile-time trim, not a missing character.

title: Paint the selected mark: contrasting halo + breathing-room fit
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-ed50's decision: the selected annotation gains a contrasting halo, and
`fitBounds` leaves the selected region breathing room. Covers V43, V44 — and V47/V41/V46
fall out of the same pass.

## The work

1. **Halo as an OSD overlay element in @render/mount.** NOT a `MarkerStyle` change —
   `surface.ts:16-22` is a single fill/stroke and Annotorious 3 has no per-shape SVG node.
   Model it on `FrameOverlay` (surface.ts:24-28), the existing non-Annotorious overlay.
   One implementation, both consumers.
   - Contrast colour chosen by the mark colour's luminance (white on dark, near-black on light).
   - The embed's hook already exists: `read-overlay.ts:253` sets `data-selected` and NOTHING in
     the repo styles it. Wire the same overlay rather than adding orphan CSS.

2. **`fitBoundsRect` margin.** `fitbounds.ts` returns the annotation bbox verbatim; the only
   widening is the sidebar reservation. Inflate by a margin fraction, default 0.15. Pure
   function — unit-test it directly, both with and without the sidebar branch active.

3. **V47** — source `ReadingLegend`'s swatch from the same `readingMarkerStyle` call the canvas
   paints with. The disagreement is a duplicated constant, not a design question.

4. **V41** — give the whole-object frame a treatment visibly distinct from a region mark, so two
   nested rectangles stop meaning two things while looking identical.

5. **V46** — "Hide all" must leave the whole-object frame; it is the canvas's only named tab
   stop. Declutter hides REGION marks, not keyboard infrastructure.

## Verify

Drive BOTH consumers — the halo exists precisely because the two renderers disagree about what
they can paint. `apps/viewer/e2e` is the place for the assertion; assert the overlay element
exists for the selected id and is absent otherwise, which is renderer-independent.

## Prior art

Re-read `docs/research/a11y-interactions.md:117-133` before choosing contrast colours — the
colour-independent-coding pattern is already written there and this halo is its natural carrier.
Do NOT reopen the colour-only-coding question (shared code: Studio AND Viewer).
closeReason:
Halo shipped as a THIRD OSD overlay layer (packages/render-mount/src/selection-halo.ts), drawn identically by both renderers — the only shape that satisfies 'expressible in the poorer renderer', since MarkerStyle is one fill/stroke and Annotorious 3 has no per-shape SVG node. Three strokes: shadow / contrast ink (white on dark, near-black on light, by WCAG relative luminance) / the mark's own colour, so the ring never spends reading identity to say 'which one'. Prior art cited: annomea viewer.ts:161 swaps to a fixed accent — right there, wrong here. Embed's data-selected hook is now filled.

V44: fitBoundsRect inflates by FIT_MARGIN 0.15 BEFORE the sidebar reservation (margin is a property of the region, the widening a property of the viewport). Anvil oracle fixtures keep margin:0 so the characterization stays honest; the margin has its own 8 tests.
V47: legend swatch drawn as SVG from the same readingMarkerStyle call the canvas uses.
V41: frame is DASHED vs a solid region mark, with a separate solid transparent hit rect — a dash's gaps are not hit-testable, and the frame also gained the V68 pointerdown stopPropagation it never had.
V46: frame survives Hide-all (the canvas's only named tab stop).

Merged 36ce001. Gates: render-mount 197 (+38), svelte-check 1500 0/0, smoke 10/10 proven red-green twice (unwiring the halo; dropping neutraliseOverlayWrapper reproduces the V68 signature exactly). Annotorious renderer driven online by hand: 455x626, 3 rings, aria-hidden, wrapper none.

GAP RECORDED: apps/viewer/e2e runs offline and every annotated seed exhibit is remote-sourced, so OSD never opens and no canvas overlay is assertable there. New specs are the offline-surviving subset; canvas proof is recipes/smoke.mjs.

title: The floating chrome covers what the reader came to look at
description:
## Question

Four findings, one shape: a floating surface sits on top of the thing it is meant to help you read.
Deferred behind Archie-ed50 (now decided) because the canvas's selected-mark treatment determines
how much of the image must stay unobstructed.

- **V22** — the floating finder pill covers two of the twelve filmstrip frames.
- **V87** — the same finder occludes the last card in the narrative spine.
- **V48** — at the moment of closest looking, two cards cover the canvas's left flank.
- **V71** — an open note hides half the filmstrip.

## Why now

Archie-ed50 settled that the selected mark is a contrasting HALO drawn as an OSD overlay, and that
`fitBounds` leaves a 0.15 margin. Both decisions assume the reader can actually SEE the region the
camera just framed — occluding chrome defeats the fit margin exactly where it was bought.

## Shape of the fix

These are layout/reservation problems, not design questions: the floating surfaces need to reserve
space rather than overlap, or retreat when the surface beneath them is the one in use. Prefer the
existing reservation seam — `fitBoundsRect`'s sidebar branch already models "a panel is eating the
right flank" (fitbounds.ts, `MAX_SIDEBAR_FRACTION`); extend that idea rather than inventing a second
occlusion model.

## Verify

`apps/viewer/e2e` — assert bounding-box non-intersection between the floating element and the
filmstrip frames / spine cards / canvas region. Geometric assertions survive restyling; screenshot
diffs would not.
closeReason:
Merged 75bc949. Four findings, two mechanisms.

LAYOUT (V22/V71/V87): the bottom band had no source of truth. --topbar-h exists so every surface escaping the TOP band clears it by the same number and they 'can't drift apart' (ExhibitView.svelte:633); the bottom had no equivalent, so the finder pill and the note card were both pinned at bottom:--space-5 — inside the filmstrip. Added --strip-h, the mirror, published LIVE by Filmstrip (the band's height is content-driven and collapses to a handle; a static token would be right in one state and wrong in the other, which is exactly how the pill ended up inside it) and --finder-h for anything scrolling under the pill. Note V87 got WORSE when the pill was lifted for V22 — raising it moves it further up the spine's column — so the spine reserves the pill's whole footprint.

CAMERA (V48): the legend + note card overlay the canvas rather than sitting beside it (measured: contiguous 502px column, ~22% of a 924x800 canvas, down the entire left edge, at the moment the reader asked to zoom in). fitBoundsRect modelled only a RIGHT sidebar; it now reserves BOTH flanks — capping the TOTAL rather than each side (two greedy sides would sum past the guard and invert the rect) and scaling a capped pair proportionally so the region lands between them. With no left inset it reduces exactly to the historical w/(1-f), so the 37 existing tests were untouched.

DISCOVERY worth recording: getFitOptions — @render/mount's reservation seam — has existed since the anvil delamination and the VIEWER HAS NEVER PASSED IT. Every fit ran on PLAIN_FIT. Both readers now supply it, measuring on demand (the seam is a callback invoked at fit time, so there is nothing to keep in sync).

Guards: e2e/occlusion.spec.ts (5), bounding-box non-intersection per the ticket — geometry survives restyling. Proven red-green: reverting the three clearances fails four of five with true coordinates. The fifth caught me first — asserting on .num passed against the unfixed padding because the last section's TITLE clears the pill even when its prose and cite card do not; now asserts the whole <li>, which is what was measured being cut.

Gates: render-mount 204, viewer 149, e2e 39, svelte-check 1504 0/0, smoke 10/10.

title: The canvas is reachable, nameable and escapable by keyboard
description:
## Question

Four keyboard findings on and around the canvas, deferred behind Archie-ed50 because the tab-stop
inventory depends on what the canvas draws.

- **V45** — in the shell an individual region is not keyboard-reachable; in the embed every region
  is. The two consumers disagree about whether a mark is a control.
- **V90** — two unnamed tab stops sit on the canvas.
- **V25** — the keyboard object-step stops working the moment the reader touches the image.
- **V26** — there is no Escape ladder inside an exhibit.

## Why it waited

Archie-ed50 decided the whole-object frame stays put under "Hide all" precisely BECAUSE it is the
canvas's only named tab stop (V46). That makes the frame load-bearing keyboard infrastructure, and
settles what the inventory is built around.

## Constraints

- V45's divergence is the interesting one: decide which consumer is RIGHT before making them agree.
  Per-region tab stops scale badly (a 60-note page is 60 tab stops) — the filmstrip's roving
  tabindex (Filmstrip.svelte, Archie-c831) is the pattern the repo already chose for exactly this,
  and is the likely answer.
- `docs/research/a11y-interactions.md` holds the adopted interaction patterns. Consume it; don't
  re-derive.

## Verify

`apps/viewer/e2e` already drives roving tabindex on the filmstrip — the same technique applies.
Assert the tab-stop COUNT and that every stop has an accessible name; both are regressions the
moment someone adds an unnamed control.
closeReason:
Merged d917a40.

V90 — the two unnamed stops needed OPPOSITE fixes, which is the whole finding. The OSD canvas IS a control (arrows pan, +/- zoom; that cede is right for deep zoom) so it gets a NAME that states the keys — which is also V25's complaint, that nothing told the reader the arrows had changed meaning. Annotorious's layer is NOT a control: in the shell it paints to WebGL and holds no focusable shape, so a stop there can never do anything. canvas-a11y.ts only ever REMOVES a stop, guarded on tabindex=0, so a future Annotorious that does expose shapes won't be silently hidden by it. Applied BEFORE the open await: a failed open must not leave an unnamed stop, and that's the state a reader is most likely stuck in.

V45 — DECIDED: neither consumer was right, and they cannot share a mechanism (Annotorious 3 has no per-shape node to focus — a fact, not a preference). They now share the GUARANTEE — every note reachable and named — by different routes. Shell: the notes list (DOM, ordered, named; per Archie-c982 the list IS the index, which is exactly this job). Embed: the region overlay, now ONE tab stop with roving arrows instead of N. 60 notes was 60 tab presses to get past the image — the same wall V27 found on the filmstrip, where roving tabindex is already the repo's ratified answer (docs/research/a11y-interactions.md).

V26 — Escape is now a ladder, smallest rung first so holding it walks out rather than teleporting: close the note → leave the canvas → up a level (the narrative's top rung is its index, not an overview). Leaving the canvas lands focus on <main>, never <body>.

VERIFICATION GAP, recorded: offline the failed mount tears its own canvas out of the DOM (measured — querySelector returns null, no OSD element anywhere in the tab list), so the canvas assertions cannot live in apps/viewer/e2e. Driven ONLINE by hand instead: canvas tabindex=0 role=img aria-label 'Deep-zoom image — arrow keys pan, plus and minus zoom'; a9s layer tabindex=-1 aria-hidden=true; ZERO anonymous tab stops on the live reader; Escape moved focus out of the canvas onto <main> while staying on the object. The offline suite keeps the no-anonymous-stops sweep over surrounding chrome, the frame's named stop (tying V46 here), and three of the four rungs.

Gates: render-mount 207, viewer 149, e2e 44, svelte-check 1506 0/0, smoke 10/10, bundle +0.4KB total / +0KB eager.

title: Decide: where a note lives, and how many places show it at once
description:
## Question

When a reader selects a note, how many surfaces show that note, and what does each one own?

## What the audit measured

- **V60** — selecting a note shows it TWICE; expanding it shows it THREE times.
- **V64** — the expanded sheet carries LESS context than the card it came from, so "expand to read"
  loses information at the exact moment the reader asked for more.
- **V65** — the note card grows a stepper that steps something other than notes, and only in a state
  the reader must first discover.
- **V23** — the four nav affordances agree about where you are and disagree about what you are
  looking at.

## Why this is a decision, not a fix

Each finding alone reads as a bug. Together they say the note has no single home: the card, the
sheet, the canvas mark and the rail each hold a partial copy with different content and different
controls. You cannot dedupe without first saying which surface is canonical and what the others are
FOR — and V64 proves the current answer is inconsistent, since the "more" surface carries less.

## Now unblocked

Archie-ed50 settled the canvas half: the selected mark is a contrasting halo, so the CANVAS now has
a real answer to "which one" that it did not have before. That removes one reason a text surface had
to duplicate the identifying context — which is exactly the pressure that produced the triplication.

## Constraints

- The standalone note card is ONE shared component (`NotePopup.svelte`) used by Reader (grid /
  steps-objects) and NarrativeReader (narrative / steps-sections). A decision that splits its
  behaviour by mode splits that component — say so explicitly if that is the answer.
- V65's stepper is the concrete instance of the general question: a control that appears in one
  state and acts on a different noun than its container.

## Follow-on tickets (filed)

- Archie-dbbc — One note surface: NotePopup is the note, the sheet is it at a larger size (V60, V64)
- Archie-01a6 — Object/section nav belongs in the canvas chrome, not inside a note card (V65; reduces V23)
closeReason:
DECIDED: the note has ONE home, and the sheet is that home at a larger size.

THE MODEL — three surfaces, three distinct jobs, no duplicated content:
1. Sidebar list = INDEX. It locates and identifies (truncated preview, reading colour, tags, position). It is never a reading of the note. When its note is open it marks position; it does not restate the text.
2. NotePopup = THE NOTE. Full text, identity eyebrow, media, tags, actions. This is the canonical content renderer, and the ONLY one.
3. ReadingSheet = the SAME NotePopup at a larger size. It becomes a shell (scrim + focus-trapped dialog) that renders NotePopup inside it, with size='sheet'. It is not a second content surface.
4. Canvas mark = WHICH ONE (settled by Archie-ed50/52a0, the halo). This is what removed the pressure that produced the triplication: no text surface has to carry identifying context to answer 'which one' any more.

WHY THIS SHAPE:
- V64 (the sheet carries LESS than the card it came from) dies BY CONSTRUCTION, not by patching. One content renderer cannot have two different headers. Any future field added to the note card is in the sheet the same day.
- V60's count goes 2→2 on select and 3→2 on expand: index + note, in both states. The sheet does not add a copy; it resizes the one that exists.
- The NotePopup-is-shared constraint is SATISFIED, not split: Reader and NarrativeReader keep the same component, and so does the sheet. The mode difference stays where it already is — the eyebrow's content (object vs section·object) — which is data, not behaviour.

PRIOR ART (cited, decisive): annomea's NarrativePane (ADR-0021) is ONE pane at mini/half/full — a reader-controlled size slider, not three surfaces. Its ADR-0007 is explicit that the popup IS the note surface, popup OR drawer, one at a time. Archie had drifted to 'popup AND drawer AND list'. quire's expanded views leading with the work's identity is the V64 half.

V65 — DECIDED SEPARATELY: the stepper leaves the note card. It steps objects (Reader) or sections (NarrativeReader), never notes, so it does not belong inside a note. It only migrated there because collapsing the aside took the real object nav away with it. Object/section nav moves to the CANVAS CHROME, visible in BOTH sidebar states, with its noun spoken visibly ('Object 2 of 12' — matching what SidebarObjectNav already reads aloud). This fixes both halves of V65: the label AND the discoverability. NotePopup loses its 'step' prop entirely.

Follow-on: Archie-<impl> (one note surface) and Archie-<nav> (object/section nav to the canvas chrome). V23 (four nav affordances disagree about what you're looking at) is materially reduced by the nav move and should be re-measured after, not fixed blind.

title: The embed resolves tree-relative asset refs against the host page (V11)
description:
## Question

Measured 2026-07-25 while fixing Archie-64ef, in a real drive of `recipes/try.html`:

```
HTTP 404 http://127.0.0.1:PORT/recipes/screenshots/assets/o1-e1-embed.png
```

The library base is `/apps/viewer/public/published/`, and the asset ref in the tree is the
tree-relative `screenshots/assets/o1-e1-embed.png`. The embed resolved it against the HOST
PAGE's directory (`/recipes/`) instead of the library base, so it 404s.

## Why this matters more in the embed than in the app

This is the portable twin of **V7**, which `Archie-a897` fixed on the gallery side with
`publishedAssetUrl` (apps/viewer/src/published.ts) — the audit flagged it as "plausibly the
portable twin" and it is now measured rather than suspected.

But the embed's exposure is strictly worse: `<archie-viewer src="...">` is loaded from an
ARBITRARY host page at an arbitrary path, so the host's directory is never the library base.
In the app the two happened to coincide often enough to hide the bug.

## Shape of the fix

Resolve asset refs against the library base the loader already holds, not against
`document.baseURI`. `publishedAssetUrl`'s rule is the right one (absolute / protocol-relative /
root-anchored pass through; anything else anchors to the base) — check whether it can be shared
from `@render/core` rather than reimplemented, since a second copy is exactly how V7 and V11
drifted apart in the first place.

## Verify

`recipes/smoke.mjs` — assert ZERO 404s on asset requests during the gallery + object-open
drive. The 404 above was visible in that exact flow and nothing was watching for it.
closeReason:
Merged 6feebdd. Reproduced exactly as filed: `404 /recipes/screenshots/assets/o1-e1-embed.png`.

FIX: the rule moved to @render/core as `assetUrlAgainst(base, ref)`, and apps/viewer's `publishedAssetUrl` is now a thin binding of it to the app's base rather than a parallel implementation. The ticket asked whether it could be shared instead of reimplemented — it can, and a second copy is exactly how V7 and V11 drifted apart. One definition, two bases.

Applied at the READ boundary (openLibraryFromTree's openExhibit), mirroring the ZIP path's blob rewrite in loadPortableExhibit (ADR-0010) — same seam, same moment, different destination. One place to be right, and no way for a future consumer of `object.source` to forget. Covers: object source, thumbnail, a baked DZI's filesPath (which would 404 every TILE, and only at deep zoom — worse than the reported symptom), and the gallery covers.

Note bodies deliberately left alone: the app rewrites those for a DIFFERENT problem (absolute canonical BASE → serving origin), and a blind rewrite of note markup here would be a second, unmeasured behaviour riding on a bug fix.

GATE, and it caught me first. recipes/smoke.mjs now fails on any same-origin 404 during the drive. My first version asserted MID-drive and passed against the unfixed code — covers are `loading="lazy"`, so the request that exposes V11 had not been made yet. Verified by a standalone probe that the 404 was real the whole time. Moved to the end of the drive it goes red with the exact V11 signature and green with the fix. That red-green mattered more than usual here: a missing image degrades to a blank box and never reaches the console, which is why nothing was watching.

NOTE FOR THE PARITY TICKETS (Archie-c314): while measuring this I found the embed also has NO equivalent of the app's `toServingOrigin` rebase — published object sources are baked as ABSOLUTE canonical URLs (https://micahchoo.github.io/...), so a locally-served or re-hosted tree loads its images from the canonical host rather than from where it is actually served. Out of scope here (V11 is the tree-relative half), real, and worth folding into the embed-parity work.

Gates: render-core 1159, archie-viewer 138, viewer 149, studio 925, render-mount 207, e2e 44, smoke 11/11, svelte-check 1507 0/0, bundle +0KB eager.

title: The rights and metadata surfaces render nothing on the read side (V103/V104)
description:
## Question

Two findings deferred INTO this map by the Viewer UX audit (Archie-c405, 2026-07-25), because this
map owns read-side rights and metadata display. They were named at resolution but never filed —
this ticket closes that gap.

- **V103 — the license ladder is inverted.** The object is licensed, the exhibit is not, and the
  library has nothing at all. Rights should get MORE general as you go up, not vanish: a reader
  arriving at the library sees no licensing, then finds it only by opening a specific object.
- **V104 — the Dublin Core metadata surfaces render nothing, anywhere in the corpus.** Not "render
  wrong" — render nothing, across every exhibit. Determine first whether this is a SEED gap (no
  exhibit sets the fields) or a RENDER gap (the fields are set and the surface drops them). The two
  have opposite fixes and the audit did not separate them.

## Why here and not on the viewer map

`Archie-c6bf` owns Dublin Core metadata end to end, including the `RightsFields` write-back
contract (`.claude/rules/metadata-rights-keyed-writebacks.md`). Fixing display on the viewer map
would have split that ownership.

## Do V104's triage first

It gates V103's framing: if no seed exhibit carries metadata, then "renders nothing" is a showroom
problem and belongs with `ledgers/SHOWROOM.md`, and the render path is untested rather than broken.
Check `apps/viewer/fixtures/sample-data.ts` (voynichExhibitMetadata is referenced there) against
what `MetadataRun.svelte` actually receives.

## Related

`Archie-aafd` decides whether the read boundary REJECTS excluded dcterms properties or displays
them — that decision changes what V104's surface is supposed to show, so land aafd first if the
triage says the render path is at fault.

title: One note surface: NotePopup is the note, the sheet is it at a larger size
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-c982's decision. Covers V60, V64.

## The work

1. **NotePopup gains `size: "card" | "sheet"`** (default `"card"`). Sheet size = wider measure,
   larger type, no anchoring to the mark. SAME markup, same header, same media/tags/actions.

2. **ReadingSheet becomes a SHELL, not a content surface.** It keeps what it uniquely owns — the
   scrim, `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`, and `use:dialog` (the focus trap V63 installed; do NOT
   regress it) — and renders `<NotePopup size="sheet" ... />` inside. It stops rendering `text`
   itself. Its `aria-label` comes from the same eyebrow NotePopup already builds, so the sheet
   finally says what you are reading (V64).

3. **The sidebar card stops restating the note while it is open.** It is the INDEX: preview, reading
   colour, tags, position. Selected state marks position — it must not read as a second copy of the
   text. (Judgement call on exactly how it de-emphasises; the constraint is that a reader never sees
   the same sentence twice in two type treatments 900px apart, which is what V60 measured.)

4. **Only ONE note-content element on screen at a time.** With the sheet open the floating card must
   not remain behind the scrim — measured, `.note-pop` is still in the DOM and legible there today,
   which is V60's third copy. Either the popup renders INTO the sheet, or it hides while the sheet
   is open. Assert whichever you choose.

## Constraints

- `NotePopup.svelte` is shared by Reader (grid / steps-objects) and NarrativeReader (narrative /
  steps-sections). This decision deliberately does NOT split it — the mode difference stays in the
  eyebrow's CONTENT (object vs section·object), which is data. Keep it that way.
- The `step` prop is being removed by the sibling nav ticket. Coordinate: do not build sheet support
  for a control that is leaving.

## Verify

- `apps/viewer/e2e/note.spec.ts` already guards V61/V62/V63 — those must stay green (especially the
  focus trap; the sheet is still a real dialog).
- Add: with the sheet open, exactly ONE element renders the note's body text.
- Add: the sheet's header carries the same identity string as the card it came from (V64) — assert
  they are EQUAL, not merely both non-empty, or the class comes back.

## Prior art

annomea `NarrativePane` (ADR-0021): one pane at mini/half/full, reader-controlled — not three
surfaces. ADR-0007: popup OR drawer, one at a time. quire: expanded views lead with identity.
---

## Resolution (2026-07-26) — merged `273bea7`

**The defect was real and worse than "styling".** Expanding a note and then clicking a tag chip put
**two `aria-modal="true"` dialogs on screen at once** (the reading sheet plus the finder). The old
sheet also took only `text`, so a note's media and tags *vanished* on expand — the larger size was
strictly lossier than the card it replaced.

**The rule the three separate judgements collapse to**, which is what makes this one decision rather
than three:

> A card affordance is withheld at sheet size **only when it is meaningless there** (the expand glyph
> offers to expand what is already expanded). Everything meaningful at any size is **kept**, and
> anything modal it opens **replaces** the sheet rather than stacking on it.

So: media and tags are carried into the sheet; the expand glyph is not; `onopenfinder` and `onmedia`
both clear `readingSheet` in both readers.

The hide mechanism is `display: contents` → `display: none` on `.note-slot`, so the card is not
unmounted while the sheet is up — state survives the round trip.

`NotePopup.svelte` remains the ONE shared standalone note card (Reader grid/steps-objects and
NarrativeReader narrative/steps-sections both use it), so this fix reached every surface at once.

### Gates
svelte-check 1518 files 0/0 · typecheck 7/7 · vitest 176 · **e2e 85 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**.

The skipped count going to zero matters: two of this slice's *own* new tests were silently vacuous
via `Locator.count()` after `goto` (one skipped on `n < 2`, one reported "no AV object in the
sampler") — **both while the fixture was perfectly fine**. Filed as
`.claude/rules/playwright-count-does-not-wait.md`.

### Follow-up filed
- **Archie-0cc6** — the `onmedia` half of the guard is correct, **unfalsifiable, and on a route no
  fixture can reach**: reverting `readingSheet = false` from `onmedia` in both readers leaves 18/18
  passing, because no fixture note is both expandable and media-bearing (a note needs `text` to show
  the expand glyph at all). The guard is right; the fixture is thin. Do not close that one by
  deleting the guard.
closeReason: Merged 273bea7 — the sheet keeps every meaningful affordance and modals replace it rather than stacking. Follow-up Archie-0cc6 filed for the unfalsifiable media route.

title: Object/section nav belongs in the canvas chrome, not inside a note card
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-c982's second decision. Covers V65; materially reduces V23.

## The work

1. **Remove the `step` prop from `NotePopup.svelte`** (`:58-74`) and its two wirings
   (`Reader.svelte:413`, `NarrativeReader.svelte:350`). A note card carries the note. It must not
   carry a control that acts on a different noun.

2. **Put object/section nav in the CANVAS CHROME, visible in BOTH sidebar states.** Today the aside
   holds `SidebarObjectNav` and the stepper only appears when the aside is COLLAPSED — a primary nav
   affordance that exists only in a state most visitors never enter. That is the discoverability half
   of V65 and it is the more serious half.

3. **Speak the noun VISIBLY.** `‹ Object 2 of 12 ›`, not `‹ Prev 1 / 12 Next ›`. The aria side is
   already honest (`SidebarObjectNav` reads "Object 2 of 12"); the visible text should match it.
   In the narrative the same control says `Section 3 of 6`. Route the wording through `product-copy`.

## Why this is the fix and not the label alone

The stepper migrated into the note card because collapsing the aside took the real nav with it. Fix
the cause — nav that lives where the thing it navigates lives — and the symptom has nowhere to
reappear. Relabelling alone leaves a primary affordance hidden behind a state toggle.

## Watch

- `V80`/`Archie-40fe` is the floating-chrome occlusion ticket. Adding chrome to the canvas is
  adding to exactly the surface 40fe is about — coordinate, or the nav lands on top of the scale cue.
  Doing 40fe FIRST is defensible if its reservation model is what this should slot into.
- `V23` says the four nav affordances agree about WHERE you are and disagree about WHAT you are
  looking at. This ticket changes one of the four. RE-MEASURE V23 after, do not fix it blind.

## Verify

Drive both modes with the sidebar OPEN and COLLAPSED — four states. The nav must be present and
correct in all four, and the note card must carry no stepper in any of them.
---

## Resolution (2026-07-26) — merged `273bea7`

Object nav now lives in the canvas chrome. The reasoning that settled it is **structural, not
aesthetic**, and worth keeping because it also explains a side effect nobody asked for.

`stepIntoReading` existed **because the stepper lived inside the note card**. Stepping had to keep a
note selected or the card would unmount — pulling the button out from under the reader's cursor
mid-gesture. The carry was never a reading feature; it was the machinery keeping the control mounted
while it was being used. Moving nav to the canvas chrome, where it neither moves nor unmounts,
dissolved the justification along with the structure that needed it.

**`MediaPlayer.svelte` deliberately keeps the sidebar stepper** — an AV object has no canvas chrome
to move object nav to. It is byte-identical to base (`8a7a8344`), because `MediaPlayer.svelte:54`
already computed the identical opt-in condition and `ExhibitView.svelte:575-578` already fed all four
props. The opt-in gate is at `SidebarObjectNav.svelte:32`. That "no change needed" is pinned by a
wiring test rather than left to look like an oversight.

### One measurement error worth recording, because it nearly shipped a false gate

The coordinator asked for a landmark assertion on the opted-out path. As specified it was **green
before the fix**: two different `<nav>`s carry the identical accessible name `"Objects in this
exhibit"` (this component's old root, and the canvas-chrome stepper via `navRegionName("object")`),
so `getByRole('navigation', {name: 'Objects in this exhibit'})` could never fail. Measured: image
path 1 → GREEN, AV path 1 → GREEN. The container-scoped form
(`Back-to-Exhibit.closest('nav')`) goes **null → RED** on both. The landmark was never actually
lost — the name migrated with the control.

### Gates
svelte-check 1518 files 0/0 · typecheck 7/7 · vitest 176 · e2e 85 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped.

### Follow-ups filed
- **Archie-5185** — flip-and-read disappeared as a consequence of removing `stepIntoReading`, and
  **neither this ticket nor Archie-dbbc asked for that.** Recorded as a decision rather than a side
  effect. The argument above is structural; whether a reader working through a sequence of annotated
  objects *wants* the note to follow them is a reading question, and only the first has been
  answered. `object-nav.spec.ts` pins the current behaviour explicitly, with a comment naming it as
  the test to invert if the project restores the carry.
- **Archie-d6e9** — V23 re-measured: two object-stepping affordances remain, named.
closeReason: Merged 273bea7 — object nav moved to the canvas chrome; MediaPlayer keeps the sidebar stepper by design. Follow-ups Archie-5185 (flip-and-read decision) and Archie-d6e9 filed.

title: The note rung resolves: match by logicalId, not by full IRI
description:
## Question

Fix V100. The cite ladder's note rung has NEVER resolved — but the grammar is fine and must not change.

## The actual defect

`route.ts` parses `#/<slug>/a/<id>` into one path segment. Published note ids are
`{baseUrl}{slug}/annotations/{ULID}/v{n}` (site.ts:510 `citeBase`). `note-arrival.ts:29,33`
compares that single segment to the WHOLE IRI with `===`. Nothing can satisfy it.

`buildNoteDeepLink(logicalId)` (deeplink.ts:76) already builds `#/a/<logicalId>`, and `brand.ts`
already owns the split (`mintLogicalId`, `versionId`, `parseVersionId`, `VERSION_ID_RE`). The
intended design was always "the URL carries the ULID". Only the comparison is wrong.

## The work

1. **A pure helper in `@render/core`** — `logicalIdOf(publishedAnnotationId): LogicalId | null`.
   Reuse `brand.ts`'s `VERSION_ID_RE` against the IRI tail; do NOT hand-roll a second regex, and do
   NOT split on "/" and take `[-2]` (a base path containing `/annotations/` would break it silently).
   Returns null for anything that is not `{...}/annotations/{ULID}/v{n}`.

2. **`resolveNoteArrival` matches on logicalId.** Accept EITHER form for the incoming id (a bare
   ULID from the address bar, or a full IRI from an internal caller) by normalising both sides
   through the helper.

3. **Audit every other `a.id === ` comparison** against a URL-supplied id. `resolveNoteArrival` is
   the one the audit measured; grep for siblings (`narrative-landing.ts` `ownerObjectOf`,
   `arrivalSectionIndex`, the search-jump path) before calling this done.

## Verify

- **Drive a REAL published id end to end**: take a ULID out of
  `apps/viewer/public/published/voynich/manifest.json`, visit `#/voynich/a/<ULID>`, assert the note
  opens and the camera fits it. The audit drove five spellings and all five degraded; this must be
  the sixth that does not.
- A tombstoned/unknown id must STILL degrade honestly (ADR-0003) — do not turn a miss into a throw.
- e2e, not a unit test alone: the bug lived in the seam between a parser and a comparison, and both
  halves were individually correct.
closeReason:
Done — merged as 4e21416 (commit ed40a42).

`logicalIdOf` lives in `brand.ts` (which already owned the split) and normalises BOTH
sides. The `{ULID}/v{n}` pattern now has ONE source, composed from `ULID_RE`; the IRI
matcher is anchored on `/annotations/` AND on end-of-string, so a deploy path containing
`/annotations/` cannot shift the match — the silent failure the forbidden
`split("/").at(-2)` would have had. Version-agnostic by construction, which is what
ADR-0003 needs: a cite minted at v1 still names the note at v9.

THE AUDIT (step 3) FOUND TWO MORE SHIPPING HALVES — this ticket was bigger than one
comparison:

1. `narrative-landing.ts` `ownerObjectOf` carried the identical raw-`===` defect, so it
   always returned null and `arrivalSectionIndex` fell back to section 0. Every
   deep-linked note in a narrative exhibit landed at the TOP of the spine instead of its
   own beat — a plausible-looking wrong answer, which is why nobody caught it.
2. `ExhibitView` set `arrivedNote = targetNote` (the raw URL segment), which feeds
   Reader's `initialSelected` and is matched against `annotation.id`. That re-opened the
   same gap one layer down: the object would open and the note still never select.
   `resolveNoteArrival` now returns the note's PUBLISHED id and callers carry that —
   hence the new `noteId` field on `NoteArrival`.

WHY THE OLD TESTS WERE GREEN, which is the part worth remembering: both fixtures used the
same synthetic string (`"n-base"`) for the queried id AND the annotation id. With both
sides identical, raw `===` passes — the suite was structurally incapable of modelling the
bug. Rewritten to the real shapes (published IRI in the data, bare ULID in the query).

VERIFIED with a REAL published id, read out of the committed manifest AT RUNTIME rather
than hard-coded — a literal would rot on the next regen and then assert the degrade path
while looking like the happy one. Drives `screenshots`: the one seed exhibit with local
images (so it runs in the hermetic offline suite), and whose notes live only on READING
pages, so arrival must flip the reading on rather than merely find the object.

Red-green proven: both happy-path e2e tests fail against the restored raw `===`; the two
degrade tests pass either way, correctly.

Gates: 2605 unit (+34), 48 e2e (+4), smoke 15/15, svelte-check 0/0, TS7 clean.

title: The address bar writes every rung the grammar already reads
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-d5cd's address decision. Covers V101, V24, V84, V52.

## The work

`route.ts` parses `/o/`, `/a/`, `/s/`, `?xywh` and `?t`; the viewer honours all of them on arrival
and writes NONE. Make the address track the DEEPEST rung currently open:

| reader state | address |
| --- | --- |
| exhibit | `#/<slug>` |
| object open | `#/<slug>/o/<objectId>` |
| note open | `#/<slug>/a/<logicalId>` |
| section active | `#/<slug>/s/<sectionId>` |
| note + region / offset | `…?xywh=…` / `…?t=…` |

- **`replaceState`, not `pushState`.** Selecting notes must not fill the back stack — Escape and the
  browser Back button both already mean "up a level", and a per-selection history entry would make
  Back mean "the previous note" instead. (If a case for pushState appears, it is arrival, not
  selection.)
- **Use `routeToHash`** (route.ts) — the inverse already exists. Do not hand-build strings.
- **Depends on Archie-67b6**: writing `#/<slug>/a/<ULID>` is only honest once that address resolves.

## What this unblocks, and why they are the same ticket

- **V84** — the narrative section index has no address, so stepping out and back loses your place.
  Writing `/s/<id>` fixes it with the rung that already exists.
- **V52** — ADR-0021's `t=` landing seek (seek PAUSED at an offset, deliberately not the play-coupled
  `seekTo`) is correctly built and structurally UNREACHABLE: no address ever carried `t=`. Working
  code, no way in. Writing the param is the whole fix.
- **V106** — the finder returns text with no address or locus. Once every result HAS an address, the
  finder can show one.

## Verify

`apps/viewer/e2e`. Assert the round trip, which is the property that matters: drive to a state, read
`location.hash`, reload, and assert the SAME state. A test that only checks the string is written
would pass against an address nothing can parse — which is exactly how V100 survived.
closeReason:
Done — merged as c903371 (commit 110cc53).

ONE writer, in ExhibitView, fed by an `onlocus` seam the three reader islands report
through (Reader, NarrativeReader, MediaPlayer). The islands stay ignorant of the address
grammar — they report the raw note id, the active section, the region, the cue offset —
and ExhibitView alone decides precedence and builds the string via `routeToHash`. A second
writer is how the writer and the parser drift apart.

Precedence is the ladder's own, with one refinement the ticket's table didn't cover: an
object opened from the NARRATIVE INDEX (ADR-0016's escape-out) is deeper than the section
behind it, so it takes the rung. Otherwise the section is the narrative's rung — an object
id would be the wrong grain there, since the spine may revisit one object across several
sections.

`replaceState`, never `pushState`, as decided.

V52 detail: the AV rung reports the CUE'S START, not `currentTime`. A link must land at the
beginning of the moment it names, and a per-frame value would rewrite the bar continuously
while citing an arbitrary instant. Fires on cue boundaries.

One interaction worth recording: the writer YIELDS to V4's honest-degrade path. While the
arrival chrome is explaining that a cited target was missing, `normalizeAddressToExhibit`
owns the bar; re-asserting a locus would race it and could restore the dead address the
reader was just rescued from.

VERIFIED as the round trip, not the string — drive, read `location.hash`, RELOAD, assert
the same state. Red-green: 4 of 5 fail with the writer disabled. The fifth (Back doesn't
walk notes) passes either way by construction; it guards a future `pushState` regression
rather than today's bug, and its comment says so rather than implying broader coverage.

Gates: 2605 unit, 53 e2e (+5), smoke 15/15, svelte-check 0/0, TS7 clean.

UNBLOCKED, as the ticket predicted: V106 (the finder can now show each result's address)
and Archie-3ea1's link grain, which must READ `location.hash` rather than re-derive it.

title: Cite panel: link, formatted citation, and IIIF Content State at equal weight
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-d5cd's taking-away decision. Covers V102 (the audit's headline finding), V106.

There is currently NO clipboard or share affordance anywhere in the read surface. For a tool whose
purpose is citable annotation, that is the finding the whole audit points at.

## The work

A **cite panel** offering three grains SIDE BY SIDE — not a menu behind a default, because the three
serve different readers and hiding two answers only the easiest case:

1. **Link** — the address for the current rung. Comes free once Archie-99b1 writes it; this panel
   must READ that address, never re-derive it, or the two drift and one of them is wrong.
2. **Citation** — a formatted, copyable reference. Prior art donor: `quire`
   (`packages/11ty/_includes/components/citation/`) builds CSL-JSON and renders MLA/Chicago. Read it
   before designing the fields; the exhibit already carries `requiredStatement` + Dublin Core
   `metadata` (Archie-c6bf), which is most of what CSL needs.
3. **IIIF Content State** — `encodeContentState` / `decodeContentState` ALREADY EXIST, unused, in
   `packages/render-core/src/url/deeplink.ts` (ADR-0022). Wire the existing codec; do not write a
   second one. Prior art: `canvases-annotations-sharing`.

Offer it at the grains the ladder has: note, object, section, exhibit.

## Constraint — do not undo Archie-40fe

`Archie-40fe` just spent a whole ticket getting floating chrome OFF the canvas (V22/V48/V71/V87).
This panel must be a **dialog** — the `ReadingSheet` shape: scrim, `use:dialog` focus trap, Escape,
focus returned to the trigger — NOT a new persistent floating surface. A cite panel parked over the
canvas is V48 again with a different name.

Reuse `dialog-a11y.ts`. `apps/viewer/e2e/note.spec.ts` has the assertions that shape must satisfy
(focus moves in, Tab is trapped, Escape returns focus); the panel gets the same.

## Verify

- Each grain's copied text is asserted from the CLIPBOARD, not from the DOM node that displays it.
- The link grain must equal `location.hash` at that moment — assert equality, not both-non-empty.
- The Content State grain must round-trip through `decodeContentState`.
closeReason:
Done — merged as 532ebdc (commit 7a45198).

Three grains side by side, as decided. The LINK grain READS `location.href`, never
re-derives it. CONTENT STATE wires the EXISTING `encodeContentState` codec (ADR-0022), which
had sat unused since it was written — no second encoding.

CITATION: prior art read first, as instructed. quire's `citation/page.js` adapts page data to
a CSL-JSON item (author / container-title / issued.date-parts / publisher / title / type /
URL) and hands it to a formatter plugin for MLA or Chicago. `render-core/cite/citation.ts`
copies quire's FIELD MAPPING and deliberately stops short of its formatter: real MLA/Chicago
means citation-js or citeproc — a new runtime dependency in the viewer island graph, which is
exactly the shape `.claude/rules/viewer-optimizedeps-bare-includes.md` records biting three
times, and it would land on the embed's eager budget too. So it emits the CSL-JSON (the
interchange format — paste into Zotero and it IS a real citation) plus one plainly formatted
line built FROM that item, so the two cannot drift.

Dublin Core supplies author/publisher/issued; `requiredStatement` rides CSL `note` so the
MUST-display credit survives being pasted.

TWO HEURISTICS PINNED HONESTLY rather than hidden:
- `cslName` keeps an institution whole (splitting "Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library"
