  family-last would cite an author named "Library"), but a two-word non-personal name like
  "Unknown scribe" still splits. Nothing in the string distinguishes it from a personal name,
  and guessing harder would misfile real people. The test says so and names the real fix (an
  authored `literal` flag on the metadata entry), rather than implying coverage it lacks.
- `yearOf` returns undefined rather than guessing — a wrong year is worse than an absent one.

Content State is ABSENT at object/section/exhibit grain, not fabricated: it names an
annotation on a canvas, so those rungs genuinely have none, and a payload decoding to a
non-existent target is worse than no payload.

DID NOT UNDO Archie-40fe: the panel is a dialog in the ReadingSheet shape (scrim + sheet
siblings, `use:dialog`, Escape, focus returned), and the trigger sits in the SAME chrome row
as the finder pill — the one strip whose geometric tests already hold it clear of the
filmstrip and the note card, inheriting the same `--strip-h` reservation.

VERIFIED as required: every grain asserted from the CLIPBOARD, not the textarea that displays
it. Link asserts EQUALITY with `location.href`. Content State is decoded and checked to be a
real Annotation/highlighting payload. Red-green: re-deriving the link instead of reading the
address fails both the link and citation tests.

Gates: 2621 unit (+16), 59 e2e (+6), smoke 15/15, svelte-check 0/0, TS7 clean, eager +0.1KB.

V106's other half (the finder showing each result's address) is now trivially available —
every result has an address and the panel proves the grain works.

title: Embed ships rights, attribution and licence (V105) — legal, do this first
description:
## Question

Implement the non-negotiable half of Archie-52a9. Covers V105.

`<archie-viewer>` shows NO attribution, licence or metadata at gallery OR object level, against a
published tree whose manifests DO carry `requiredStatement` — the shell renders it on the same
object, from the same bytes. An embed that strips a required statement is legal exposure, not a
missing feature, and it is the reason this is filed separately and first.

## The work

- Render the exhibit-level and object-level `requiredStatement` (label + value) and `rights` (licence
  URI) wherever the embed shows an exhibit or an object.
- Read them from the SAME already-resolved published values the shell reads (`readExhibitTree` →
  `PortableExhibit`). Do NOT re-run the opt-in cascade — it collapsed at publish time (the Q5 note in
  ExhibitView.svelte), and re-deriving here would let the two consumers disagree about what a work is
  credited to.
- Dublin Core `metadata` (Archie-c6bf) rides the same already-resolved path; include it.

## Weight

~0KB. The bytes are already fetched — this is rendering data the embed downloads and discards.
Assert it: `node build.mjs --check` must show eagerGzKB unmoved.

## Verify

`recipes/smoke.mjs`, against the BUILT bundle: open an object whose manifest carries a
`requiredStatement` and assert the statement's VALUE appears in the shadow DOM. Not that a rights
element exists — that its text matches the manifest, or the two can drift exactly as they did before.
closeReason:
Done — merged as 4df71ee (feat commit 309dd67).

The credit line renders at all three view-levels from the already-resolved published
values: the gallery's on `ExhibitsJson.library`, the exhibit's spread onto
`PortableExhibit` by `rightsFromIIIF`, the object's on `AObject`. The reader shows the
OBJECT's own credit with NO display-time inheritance — matching ExhibitView.svelte's Q5
rule. Markup follows Credit.svelte, with `<details>` instead of a wired button so the
open/close and a11y semantics are the platform's. The credit VALUE is never behind the
disclosure; licence and Dublin Core rows ride it.

WEIGHT — the ticket's "~0KB" was wrong, and this is the one thing worth carrying forward.
Eager page-load payload moved 33.1KB -> 36KB gz (+2.9KB, ~9%). Isolated by measurement:
markup+CSS +0.8KB, `licenseLabel` +0.3KB, `metadataRows` +1.8KB (it pulls the dcterms
vocabulary table). The estimate was reasoning about DATA — those bytes genuinely were
already fetched and discarded — and didn't account for the display helpers' CODE. Inside
the ratchet's +10KB allowance; baseline re-recorded at 36KB.

VERIFIED as the ticket asked: `recipes/smoke.mjs` against the BUILT bundle, comparing the
shadow DOM against the MANIFEST's own values, not merely that a rights element exists.
Four new hard assertions (exhibit statement, object statement, licence href, every Dublin
Core label present), 11/11 -> 15/15, proven red-green — all four fail against the pre-fix
bundle.

One trap worth recording: `recipes/try.html` loads `/dist/archie-viewer.js` (the ROOT
mirror), not `packages/archie-viewer/dist/`. Rebuilding the package alone leaves the smoke
driving the OLD bundle — it reported this fix as still-broken until `node
scripts/sync-dist.mjs` ran. Same shape as the stale-generated-artifact class in
.claude/rules/svelte-no-typecheck-net.md.

title: ADR-0019 gains a capability contract, and smoke enforces it
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-52a9's enforcement decision: make the embed's obligations explicit and gated.

## Why convention failed

`element.ts:9-10` records the mechanism: the markup was **ported, not imported**. Ported markup
drifts silently, and nothing was watching.

Prior art is decisive, and it is a cautionary tale about the AUDIT as much as the code. annomea's
`EMBED-AUDIT.md` found its whole Channel-3 Web Component had "evaporated silently" — and explains
why the previous audit missed it: that audit was **file-driven**, annomea had no `embed/` directory,
so every counterpart file "had zero counterpart to compare against and was **invisible by
construction**." Archie lost readings, navigation, rights and the narrative the same way, with every
test green throughout.

So the gate must be **capability-driven**. A capability with no file cannot go missing quietly.

## The work

1. **A contract table in `docs/adr/0019`**, one row per capability, using annomea's own verdict
   vocabulary — `PORT` / `ADAPT` / `DROP-justified` / `DEFER-tracked` / `ABSENT`:

   | capability | verdict | gate |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | rights / attribution / licence | MUST | smoke |
   | object navigation | MUST | smoke |
   | note list | MUST | smoke |
   | readings + legend | MUST | smoke |
   | narrative | MUST | smoke |
   | authoring / drawing | DROP-justified | — |
   | Annotorious + PixiJS | DROP-justified | eagerGzKB |

2. **`recipes/smoke.mjs` asserts every MUST row** against the BUILT bundle. It is already the gate
   that drives real Chromium and already the only thing that catches this class.

3. Adding a `DROP` row becomes a deliberate, reviewable act with a written reason — which is the
   whole point. A silent drop becomes a failing build.

## Watch

Scope this to a CONTRACT plus assertions. A shared framework-free component layer was considered and
REJECTED in Archie-52a9: the embed is framework-free by design and the shell is Svelte, so it means
shipping a framework in the embed or rewriting the shell's UI. Don't reopen it here.

title: Embed parity: object nav, note list, readings, narrative, shared tokens
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-52a9's parity decision. Covers V30, V56, V70, V88, and V9/V31/V69.

The audit's clearest pattern: the embed did not lose polish, it lost FUNCTION. ADR-0019 sanctions
dropping Annotorious/PixiJS for a geometry-only DOM-SVG overlay. It sanctions nothing else.

## The work, each behind the EXISTING lazy boundary

The weight argument mostly dissolves: ADR-0019's budget is enforced on `eagerGzKB` (32.9 today), and
every one of these rides behind the same `await import("./reader.js")` boundary the canvas already
uses. Measured expectation — confirm each with `node build.mjs --check`, and treat any eager
movement as the bug:

- **V30 object navigation** (~1KB) — a 12-object exhibit's entire visible control set is
  `["← The Whole Manuscript"]`. There is no way to move between objects at all.
- **V70 note list** (~2KB) — with no list, the marker is the only door to a note, and V69 makes the
  marker near-invisible. Per Archie-c982 the list is the INDEX; that role is what is missing here.
- **V56 readings + legend** (~2KB) — three readings in the library, zero coloured marks, no legend.
  Colour the marks through `readingMarkerStyle` (render-core), the same call the shell and the
  legend swatch use — do not hand-roll a third copy of those numbers.
- **V88 narrative** (~8KB, and only downloaded for exhibits that HAVE sections) — `voynich-reading`
  renders 12 thumbnails, zero prose, no sections, no spine. The one exhibit whose entire subject is
  the narrative.

## V9 / V31 / V69 — share the tokens, do not copy them

Decided in Archie-52a9: the duplicated `markers.css` / `tokens.css` / `atmosphere.css` copies are
NOT the right boundary, because they are precisely what produced the drift the audit saw — white +
system-ui + orange + square cards + a 1.5px near-black hairline marker, against the shell's green
atmosphere, display face and reading colours. Share the token layer.

## Order

`Archie-b681` (rights) ships first — it is legal exposure. `Archie-f90d` (the contract + smoke gate)
should land BEFORE or WITH this, so each capability is asserted as it arrives rather than after.

title: The image follows along: couple the spine and the camera, both directions
description:
## Question

Implement Archie-e902's decision: the image follows along. Covers V81, V82, V85.

## The state you are starting from

Better than the audit implies. All beats are ALREADY rendered in one scrollable column — measured,
the spine aside has `scrollHeight` 2255 against `clientHeight` 720, six `<li>` present, each with its
own `<div class="prose">`. Nothing hides the non-active beats. The mode is one observer away from
its own stated premise.

## The work

1. **Scroll → camera (V81).** An `IntersectionObserver` over the beat `<li>`s drives `activeIndex`;
   the camera follows through the existing `fitRegion(section.start)` path.
   Prior art, in the corpus and exact: **scrollama**, explicitly built on "IntersectionObserver in
   favor of scroll events" — same choice, same reason. Do not hand-roll scroll math or listen to
   `scroll` directly.

2. **Activate → scroll (V82).** This is the SAME coupling run backwards, not a second feature. A
   section cite currently lands the camera and strands the prose off-screen because activation only
   ever drove one half. `activate(i)` must also scroll that beat into view. One coupling, two
   directions, so both halves of the mode arrive together whichever door the reader came in by.

3. **Number the beats (V85).** Once the active beat moves under the reader, "where am I" needs an
   answer that is not just typographic emphasis. `Section 3 of 6`, matching the noun-and-position
   idiom `SidebarObjectNav` and Archie-01a6 already use.

## The hazard this creates

The two directions will fight if you let them. A programmatic scroll from `activate()` re-enters the
observer and can bounce the reader to a neighbouring beat. Either suppress the observer for the
duration of a programmatic scroll, or ignore observer callbacks that disagree with an intended
target. Whichever you choose, TEST IT: drive a section cite and assert the spine settles on the cited
beat, not its neighbour.

## Verify

`apps/viewer/e2e`, offline — the spine and its prose render from the local manifest, so this whole
interaction is testable with the network cut (unlike anything needing a painted canvas; see
selection.spec.ts's header). Assert: scrolling the spine changes the active beat; activating a beat
scrolls it into view; a section cite lands on the CITED beat and stays there.

title: Hiding the narrative spine is per-exhibit and plainly reversible
description:
## Question

Fix V83, which Archie-e902's decision makes more urgent than the audit rated it.

## Why it got worse

Hiding the spine is sticky, global and near-irreversible. Under the OLD behaviour that cost the
reader a panel. Under Archie-0d6c's scroll coupling the spine becomes the mode's INPUT DEVICE — the
thing that drives the camera — so hiding it does not merely hide prose, it silently removes the
interaction the mode is named for, and leaves an image that no longer follows anything.

## The work

- **Per-exhibit, not global.** Collapsing the spine on one narrative must not collapse it on the
  next. The persistence idiom is already here: `aside-persistence.ts` + the `archie.*.v1` metadata
  keys; scope the key by exhibit slug.
- **Plainly reversible.** Whatever the collapsed state renders must carry a visible, named way back —
  the same discipline `Archie-3d55` applied to the canvas (`ResizeDivider` stays a sibling of the
  collapsed aside precisely so un-collapsing stays reachable; check that idiom before inventing one).
- Consider whether "hidden" should even survive a reload for a scroll-coupled mode. A reader who
  returns to a narrative and finds its driving surface gone has no way to know what they are missing.

## Watch

`Archie-40fe` already fixed V80 (canvas chrome rendering over the spine) via the `--strip-h` /
`--finder-h` reservation. RE-MEASURE rather than re-fixing it.

## Verify

`apps/viewer/e2e`, offline. Collapse the spine on one exhibit, open another, assert its spine is
present. Then assert the collapsed state still offers a named control that restores it.

title: The finder says what it found, not where it is
description:
## Question

Fix **V106** — the finder's results don't show where a hit lives. Orphaned by an audit
reconciliation on 2026-07-26: no ticket has ever owned it.

## Why it was missed, and this is the instructive part

`Archie-3ea1` (the cite panel) and `Archie-99b1` (the address writes every rung) both record V106's
capability as now "available" / "unblocked" — and both are telling the truth about the *substrate*.
The address grammar exists, `routeToHash` builds every rung, and `logicalIdOf` resolves a note id
from either form.

Neither ticket touched `SearchOverlay.svelte`. **A capability being reachable is not the same as a
surface using it**, and both closures read as if it were. That is the same epistemic shape as
`.claude/rules/svelte-no-typecheck-net.md`'s "a gate proves the code COMPILED, never that the output
CARRIES anything" — here, the plumbing landed and nothing consumed it.

## The work

A finder result should say where it is, in the same noun-and-position idiom the rest of the viewer
now uses. At minimum a hit should name its object (and its section, in a narrative); ideally the
result carries the locus so activating it lands on the exact rung rather than the object's top.

Read `ExhibitView.svelte`'s `locus` derivation first — it is the ONE address writer and already
computes precedence across noteId / objectId / sectionId / xywh / t. The finder should read from
that vocabulary, not re-derive an address of its own. Do not add a second address writer.

## Verify

`apps/viewer/e2e`, offline. Open the finder, assert a result displays its locus, and assert that
activating it lands on that locus rather than the object's default view. Inject the bug (strip the
locus from the result) and confirm the test fails before trusting it.

---

## Prior art swept 2026-07-26 — clover-iiif is a fully worked donor

`IIIF/clover-iiif/src/components/.../ContentSearch.tsx` and `Annotation/Item.tsx`:

- **Canvas name is a GROUP header, not a per-row field.** `ContentSearch.tsx:50-58` groups hits by
  `target.source.id`; `:83-88` renders each group under `<header><Label label={canvas.label}/></header>`.
  Avoids repeating the same canvas name down every row.
- **The thumbnail IS the locus.** `Item.tsx:41-52` builds each row's thumbnail from the hit's own
  `FragmentSelector` xywh, requesting a IIIF image crop AT THAT REGION
  (`${targetResource}/${xywh}/!${w},${h}/0/default.jpg`) — not a generic canvas cover. A result shows
  *where* it is by showing what is there.
- **Activation lands on the exact region.** `handleClick` (`Item.tsx:134-155`): if the hit's canvas is
  already visible, `handleOverlayZoom()` (`:101-117`) fits the viewport to the annotation's own overlay
  bounds with padding. If not, it dispatches `updateActiveCanvas` first and a `useEffect` (`:119-132`)
  polls at 1000ms until that annotation's overlay exists, then runs the same zoom — the cross-canvas
  path still ends at the exact region, it just waits for the swap.
- Position count ("3 of 12") is **not** shown per result. clover-iiif has that idiom
  (`Slider/Items/Items.tsx:127`) but does not wire it to search.

**Two other strategy families, for contrast:**

- **universalviewer — hits as a spatial minimap, not a list.** `uv-searchfooterpanel-module/FooterPanel.ts`
  places each hit as a tick on a page-position ruler (`:520-523`, `:713-729`). Hover
  (`onPlacemarkerMouseEnter`, `:594-673`) shows canvas identity (`"Page {label}"` / `"Image {N+1}"`,
  `:617-635`) plus a match count from `result.rects.length` and the ellipsized terms (`:644-667`), and
  publishes `SEARCH_PREVIEW_START` (`:603-606`) — a live preview-pan before any click.
- **quire — the fragment is baked at index time.** `_plugins/search/search.js:100-101` indexes each unit
  with its own `canonicalURL + '#' + id`, so "land on the exact locus" is a plain anchor, not app logic.
- **tropy — filter-in-place.** Search filters the existing item grid; there is no result row to carry a
  locus at all.

Checked and not comparable: immarkus (structured knowledge-graph query builder, not full-text over
image content).

**One gap worth knowing:** clover-iiif appears to render only the Content Search `resources`, not the
Search API 2 `hits` array (match-context objects). If Archie ever consumes a real Content Search
response, that distinction is unresolved in the corpus.

title: Canvas chrome needs a contrast floor against an arbitrary image
description:
## Question

Fix **V42** — the canvas chrome has no contrast floor against the image beneath it. Orphaned by an
audit reconciliation on 2026-07-26.

## Provenance

`Archie-c831` deferred V42 by name into `Archie-9a81`. `Archie-9a81` closed having fixed V40 and V80
without touching V42, and nothing has owned it since. A deferral that names its destination is only
as good as the destination's memory of it — this one was dropped in the handoff.

## The work

Canvas chrome (scale cue, locator, finder pill, nav) sits over an arbitrary image. A photograph can
be any luminance at any point, so chrome that relies on the image being light — or dark — is
unreadable against half the corpus. `screenshots` is the useful adversarial exhibit here: it is full
of near-white UI captures.

Establish a contrast floor that holds regardless of what is beneath. Prior art in the corpus should
be checked before inventing one — how do clover-iiif / canvas-panel / universalviewer keep overlay
chrome legible over unknown imagery (scrim, backdrop-filter, outline, plate)? Cite what you find.

## Watch

`Archie-40fe` established the `--strip-h` / `--finder-h` reservation model for WHERE chrome sits.
This ticket is about LEGIBILITY once it is there — a different axis, same elements. Don't disturb
the reservation while fixing the contrast.

Note also that V80's fix was `Archie-9a81`'s, not `Archie-40fe`'s — several tickets carry that
attribution wrongly. Cite 9a81 for the V80 fix and 40fe for the reservation idiom.

## Verify

Measure, don't eyeball: compute the actual contrast ratio of chrome text/glyphs against the sampled
pixels beneath it, on a light exhibit and a dark one. `screenshots` (light) and a Voynich folio
(dark parchment) are the two poles. State the ratio achieved and the floor targeted.

---

## Prior art swept 2026-07-26 — and it complicates the ticket's premise

**The corpus default is: don't float chrome over the image at all.**

- `IIIF/clover-iiif/src/components/Viewer/Viewer/Viewer.tsx:180-184` — `<ViewerHeader>` and
  `<ViewerContent>` are SIBLINGS in normal flex flow (`Viewer.styled.tsx:15-22`). The header can be
  `background-color: transparent !important` (`Header.styled.ts:57-73`) precisely because it never
  sits over the image. Its one over-canvas control, `PanelToggle`, is an **opaque plate**
  (`background: $primary` + `boxShadow: 2px 2px 5px #0003`) — contrast sidestepped, not solved.
- `tropy/src/components/esper/container.js:11,39` — overlay toolbar is opt-in (`hasOverlayToolbar`
  default `false`); the default lives outside the canvas. Even in overlay mode it is hidden
  (`translate3d(0,-100%,0)`) until hover/focus (`_toolbar.scss:139-158`).
- `canvas-panel` paints no chrome over the image. `cozy-iiif` is headless.

Archie has already committed the other way — `Archie-40fe`'s `--strip-h`/`--finder-h` reservation
model, plus scale cue, finder pill, locator, and (in flight) object nav. That commitment is not
re-opened by this ticket, but **whoever takes this should know it is the minority posture**, and
should say why it stands rather than treating it as given.

## When chrome DOES float, five mechanisms with real values

| technique | donor | values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| opaque plate | clover-iiif `Viewer.styled.tsx:41-82` | solid theme colour + `2px 2px 5px #0003` |
| scrim + backdrop-filter, solid fallback FIRST | universalviewer `center-panel.less:79-83` | `background: @gray-dark` (fallback, commented `// ie8`) → `fadeout(@gray-dark, 30%)` → `blur(5px)` |
| theme-adaptive scrim + heavy blur, transient | tropy `_tropy.scss:429`, `_variables.scss:263` | 80% opacity, swaps light/dark **by UI theme, not by sampling the image**; `blur(20px)` |
| token-routed scrim + hairline border | anvil `Toolbar.svelte:80-93` | `var(--surface-floating)` + `blur(8px)` + `1px solid var(--border-floating)` |
| gradient scrim + doubled text-shadow halo | immarkus `Images.css:22-30` | directional gradient only under the label + `text-shadow: 0 0 2px rgba(0,0,0,.5), 0 0 6px rgba(0,0,0,.35)`, same recipe as `drop-shadow()` for SVG |

Cascade order is UV's guard for non-supporting browsers, not `@supports`. anvil's border substitutes
for contrast when fill and blur fall short. immarkus doubles gradient AND halo rather than trusting
either.

**Nobody samples the underlying pixels.** Tropy adapts to UI theme; no one adapts to the image.

## The measured-ratio ask is ORIGINAL, not a port

All seven repos grepped for `4.5:1`, `3:1`, "contrast ratio", "WCAG" — **zero real hits**. Every
technique above was chosen by eye. The measurement discipline this ticket asks for has no corpus
precedent; keep it, but label it as Archie's own rather than implying a donor.

title: The seed corpus has no polygon region, so the path is never seen
description:
## Question

**V54** — the seed corpus contains zero polygon regions, so the polygon path is never exercised by
anything a reader or a developer actually looks at. Orphaned by an audit reconciliation on
2026-07-26: never named outside the map epic and its own audit ledger.

## Why this is filed low, and honestly

This is a **showroom gap, not a viewer defect**. The polygon selector is implemented; nothing in the
shipped seed data uses it. So every screenshot, every demo, every manual drive and every e2e run
exercises rectangles only — and a polygon regression would surface in front of a user rather than in
front of us.

It is scoped as content work, which is why it sat unowned: it does not look like a bug in any file.

## The work

Add at least one polygon region to the seed corpus, on an object where a polygon is the *right*
shape rather than a demonstration of the feature (an irregular illustration, a marginal figure —
the Voynich rosettes are the obvious candidate).

Two seed sources exist and they are not the same thing — check which one this belongs in before
editing: studio `seed-data` versus viewer `sample-data` → `gen-published.mts`. Shared content lives
in `apps/viewer/fixtures`.

Then assert it: a polygon region should appear in the offline e2e suite, so the path has a gate and
not just a presence.

## Watch

Do NOT change an existing fixture to make it a polygon — the project rule is that a shared fixture
is never modified to serve one need; add a new one. Changing one requires checking every consumer.

title: Studio and Viewer token files have already drifted — unify onto one floor
description:
## Question

Studio and Viewer each carry their own `tokens.css`, and the two have **already drifted**. Unify
them onto one source, or record why they must stay separate.

## The measurement (2026-07-26, found while landing the embed's shared token layer)

- `apps/studio/src/tokens.css` has `--text-lede` and `--text-note`; the viewer's copy does not.
- `apps/viewer/src/tokens.css` has `--topbar-h`, `--scrim-top`, `--pane-top`; studio's copy does not.

Neither divergence was decided. They accumulated, which is the entire failure mode `Archie-52a9`
named when it rejected copied `markers.css` / `tokens.css` / `atmosphere.css` for the embed:
duplicated token files are *precisely* what produced the visual drift the viewer UX audit measured
(white + system-ui + orange + square cards against the shell's green atmosphere, display face and
reading colours).

The embed work (`Archie-c314`) moved the **viewer's** copy down into a shared package so the embed
and the shell consume one floor. **Studio was deliberately left out of that change** — it is a
bigger fish than the embed ticket, and folding it in would have made a scoped slice unreviewable.
This ticket is that fish.

## The work

1. Diff the two files properly. Separate genuine divergence (a token only one app can meaningfully
   have) from accidental divergence (a token both want, added to one).
2. For accidental divergence: promote to the shared token package the embed work created.
3. For genuine divergence: keep it app-local, and say in a comment WHY it is app-local. An
   unexplained app-local token is how this recurs.
4. Decide whether studio consumes the shared floor plus a local layer, or stays wholly separate.
   Consuming plus layering is the obvious default; argue it down if it doesn't hold.

## Watch

- The shared floor now has THREE consumers once studio joins: `apps/viewer`, `packages/archie-viewer`
  (the embed), and `apps/studio`. A token added to the floor lands in the published embed bundle —
  check the `eagerGzKB` ratchet (`cd packages/archie-viewer && node build.mjs --check`) after, since
  the embed inlines the token text into its entry.
- Studio is an authoring surface and the viewer is a reading surface. Some divergence is legitimate
  — authoring chrome has no reason to exist in a reader. Don't unify for symmetry's sake.
- `recipes/smoke.mjs` now asserts the embed's computed token values AGREE with the shared source
  (not merely that tokens exist). If you change the floor, that assertion is the thing that tells
  you whether the embed followed.

## Verify

`pnpm --filter @archie/studio run check` and `pnpm --filter @archie/viewer run check:svelte` both at
0/0, `pnpm -r run typecheck`, and a driven look at both apps — a token move that typechecks and
silently changes a colour is the failure this ticket exists to prevent. Screenshot both surfaces
before and after and compare.

title: The seed has no local audio/video, so the AV surface has no offline gate
description:
## Question

The seed corpus has **no locally-sourced audio or video object**, so the entire AV reading surface is
untestable offline — and V49 in particular has no gate.

## The measurement (2026-07-26, found while moving canvas assertions into the offline suite)

`screenshots` is now proven fully offline-capable: 21 image responses all from localhost, **0**
aborted remote requests, **0** responses ≥ 400, and OSD paints (860×720, 660 distinct sampled
colours). That unlocked the halo, canvas-keyboard, Escape-ladder and V48 assertions, which previously
had to be driven by a human online.

**V49 could not follow, and the reason is structural:** all 21 published `screenshots` bodies are
`type: "Image"`. The seed's one sounded folio is **archive.org-hosted**, so offline it never loads.
The AV temporal map (`.timeline`) renders only under `cues.length > 0 && !mediaError && dur > 0`, and
`dur` comes from media metadata — which never arrives with the network cut. Driven ONLINE it still
did not render within 60s headless (recorded on `Archie-7b86`).

So V49's fix is merged and **unverified end-to-end**, and will stay that way until a local media
asset exists.

## The work

Add a small locally-sourced audio or video object to a seed exhibit, published into the tree like the
`screenshots` images are.

- Keep it **small** — this lands in the repo and in every published tree. Seconds, not minutes; a
  few hundred KB. It exists to make `dur > 0` and a cue band real, not to be listened to.
- It needs at least two cues so the active-cue logic (`activeNoteIndex`, and the `started`
  precondition added for V51) has something to discriminate.
- Check which seed source this belongs in before editing — studio `seed-data` vs viewer `sample-data`
  → `gen-published.mts` are two different things, and shared content lives in `apps/viewer/fixtures`.
- Do NOT repurpose an existing fixture to serve this. Project rule: a shared fixture is never
  modified to serve one need; add a new one, and changing one requires checking every consumer.

Then close the gate: assert V49 (the temporal map is not covered by the item strip) in the offline
e2e suite, and prove it red-green by injecting the occlusion.

## Why this is worth doing rather than deferring

Two independent things are blocked on it, and both are currently trusted rather than verified:

1. **V49's own fix.** It uses `padding-bottom: var(--strip-h, 0px)` + `box-sizing: border-box` — the
   same reservation `Archie-40fe` established. The `box-sizing` is load-bearing: without it the
   padding ADDS to the 100vh, the column overflows, and the timeline is pushed off the bottom
   instead of covered — *a different defect wearing the fix's clothes*. Nothing currently catches
   that regression.
2. **`Archie-7b86`'s V53 work** (the six affordances the AV reader drops) will land with no offline
   gate at all unless this exists.

## Verify

The new object loads with the network cut, `dur > 0`, the cue band renders, and the timeline is
fully visible above the item strip. Inject the `box-sizing` removal and confirm the assertion fails.

title: The embed's four DEFER-tracked capabilities: note media, reading sheet, cite hovercards, search
description:
## Question

`docs/adr/0019`'s capability contract carries four **DEFER-tracked** rows. This is the ticket that
makes "tracked" true.

## Why this ticket must exist

`Archie-f90d`'s whole argument is that **a capability with no file cannot go missing quietly**. It
borrows annomea's verdict vocabulary, in which `DEFER-tracked` means *deliberately not done yet, and
someone is holding the string*. A `DEFER-tracked` row with no ticket behind it is just `ABSENT`
wearing a better word — which is precisely the state the contract declares no row may occupy.

So: four rows, one ticket, named below. If any is done or dropped, update the ADR row at the same
time — the row and this ticket are two ends of the same string.

## The four

1. **Note media.** The shell renders a note's media tiles (`NoteMedia`, `NoteLightbox`). The embed
   drops them, so an annotation with images shows none. Check `Archie-ff79`'s work first — the
   author's media *description* is carried through the model now, and the embed should not
   re-drop it.

2. **Reading sheet.** No expand-to-read in the embed, so a long note truncates with no way to see
   the rest. Note the shell's sheet was just reshaped by `Archie-dbbc` — it is now `NotePopup` at a
   larger size, sharing one content renderer, with the card hidden (not unmounted) while the sheet is
   open for focus-restore reasons. **Port the shape, not the Svelte** — the embed is framework-free
   by design (`Archie-52a9` rejected a shared component layer explicitly; do not reopen it).

3. **Prose cite hovercards.** The shell gives a cite link scent and a hovercard; the embed renders
   the text. Relates to `Archie-3ea1`'s cite ladder — check what the embed can resolve before
   designing, since a hovercard that cannot resolve its target is worse than a plain link.

4. **Full-text search.** The shell has the finder; the embed has no way to search an exhibit.
   Note `Archie-9eeb` (the finder shows results without saying where they are) is open against the
   shell's finder — do not port the defect. `minisearch` is the shell's engine and is subject to
   `.claude/rules/viewer-optimizedeps-bare-includes.md` on the viewer side; the embed's constraints
   are different (esbuild, no Vite optimizeDeps) but the weight question is sharper.

## The constraint that governs all four

**Everything rides behind the existing `await import("./reader.js")` boundary.** The gate is
`cd packages/archie-viewer && node build.mjs --check`, which ratchets `eagerGzKB` — the gz total of
the entry's transitive `import-statement` closure. `entryGzKB` and `totalGzKB` **cannot** catch a
leak here; see `.claude/rules/archie-viewer-eager-closure.md`, which records the time this shipped
silently at 257.9KB instead of 32.7KB.

Any eager movement is the bug, not the cost of the feature. Full-text search is the one most likely
to argue otherwise — if it genuinely cannot be lazy, that is an escalation, not a budget raise.

## Verify

Each capability gets a `recipes/smoke.mjs` assertion against the BUILT bundle, proven red-green by
deleting the capability and watching smoke fail — the discipline `f90d` established. Run
`node scripts/sync-dist.mjs` after every rebuild: `recipes/try.html` loads the **root** `/dist/`
copy, and skipping the sync makes smoke report on the previous bundle.

title: V23 re-measured: two object-stepping affordances remain, named
description:
## Question

**V23 re-measured, 2026-07-26.** `Archie-01a6` required this: *"V23 says the four nav affordances agree
about WHERE you are and disagree about WHAT you are looking at. This ticket changes one of the four.
RE-MEASURE V23 after, do not fix it blind."*

This ticket carries the measurement and the precise remainder. It is deliberately **not** a fix.

## What was measured

A driven browser pass over `#/sampler` (3 objects: video, audio, image) and `#/voynich` (12 images),
in a pristine detached checkout at `d004ca8`, `git status --porcelain` empty before the build and
after the drive.

Nav landmarks, identical on **every** reader surface — AV and image alike:

```
["Breadcrumb", "Media in this exhibit", "Objects in this exhibit"]
```

| object | `.player` | sidebar stepper | canvas nav |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ex-sampler.sv1` (video) | 1 | 1 — "Object 1 of 3" | 0 |
| `ex-sampler.sa1` (audio) | 1 | 1 — "Object 2 of 3" | 0 |
| `ex-sampler.si1` (image) | 0 | 0 | 1 — "Object 3 of 3" |
| `voynich o1` (image) | 0 | 0 | 1 — "Object 1 of 12" |

Exactly **one** object stepper per surface, and the right one on each: sidebar footer on AV (no canvas
chrome to hold it), canvas chrome on image surfaces. Visible and announced channels agree throughout.

## The remainder, stated precisely

**Two object-stepping affordances are co-present on every reader surface**, and the pairing is
universal rather than AV-specific:

1. **"Media in this exhibit"** — the top-bar carousel/filmstrip. Predates this work.
2. **"Objects in this exhibit"** — the object stepper, sourced from whichever surface owns it.

`Archie-01a6` reduced the count from **three** to **two**. Before it, a reader could have the carousel,
the sidebar stepper, *and* `NotePopup`'s `np-stepper` (when the aside was collapsed) in view at once.
That third one is now deleted.

The duplication was **known and deliberate** — the original `SidebarObjectNav` header, i.e. the code
`01a6` replaced, says so outright:

> Sidebar bottom object-nav (R4): a VISIBLE, labelled stepper pinned to the foot of a reader sidebar
> for multi-object exhibits. The top-bar carousel is the glance-and-step affordance over the canvas;
> **this is its discoverable, full-width twin** in the reading pane

## The judgement, and why this stays open

The remaining two are probably **not** a defect. A filmstrip is *glance-and-jump* — random access to a
named thumbnail. A stepper is *prev/next relative motion*. Different affordances serving different
tasks, and the carousel long predates this work.

But that is a judgement, not a measurement, and `01a6` asked for the measurement precisely so V23
would not be assumed closed. So V23's remaining statement is: **two object-stepping affordances,
named above, co-present on every reader surface, differing in access model.** Whoever takes this
decides whether that pairing is correct, or whether one should yield — with the numbers above rather
than a fresh audit.

## Watch

- The original header's "twin" framing is an argument FOR the pairing, not an oversight to correct.
  Read it before proposing a removal.
- `Archie-01a6`'s own fix put the stepper in the canvas chrome. Prior art is against floating chrome
  over arbitrary imagery at all (see `Archie-de08`) — clover-iiif and tropy both default to chrome
  outside the canvas. If this ticket concludes one affordance should yield, that finding is relevant
  to which.

title: The collapsed rail is inert — but the a11y-tree half of that claim is unverified
description:
## Question

The collapsed reader rail is `inert`, and a comment claims that removes it from the accessibility
tree. The tab-order half is confirmed; **the a11y-tree half did not reproduce.** Establish which is
true and make the comment match.

## The measurement (2026-07-26, found during review of `Archie-dbbc`/`01a6`)

`Reader.svelte` (base `85c8ba5:403`, byte-identical at `d004ca8` — this is **pre-existing**, not
introduced by the note-surface work) carries:

> must leave the a11y tree + tab order too — `inert` stops its note list

Driven against the built bundle, rail collapsed, `inert` set:

| half of the claim | result |
| --- | --- |
| **tab order** | **CONFIRMED** — `btn.focus()` does not move `document.activeElement`; `elementFromPoint` at its centre returns nothing |
| **a11y tree** | **DID NOT REPRODUCE** — `getByRole` still returns **1** for the note entry, and its text is still present in the ARIA snapshot |

The reviewer explicitly declined to call this a defect, and that caution is right: no real screen
reader was tested, and this may be Playwright's accessibility computation not modelling `inert`
rather than Chromium failing to expose it. **Do not assume the comment is wrong — assume it is
unverified.**

## Why it matters enough to check

The rail collapses to `width: 0; overflow: hidden`. Children therefore keep layout boxes and report
`isVisible() === true`, so `inert` is the *only* thing doing the hiding. If `inert` genuinely does
not remove the subtree from the a11y tree, a screen-reader user hears the entire note list of a
panel the sighted reader has collapsed — with no visual counterpart and no way to reach it by tab.

There is a useful contrast right beside it. The note card's hiding technique from `Archie-dbbc`
(`display: none` on a `display: contents` wrapper) measured **role-count 0 and an empty ARIA
subtree** on the same page in the same run. So the two hiding mechanisms in these components are
**not** equivalent on the a11y axis, and the weaker one is the one whose comment claims more.

## The work

1. Determine whether Chromium actually removes an `inert` subtree from the a11y tree — test with a
   real screen reader or Chromium's own accessibility inspector, not Playwright's `getByRole`, which
   is the instrument under suspicion.
2. If `inert` does the job: **correct the test instrument**, and add a note that `getByRole` is not a
   reliable probe for `inert` so the next person doesn't re-open this.
3. If it does not: hide the collapsed rail by a mechanism that measurably works. `display: none` is
   proven on this page — but check it against the width-transition and any measurement the collapse
   animation depends on before swapping.
4. Either way, make the comment state exactly what is verified.

## Watch

Do not "fix" this by weakening the comment to match the tooling. The comment names a real user
guarantee; the question is whether the code delivers it, not whether the sentence is convenient.

title: Flip-and-read was removed with the note-card stepper — decide whether it returns
description:
## Question

`stepIntoReading` was removed by `Archie-01a6`. Stepping between objects no longer carries the open
note forward — "flip-and-read" is gone. **Neither `dbbc` nor `01a6` asked for that.** This ticket
records the decision so it is a choice rather than a side effect, and names what to do to reverse it.

## Why it was removed, and the reasoning is structural rather than aesthetic

`stepIntoReading` existed **because the stepper lived inside the note card**. Stepping had to keep a
note selected or the card would unmount — pulling the button out from under the reader's cursor
mid-gesture. So the carry was never a reading feature; it was the machinery that kept the control
mounted while it was being used.

`Archie-01a6` moved object nav into the canvas chrome, where it does not move or unmount when a note
closes. Nothing needs keeping alive any more, and the justification evaporated with the structure it
served.

Preserving the carry now would cost something the old design never paid: a `selected !== null` gate.
The canvas nav is usable with **no note open**, so an unconditional carry would ambush a reader who
has never opened one. That gate makes a *persistent* control behave differently based on invisible
prior state. Inside the note card the conditionality was free — the control only existed while a note
was open.

Supporting: `MEMORY.md` records the behaviour as *"stepper only when collapsed, flip-and-read"* —
**both halves of that entry are what `01a6` deletes**, and `Archie-c982` says the stepper "only
migrated there because collapsing the aside took the real object nav away."

## Why this is a ticket rather than a closed decision

Flip-and-read is a **reading** behaviour, and the argument above is a **structural** one. It explains
why the old implementation's reason is gone; it does not establish that a reader working through a
sequence of annotated objects doesn't want the note to follow them. Those are different claims, and
only the first has been made.

Someone who actually reads a multi-object exhibit end to end should decide. The likely shapes:

- **Leave it removed.** Stepping is navigation; opening a note is a separate act.
- **Restore it, gated.** Carry the open note only when one is already open — accepting the
  invisible-prior-state cost, which is real but small.
- **Restore it as an explicit affordance.** A "keep notes open while stepping" toggle, which makes
  the state visible instead of inferred.

## How to reverse it

`object-nav.spec.ts` asserts the current behaviour explicitly — *"stepping objects does NOT carry the
open note forward"* — with a comment naming it as the test to invert if the project restores the
carry. So the reversal is: invert that test, then make it pass. The behaviour is pinned in exactly
one place on purpose.

## Watch

Do not restore the carry by reinstating `stepIntoReading` as it was. It was shaped around a control
that no longer exists there, and its unconditional form would now fire with no note open.

title: V48: the chrome reservation is horizontal-only and cannot clear a full-height region
description:
## Question

**V48's chrome-clearance reservation is horizontal-only, so it cannot clear a region that fills the
canvas height.** Discovered 2026-07-26 while migrating the canvas assertions offline; measured, with
the mechanism traced to source.

## The measurement

All 67 halo-drawing notes on `screenshots` swept against the unmodified production build. **Two
offend**, both against `.note-pop` (the bottom-left note card), both roughly 1:4 aspect fitted to
626px of a 720px canvas:

| idx | ulid | halo box | note card |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | `01KVPQ3WXQ4PJ0614J4BEAC2XN` | `[484,47 134x626]` | `[20,546 506x140]` |
| 46 | `01KVPV0NCEFYM5Z8R3MR7DVKB2` | `[499,47 170x626]` | — |

The top-left **legend is cleared correctly**. The bottom-left note card is not.

## The mechanism, from source

`fitBoundsRect` returns `{ x: box.x - w * l, y: box.y, w, h: box.h }` — it widens the target box and
slides it **horizontally**, and never touches `y` or `h`.

For a **height-constrained** fit, widening the box changes no zoom (height is what binds), so the
horizontal slide is the only effect. Nothing in the current reservation can lift such a region clear
of a control anchored to the bottom.

So this is not a tuning problem and not a test artifact. The reservation model `Archie-40fe`
established works for the width-constrained case and is structurally unable to serve the
height-constrained one.

## What the test currently does, and why it is not the fix

`occlusion.spec.ts` now sweeps **every** halo note — there is no sweep width left to tune, which was
how this was found (the original test checked one note; widening to ten, then to all, exposed it).
The assertion states what actually holds: cleared for every region **except** one filling the canvas
height. Two properties are deliberate:

- An offender that is **not** height-constrained fails **as a regression**, with a message saying so
  explicitly rather than being absorbed into the known gap.
- The count is **ratcheted at today's two**. A fix that drops it to zero still passes — a fix must
  not be punished by its own regression test.

So the gap is pinned and bounded, not hidden. Closing it is this ticket.

## The work

Extend the reservation to the vertical axis, or change what `fitBoundsRect` is allowed to do for a
height-constrained fit. Options worth weighing rather than assuming:

- Reserve vertically too — but note the canvas is already height-bound in this case, so a vertical
  inset necessarily **zooms out**, which changes what the reader sees. That may be right; it is a
  visible trade, not a free one.
- Move the note card for tall regions specifically (right-anchor, or top-anchor) — cheaper, but it
  makes chrome position depend on content geometry, which is its own kind of surprise.
- Accept the overlap for full-height regions and make the card dismissable/translucent in that case.

Whichever, **check `Archie-de08` first** — the corpus consensus is against floating chrome over
arbitrary imagery at all, and clover-iiif/tropy both default to chrome *outside* the canvas. If that
argument wins, this gap disappears rather than being solved.

## Verify

Drop the ratcheted count in `occlusion.spec.ts` to zero and watch the sweep pass. Do **not** relax the
"a non-height-constrained offender is a regression" branch — that is the part protecting the case that
already works.

title: The sheet's media-route modal guard is correct but unfalsifiable — no fixture reaches it
description:
## Question

The `onmedia` half of the "a modal replaces the sheet, never stacks on it" guard is **correct,
unfalsifiable, and on a route no fixture can currently reach.** Give it a fixture that makes the
existing assertion do real work.

## What was measured (2026-07-26, verifying `cd9b33f`)

`Archie-dbbc` fixed a real defect: expanding a note and then clicking a tag chip put **two
`aria-modal="true"` dialogs on screen at once** (sheet + finder). The fix clears `readingSheet` on
both routes out of the sheet — `onopenfinder` (tag chips) and `onmedia` (`NoteLightbox`, which is
also modal) — in both readers, so the new surface **replaces** the sheet.

The tag-chip route is genuinely gated: the test waits for both transitions before snapshotting and
guards against vacuity.

**The media route is not.** The test named *"never two aria-modal elements, on any route out of the
sheet"* opens the sheet, presses Escape, and asserts `[]` — it **never clicks a media tile**, despite
a comment saying the media tile is the second route.

Proven rather than inferred: reverting `readingSheet = false` from the `onmedia` handler in **both**
readers leaves `note-surface.spec.ts` + `note.spec.ts` at **18/18 passing**.

## Why it isn't a live defect

Driving the built, injected bundle across every reading and every note found **no note in the fixture
that is both expandable and media-bearing** — a note needs `text` to show the ⤢ at all. So the
stacking route is presently **unreachable**, which is exactly why reverting the guard breaks nothing.

The guard is right and should stay. What's wrong is a test name that implies coverage the body
doesn't provide.

## Why this is worth closing rather than noting

"The sheet gaining media" was **this branch's own fix** — the old sheet took only `text`, so media
and tags vanished on expand. The moment a fixture gains a note carrying both text and media, the
stacking behaviour returns, silently, past a test whose name says it is covered.

## The work

1. **Add a fixture note with both `text` and media** to a driven exhibit. That alone makes the
   existing assertion exercise the route it names, with no test change.
2. Then prove it: revert `readingSheet = false` from `onmedia` and confirm the test now **fails**.
   Restore.
3. If (1) is not wanted for some reason, the honest minimum is amending the test's comment and name
   to say the media route is **knowingly uncovered** — the way `S1`'s `readingSheet` flag fix is
   recorded as uncovered rather than implied covered.

Do NOT close this by deleting the guard. It is correct; it is the fixture that is thin.

## The principle this sits under, worth keeping

From the same review, covering ⤢, tags and media under one rule instead of three judgements:

> A card affordance is withheld at sheet size **only when it is meaningless there** (the ⤢ offers to
> expand what is already expanded). Everything meaningful at any size is **kept**, and anything modal
> it opens **replaces** the sheet rather than stacking on it.

## Watch

`.claude/rules/playwright-count-does-not-wait.md` and the fixture rule both apply: never modify a
shared fixture to serve one test — add a new one, and changing an existing one means checking every
consumer.

title: The AV surface has no reading legend, and no fixture note to legend
description:
## Question

The AV reading surface has no `ReadingLegend`. `Archie-7b86`'s V53 pass enumerated it as a real drop
against the image reader and deliberately did **not** build it. This ticket carries that measurement
so the gap is a recorded decision rather than an omission.

## Why it was not built, and the reason is the interesting part

Two independent blockers, and the second is the one that matters:

1. **It needs props from off-limits territory.** `readings`, `activeReading`, `onreading`, `styleOf`
   and `readingCount` would all have to be threaded from `ExhibitView.svelte`, which a concurrent
   slice owned at the time. That is a scheduling problem and dissolves on its own.

2. **No fixture AV object carries a note with a `reading`.** So a legend built today would list
   nothing, and any assertion over it would be **vacuous in exactly the way this repo has now been
   bitten by four times** — most precisely `Archie-0cc6`, where a correct guard sits on a route no
   fixture can reach, and reverting it leaves 18/18 passing.

Building the legend now would produce a control that renders empty, an assertion that cannot fail,
and a MUST row that reads as covered. That is worse than the honest absence.

## The work

**Fixture first, then the control.** In that order, or this ticket recreates the problem it was
filed to avoid.

1. Add a fixture AV note carrying a `reading` — a **new** note, not a modification of an existing
   one (`.claude/rules/test-fixtures.md`: never modify a shared fixture to serve one test; changing
   one means checking every consumer).
2. Thread the five props from `ExhibitView.svelte` to both `<MediaPlayerLazy.current …>` instances
   (`:570` and `:592`). Note the sibling wire being done at the same seam for `onopenfinder` — do
   both in one pass if they land together.
3. Build the legend, then **revert step 1 and watch the assertion fail**. If it still passes, the
   assertion is measuring nothing.

## The design constraint the AV surface adds

`hyperaudio-lite`'s `hyperaudio-lite.js:648-664` re-homes the spoken word to `document.title` when
the transcript is hidden — i.e. the position signal must survive the surface that carries it
narrowing. Whatever the legend does to the spine's width, the `.timeline` has to remain a legible
position signal. This is why V53 did **not** port the image reader's collapse-to-position-mark idiom
to AV.

## Watch

`MediaPlayer.svelte` deliberately keeps the sidebar stepper — an AV object has no canvas chrome to
move object nav to — and `ResizeDivider` is mounted with `collapsible={false}` for the same reason
(collapsing the aside would strand the object nav, re-creating V65). A legend that pushes the aside
toward collapse must not defeat either.

## Related

- `Archie-7b86` — the parent; V53's full **eleven**-drop enumeration lives in its resolution — six restored, five
  enumerated-not-built. (This ticket originally said 'ten'; that number was the coordinator's, not the measurement's, and the implementer corrected it.)
- `Archie-0cc6` — the canonical instance of the unfalsifiable-guard failure this ticket is shaped to
  avoid.
- The sibling `onopenfinder` wire at the same `ExhibitView` seam, with the same fixture problem (no
  fixture AV note carries a tag).
